title: GM Stock Value Stable During Week Of December 28 – December 31, 2020
summary: GM stock remained stable between December 28th and December 31st, 2020, closing at $41.64 per share with a minimal decrease of 0.14 percent. This stability follows earlier share losses and was influenced by factors like an increased price target from JP Morgan, executive stock sales, and developments in GM's electric vehicle strategy and legal challenges. The article provides a comprehensive overview of factors impacting GM's stock performance leading up to this period, including EV investments, sales figures, and pandemic-related challenges and recoveries.

title: Li Auto Crushes Delivery Guidance. The Chinese EV Sector Remains Hot.
summary: Li Auto (LI) crushed its delivery guidance for 2020, delivering 14,464 vehicles in the fourth quarter and 32,624 for the full year. This strong performance, along with that of peers like Nio and Tesla, indicates that the Chinese electric vehicle sector remains robust entering 2021.

title: Nio (NIO) ends 2020 on a high note with triple-digit growth in deliveries
summary: Nio Inc. (NIO) reported strong triple-digit growth in vehicle deliveries for December, Q4, and the full year of 2020, exceeding its guidance and marking a robust end to the year. The company delivered 7,007 vehicles in December, 17,353 in Q4, and 43,728 for the full year, all showing significant year-over-year increases. Nio's shares rose 6% on Monday, having surged over 1,200% in the past year, as it continues to compete with Tesla.

title: Chinese electric car company Nio doubles deliveries in 2020 as local competition ramps up for Tesla
summary: Chinese electric vehicle startups Nio, Li Auto, and Xpeng significantly increased their deliveries in 2020, with Nio doubling its deliveries to 43,728 vehicles. Despite this growth, their combined sales are still a fraction of Tesla's global deliveries, which neared 500,000 in 2020. The Chinese government's support, including subsidies and infrastructure development, has fueled the surge in EV demand in the country, intensifying competition for Tesla in the world's largest auto market.

title: Low Inflation? Asset Prices at Record Highs Suggests Otherwise
summary: Frank Holmes argues that official low inflation figures do not reflect the reality of soaring asset and commodity prices. He highlights significant increases in gold, Bitcoin, food, lumber, and copper prices, attributing these rises to massive government stimulus and easy monetary policy. Holmes suggests that investors should be critical of media biases and consider holding hard assets as stores of value given concerns about currency debasement.

title: Up 120% in 2020, Can the LIT Lithium ETF Hold Its Charge in 2021?
summary: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) surged over 120% in 2020, driven by the growth in electric vehicle demand. With Tesla as a top holding and its supplier CATL expanding production, the article explores whether LIT can maintain its momentum in 2021. Technical indicators show the fund is overbought, but a MACD filter suggests a potential buying opportunity.

title: Up 120% in 2020, Can the LIT Lithium ETF Hold Its Charge in 2021?
summary: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) soared over 120% in 2020, driven by the booming electric vehicle market and the expansion plans of Tesla supplier Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd (CATL). As demand for green energy vehicles increases, the article questions if LIT can maintain its strong performance in 2021, noting some technical indicators like RSI are in overbought territory while MACD suggests a buying opportunity.

title: Rock star chip designer Jim Keller joins Tenstorrent
summary: Legendary computer chip designer Jim Keller has joined Toronto startup Tenstorrent Inc. as its new president and chief technology officer. Keller, known for his work at AMD, Apple, and Tesla, will guide Tenstorrent in its mission to create a machine learning training chip that utilizes software to optimize computing power and increase efficiency, challenging established players like Intel, AMD, and Nvidia.

title: Elon Musk overtakes Bezos to become world’s richest person
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, has surpassed Amazon's Jeff Bezos to become the world's richest person. His net worth reached $188.5 billion after a 4.8% rally in Tesla's shares on Thursday, just over $1.5 billion more than Bezos. This milestone caps a remarkable year for Musk, whose net worth soared by over $150 billion, largely due to Tesla's impressive 743% stock surge in the past year.

title: Stock Option Volume ‘Exploded’ in 2020. What Comes Next.
summary: In 2020, stock option volume saw a significant surge, largely driven by individual investors entering the market. These investors showed a strong preference for popular stocks such as Apple, Tesla, and NIO, a Chinese electric vehicle company. The article discusses this explosive growth in option trading and anticipates future trends.

title: More Cells, More Range: TI’s Wireless Battery Management System Frees EV Space for More Design Innovation
summary: Texas Instruments has introduced a new wireless battery management system (BMS) that aims to address the limitations of wired BMS in electric vehicles (EVs). This solution, featuring the CC266C2R-Q1 wireless MCU and BQ79616-Q1 battery monitor, reduces cabling, weight, and space while improving reliability and enabling more design innovation and battery cells for extended EV range. It achieves high accuracy and network availability, and is the first wireless BMS to receive ASIL-D compliance, making it a significant advancement for the EV industry.

title: Albemarle to double capacity at Silver Peak lithium brine operation
summary: Albemarle Corp announced plans to invest $30-$50 million to double the production capacity at its Silver Peak, Nevada lithium facility by 2025, utilizing its brine water rights. The company will also explore clay resources and new technologies for lithium production in Nevada, aiming to meet the growing domestic demand for lithium from the electric vehicle market. This expansion reinforces Albemarle's commitment to optimizing its US lithium resources for greater security and sustainability of the North American supply chain.

title: Tesla market value crosses $800 billion for the first time
summary: Tesla's market capitalization surpassed $800 billion for the first time, driven by a 5.6% jump in its shares. This surge also propelled CEO Elon Musk past Jeff Bezos to become the world's wealthiest individual. The electric automaker's valuation now dwarfs the combined market caps of traditional Detroit automakers, despite its production being a fraction of larger rivals.

title: General Motors Unveils New Logo
summary: General Motors has introduced a new corporate logo featuring lowercase script and an underlined "m" within a rounded square border. This refreshed branding is designed to reflect the company's intensified focus on electric vehicles (EVs) and its vision for a future with zero crashes, zero emissions, and zero congestion. The new logo will be rolled out across all corporate communications and coincides with a new marketing campaign called "Everybody In," promoting GM's upcoming range of electric vehicles across its brands.

title: Tesla market value crosses $800 billion for the first time
summary: Tesla Inc.'s market capitalization surpassed $800 billion for the first time, driven by a significant jump in its stock price on Friday. This surge has also propelled CEO Elon Musk to become the world's richest man, surpassing Amazon's Jeff Bezos. The company's valuation now places it among Wall Street's most valuable firms, despite its production volume being a fraction of larger automotive rivals.

title: These Hot Stocks Made This American Century's Best 2020 U.S. Diversified Stock Fund
summary: The American Century Focused Dynamic Growth Fund (ACFSX) was the top-performing U.S. diversified stock fund in 2020, up 73.63% compared to the S&P 500's 18.40%. The fund achieved this success by investing in high-growth companies like Amazon, Facebook, Alphabet, Tesla, Square, DocuSign, Nike, Chipotle Mexican Grill, and Chegg, focusing on those with high sustainable growth rates and strong fundamentals, consistent with CAN SLIM principles. Its strong performance has earned it repeated IBD Best Mutual Funds Awards.

title: TI Unveils Wireless Battery Management System
summary: Texas Instruments (TI) has introduced a wireless battery management system (BMS) for electric vehicles, aimed at simplifying electrical architectures, reducing weight by eliminating bulky cabling, and improving reliability. The system boasts high network availability and accuracy, with the potential to significantly reduce manufacturing costs and car weight. Industry experts like Asif Anwar from Strategy Analytics believe that wireless BMS will be a growing trend in the EV market due to its flexibility, lower complexity, and cost-effectiveness.

title: Here Are All 43 GM Brands, Listed In One Place
summary: This article lists and describes 43 automotive brands that have been part of General Motors since its founding in 1908. It covers well-known current brands like Chevrolet, Buick, Cadillac, and GMC, alongside historical and international brands such as Acadian, Oldsmobile, Saturn, and Opel. The article highlights the diverse portfolio GM has managed over its history, including several that were short-lived, market-specific, or now discontinued.

title: Which Automaker Has the Best MPG Cars?
summary: The EPA's annual Automotive Trends Report for 2020 analyzed which manufacturers produce the most fuel-efficient vehicles based on fleetwide fuel economy ratings for the 2019 model year and projections for 2020. Tesla significantly leads both years due to its all-electric lineup, while traditional automakers with truck and SUV-heavy lineups, such as the Detroit Three, rank at the bottom. The report highlights trends in fuel economy and how vehicle electrification is expected to increase these figures in the future.

title: General Motors revamps logo to reflect drive towards "all-electric future"
summary: General Motors has updated its logo for the first time in over 50 years to align with its new focus on electric vehicles. The redesigned logo features a lowercased "gm" with a subtle electric plug shape in the 'm' and a bright blue gradient, symbolizing a zero-emissions future. This change supports GM's commitment to releasing 30 new EVs by 2025 and an "Everybody In" advertising campaign to promote mass EV adoption.

title: Carmaker Nio is 'well positioned' to capture a lot of China's electric vehicle market, analyst says
summary: An analyst believes that Chinese carmaker Nio is well-positioned to secure a significant share of China's electric vehicle market, despite competition from Tesla. Nio recently unveiled its first sedan, the et7, featuring self-driving technology it claims surpasses Tesla's, and is establishing itself as a premium EV brand. While homegrown EV makers saw delivery surges, their numbers still trail Tesla's, the current market leader.

title: World’s top maker of tiny motors has sights on Tesla as EVs gather pace
summary: Nidec Corp., the leading supplier of motors globally, is aiming to become a key component provider for Tesla's electric vehicles. Nidec's president, Jun Seki, expressed a strong desire to collaborate with Elon Musk, stating that Tesla would not meet its 2030 production goals without external partnerships. This move highlights Nidec's confidence in its ability to produce EV components more cheaply and effectively than competitors.

title: ALPS’s Clean Energy ETF Doubled its AUM Last Year While Producing Triple-Digit Returns
summary: ALPS's Clean Energy ETF (ACES) experienced significant growth in 2020, doubling its assets under management to $783 million with $333.75 million in net inflows and delivering a 140% return. The fund's diversified portfolio, focused on wind, solar, and efficiency companies, contributed to its success, even as technical indicators suggest a potential short-term pullback. Despite possible short-term risks, the mid-term outlook for ACES appears promising, with identified support levels and potential for further upside.

title: Spotify Bets Big on Podcasts as a Path to Profitability
summary: Spotify is facing profitability challenges due to its business model, which dedicates over 70% of its revenue to rights holders, preventing it from making a profit since its inception despite high sales. CEO Daniel Ek believes that podcasts, exemplified by investments in major creators like Joe Rogan, offer a crucial path to profitability by diversifying content beyond music and shifting away from reliance on traditional record labels. This strategy aims to give Spotify more control over content costs and attract more users, thereby securing its financial future.

title: General Motors' stock hits all-time high after Consumer Electronics Show
summary: General Motors' stock reached an all-time high of nearly $51 after the company showcased aggressive electric and autonomous vehicle plans at the Consumer Electronics Show. Analysts are cautiously optimistic that GM's focus on EVs, new battery technology (Ultium), and ventures like BrightDrop could lead to sustained stock growth, contrasting with its previous struggles since emerging from bankruptcy. The company aims to invest $27 billion in EVs and AVs, launching 30 new EVs globally by 2025.

title: China Mulls Giving Green Light to Highway Self-Driving Car Tests
summary: China is considering a draft plan to allow self-driving car tests on highways, responding to industry demand to broaden testing scenarios. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's proposal would permit vehicles that have completed extensive road tests without incident to apply for highway testing. This move could also lead to a nationwide regulatory system where test results from one region are recognized across others.

title: 5 reasons General Motors' shares are trading at all-time highs
summary: General Motors' shares reached all-time highs due to investor confidence in its future business plans, particularly in electric vehicles (EVs). CEO Mary Barra outlined ambitious strategies at the CES technology conference, including a $27 billion investment in EV and autonomous vehicle technology, introducing the BrightDrop commercial EV division, and showcasing an electric air taxi concept. The company's Ultium battery system and continued development in autonomous vehicles also contribute to the positive market outlook.

title: Weak lithium prices could slow EV revolution, Albemarle warns
summary: Albemarle, a leading lithium producer, has warned that low lithium prices could impede the expansion of supply needed for electric vehicle (EV) batteries, potentially slowing the EV revolution. The company stated that prices need to increase by at least 10% to make new expansions financially viable, despite a projected demand increase that could outstrip supply significantly by 2025. Albemarle is also exploring new production methods, such as extracting lithium from clay reserves, in anticipation of growing demand.

title: U.S. vehicle safety agency asks Tesla to recall 158,716 older vehicles over touchscreen glitches
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has requested Tesla recall 158,716 Model S and Model X vehicles produced before 2019 due to touchscreen failures. This issue, stemming from a memory device with a limited "write cycle" in the media control unit, can lead to the loss of safety-related features like rearview cameras and defrost systems. Failure rates are projected to increase with vehicle age, with all 2018 models expected to fail within 10 years.

title: Chinese driverless car start-up WeRide raises $310 million in funding as competition heats up
summary: Chinese driverless car start-up WeRide has successfully raised $310 million in a new funding round, led by Yutong Group, as it intensifies its efforts to commercialize its autonomous driving technology. This funding round follows a similar cash injection into rival Pony.ai and highlights the fierce competition within China's driverless car market, which also includes major players like Baidu and Didi. WeRide plans to launch trial operations for "Mini Robobuses" soon and anticipates large-scale robotaxi applications and profitability within the next few years.

title: NHTSA urging Tesla to recall 158,000 cars for touchscreen safety defect
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is pressuring Tesla to recall 158,000 vehicles over concerns about faulty touchscreen displays in certain Model S and Model X cars. These failures can disable crucial safety features like backup cameras and defroster controls. NHTSA has given Tesla until January 27 to respond, threatening a public hearing if the automaker doesn't address the issue.

title: Bus maker leads $310m funding for China self-drive startup WeRide
summary: Chinese autonomous vehicle startup WeRide has secured $310 million in funding, led by bus manufacturer Zhengzhou Yutong Group and other state-backed investors. This investment comes as Beijing initiates new guidelines for self-driving car testing. WeRide is also set to commence testing its autonomous buses in Guangzhou this week.

title: 3 stocks for climate transition
summary: Jaime Ramos Martin, co-portfolio manager for Aviva Investors' Climate Transition Global Equity Fund, discusses three stocks included in the fund: Union Pacific, Trane Technologies, and Volkswagen. These companies are identified as key players in the decarbonization of the economy and adaptation to climate change. Martin explains how each company, ranging from freight rail to efficient HVAC systems and electric vehicles, contributes to climate transition goals.

title: Tesla (TSLA) launches its own solar power inverter
summary: Tesla (TSLA) has launched its own solar power inverter, completing its home solar offering alongside the Powerwall and solar roof tiles. This move leverages Tesla's power electronics expertise to integrate its solar ecosystem further, offering models with 3.8 kW and 7.6 kW power outputs and 97.5% efficiency. The new inverter features Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cellular connectivity with over-the-air updates, and is designed to integrate with the Tesla Powerwall and app.

title: Monterey Bay power plant now a record-breaking battery project to ward off blackouts
summary: The former fossil fuel-burning power plant in Moss Landing, Monterey County, is being converted into a massive battery storage facility by Vistra Corp. This new project, expected to become the world's largest at 300 megawatts, will help California's energy grid by storing excess solar power and releasing it during peak demand, thereby mitigating the risk of blackouts. Alongside Vistra's project, PG&E and Tesla are also developing a substantial battery system at an adjacent substation, further contributing to grid reliability and the state's transition to cleaner energy.

title: Digital Realty moves headquarters to low-tax Texas
summary: Digital Realty, a data center REIT, has moved its corporate headquarters from San Francisco, California, to Austin, Texas, following other tech companies like Oracle and HPE. This move is influenced by Texas's lower corporate tax rate of one percent compared to California's 8.84 percent, as well as the absence of individual income tax and a lower cost of living. CEO A. William Stein and several executives have already relocated, with the company maintaining a significant presence in the Bay Area while expanding its office space and data center footprint in Texas.

title: The bull chasing the bandit: Webull takes on Robinhood
summary: This article discusses how Webull, a Chinese-owned digital brokerage, is gaining traction in the US market as a competitor to Robinhood. Webull differentiates itself with a more professional platform, in-depth data, desktop support, and live customer service, appealing to seasoned investors while Robinhood faces regulatory challenges and criticism for its "gamification" of investing. Despite being Chinese-owned, Webull has largely flown under the regulatory radar due to its proactive government relations and low-key marketing strategy.

title: The ENFR ETF: Energy Perks, Without the Volatility
summary: The Alerian Energy Infrastructure ETF (ENFR) is positioned for a potential comeback in 2021 as the energy sector shows signs of recovery after being the worst-performing group in the S&P 500 last year. ENFR offers investors exposure to midstream energy assets, providing high yields similar to MLPs but with limited tax implications. This ETF allows investors to access the U.S. energy market while avoiding the volatility associated with exploration, production companies, and integrated oil giants.

title: The ENFR ETF: Energy Perks, Without the Volatility
summary: The article highlights the potential for a rebound in the energy sector in 2021, favoring midstream assets like the Alerian Energy Infrastructure ETF (ENFR). ENFR offers a hybrid approach to energy infrastructure investing, combining the high yields of MLPs with reduced tax implications. The ETF is presented as a way for investors to benefit from energy market recovery without the volatility associated with exploration and production or integrated oil giants.

title: Feeling Bullish? Amplify Your Investment with the SPXL ETF
summary: This article discusses the Direxion Daily S&P 500® Bull 3X Shares ETF (SPXL) as a tool for bullish traders to amplify investment in the S&P 500 amidst economic recovery and a lack of short interest in ETFs. It highlights SPXL's 25% jump over three months, reflecting growing investor confidence in a stock market recovery. The article also notes how falling short interest indicates increasing faith in a stock rally and diminishing concerns about market downside in the near future.

title: New Year, Same Story: Tesla and ARKK Still on Fire
summary: The ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) continues its strong performance from the previous year, significantly driven by its substantial investment in Tesla (TSLA). Analyst Dan Ives recently increased his target price for Tesla, citing the company's continuous advancements in electric vehicle technology and its dominant position in the EV market. ARKK, now the largest actively managed ETF by assets, has already seen a nearly 14% gain early in 2021.

title: Tesla launches a standalone solar inverter, challenging Enphase and SolarEdge for market share
summary: Tesla has introduced its first standalone solar inverter, available in 3.8kW and 7.8kW capacities, featuring multiple maximum power point trackers. This move positions Tesla as a direct competitor to Enphase and SolarEdge in the inverter market, allowing the company more control over the cost of its solar systems and offering complete product verticality for solar installations.

title: ARK Investment Plans to Augment Offerings with a Space ETF
summary: ARK Investment, led by Cathie Wood, plans to launch a new actively managed space-focused ETF to invest in domestic and foreign companies engaged in space exploration and innovation. This follows the firm's significant success with its existing disruptive technology ETFs. The article discusses potential holdings like Virgin Galactic and defense contractors, and the broader impact on mainstream investments in the space sector, especially considering a potential indirect exposure to SpaceX IPO.

title: Tesla’s Advanced Battery Research group gets new leadership, Jeff Dahn to become advisor for Novonix
summary: Professor Jeff Dahn, a renowned battery researcher who has had an exclusive partnership with Tesla since 2016 through Dalhousie University, is stepping down from his leadership role at Tesla’s Advanced Battery Research group. He will now serve as Chief Scientific Advisor at Novonix Battery Technology Solutions, a company spun out from his research group. Dahn and his team will continue working with Tesla, which has extended its contract with the Dalhousie University group until 2026, welcoming two new chairs to lead research into advanced Li-ion battery materials and performance.

title: Tesla’s Autopilot Won’t Achieve Full Autonomy, Waymo CEO Says
summary: The CEO of Waymo, John Krafcik, stated in an interview that Tesla's Autopilot will not achieve full autonomy, calling its development approach "misguided." He criticized the idea that a driver assistance system can magically evolve into a fully autonomous one and emphasized that Waymo does not consider Tesla a competitor in the driverless vehicle space, instead viewing their system as a "really good driver assistance system." This comes despite Tesla CEO Elon Musk's past claims about achieving full autonomy.

title: Up 140%, the 'SMOG' ETF Is Literally Cleaning House
summary: The VanEck Vectors Low Carbon Energy ETF (SMOG) has seen significant gains, up 140% in the last 12 months, driven largely by its holdings in electric car companies like Tesla and Nio. The fund invests in companies focused on alternative energy and related enabling technologies. The broader clean energy sector continues to surge, further supported by policy changes under the new Biden administration, which has rejoined the Paris Climate Agreement and pledged investments in renewable energy.

title: BorgWarner to Supply Transfer Cases for Nissan SUV and Pick-up
summary: BorgWarner has secured a contract to supply its part-time transfer cases to Nissan for their Navara pick-up and Paladin SUV models. This is the first time BorgWarner will supply transfer cases to Nissan, strengthening their relationship. The advanced two-speed, shift-on-the-fly system offers quick and accurate shifting between 2WD high, 4WD high, and 4WD low modes, improving vehicle dynamics and performance.

title: CarParts.com Launches First Electric Vehicle & Hybrid Focused Shopping Hub
summary: CarParts.com has launched a new online shopping hub specifically for hybrid and electric vehicle (EV) parts, featuring over 700,000 applications for various popular makes. This initiative aims to address misconceptions about EV and hybrid repairs and provide a comprehensive resource for owners as these vehicles become older and require aftermarket parts. The company emphasizes its commitment to becoming the leading online destination for the EV community, offering parts, information, and tools.

title: Which Chinese EV Stocks Are Worth Betting On
summary: Despite a slow start to the year for oil prices due to COVID-19 concerns, the EV sector continues its strong performance, with Chinese EV companies showing significant gains. This article highlights three Chinese EV manufacturers—XPeng Motors, NIO Limited, and Li Auto—as promising investment opportunities, detailing their market performance, financial health, and innovative strategies.

title: Tesla's report could trigger $7 billion payout to Musk
summary: Tesla's upcoming quarterly report could lead to a $7 billion options payout for CEO Elon Musk if the company's adjusted EBITDA reaches $2.3 billion, triggering the vesting of a fifth tranche from his 2018 pay package. Investors are also keenly awaiting Tesla's 2021 delivery target after the company's stock soared nearly 700% in the past year, making it the fifth-most-valuable publicly traded U.S. company. The company's market capitalization now stands at $843 billion, despite producing a fraction of the vehicles compared to traditional automakers.

title: Baron Partners' Huge Tesla Stake Leads to Downgrade
summary: Baron Partners fund has been downgraded to a Morningstar Analyst Rating of Neutral from Bronze due to its highly concentrated stake in Tesla, which grew to 47% of net assets. Despite lead manager Ron Baron selling some shares and reducing overall fund leverage, the stock's meteoric rise disproportionately influenced the fund's risk profile, highlighting lax risk controls. This concentration, while leading to significant returns in 2020, introduces substantial volatility and risk.

title: Fort Lauderdale Tunnel Could Be ‘Game Changer' for Traffic Issues: Mayor
summary: Fort Lauderdale Mayor Dean Trantalis believes a proposed three-mile tunnel under the New River, built by Elon Musk's The Boring Company, could be a "game changer" for the city's traffic issues and help establish South Florida as a tech hub. The project, estimated at a minimum of $10 million per mile, could also extend commuter lines to suburbs and beaches. The idea gained national attention after discussions between Musk and Miami Mayor Francis Suarez, with Trantalis planning further talks with Boring Company representatives to assess ground topography.

title: SPI Energy’s Phoenix Motorcars Appoints Former Tesla HR Executive as its VP Human Resources
summary: Phoenix Motorcars, a subsidiary of SPI Energy, has appointed Tom Zhang, Ph.D. as its new Vice President of Human Resources. Dr. Zhang brings 14 years of HR experience from companies like Google, Tesla, and Tencent. His appointment is expected to help Phoenix Motorcars scale operations and build a strong team for its long-term vision in the EV market.

title: AI fund that's beating S&P 500 has shifted into tech stocks
summary: A machine-guided fund, the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), has significantly shifted its holdings into technology stocks, now comprising over 37% of its portfolio. This move comes as the fund continues to outperform the S&P 500 Index, having risen 12% this year compared to the S&P 500's nearly 3% gain. The fund has also halved its industrial exposure and doubled its position in Tesla Inc., while significantly reducing its Apple Inc. holdings.

title: STMicroelectronics, Tesla and Apple: what happens when eMobility & 5G collide
summary: This article examines how STMicroelectronics' Q4 2020 results were bolstered by its key relationships with Tesla in e-mobility and Apple in 5G mobile and consumer markets. It highlights STMicroelectronics' dominance in Silicon Carbide (SiC) for electric vehicles, largely driven by Tesla's adoption, and its significant role in CMOS image sensors for Apple's 3D imaging and sensing applications. The article also discusses the company's strategies to address capacity constraints and maintain its market position against competitors.

title: GameStop stock market surge captures attention, enriches Michigan billionaire Donald Foss
summary: The article details the significant surge in GameStop's stock price, highlighting how it substantially increased the wealth of Michigan billionaire Donald Foss, who held a 5.3% stake. It describes the phenomenon as a battle between day traders and Wall Street short sellers, driven by activity on Reddit, and notes the skepticism of financial analysts regarding the company's underlying fundamentals. The piece also mentions the broader market impact, the involvement of figures like Elon Musk, and warnings about the irrationality of the market.

title: GM's all-electric pledge: No tailpipes by 2035, net-zero carbon by 2040
summary: General Motors announced its intention to achieve net-zero carbon status by 2040, with an aspiration to eliminate tailpipe emissions from new light-duty vehicles by 2035. The company plans to introduce 30 all-electric models globally by mid-decade and aims for 40% of its U.S. models to be battery electric vehicles by the end of 2025. This commitment is supported by a $27 billion investment in electric and autonomous vehicles over the next five years, and a push for 100% renewable energy in its facilities by 2030 in the U.S. and 2035 globally.

title: UVXY ETF Is a Good Buy as Earnings and WSB Drive Volatility
summary: The article discusses why the ProShares Ultra VIX Short-Term Futures ETF (UVXY) is a good buy amidst rising market volatility. It explains that the VIX Index, which UVXY tracks, is rising due to the earnings season, fears of a stock market bubble, and the impact of the WallStreetBets Reddit community on certain stocks. The article suggests UVXY as a way to bet on continued volatility given its asset size, liquidity, and expense ratio compared to competitors.

title: General Motors plans to exclusively offer electric vehicles by 2035
summary: General Motors announced its aspiration to exclusively offer electric vehicles by 2035, ending the production of gasoline- and diesel-powered cars, trucks, and SUVs. This move is part of the company's broader plan to become carbon neutral by 2040 in its global products and operations, and comes a day after President Joe Biden signed executive orders prioritizing climate change. GM also plans to use 100% renewable energy for its U.S. facilities by 2030 and global facilities by 2035.

title: General Motors Aims To Be Carbon Neutral By 2040
summary: General Motors announced its goal to achieve carbon neutrality by 2040, including eliminating tailpipe emissions from light-duty vehicles by 2035. The company plans to take a science-based approach and have 40% of its vehicles be battery-powered by 2025. GM also aims to power its U.S. sites with 100% renewable energy by 2030 and globally by 2035, while working with EVgo to expand fast-charging infrastructure.

title: In a Major Move Away From Fossil Fuels, General Motors Aims to Stop Selling Gasoline Cars and SUVs by 2035
summary: General Motors announced its intention to stop selling gasoline and diesel vehicles by 2035, aligning with a broader plan to achieve carbon neutrality by 2040. This significant shift by the largest U.S. automaker is driven by technological advancements making electric vehicles more affordable and a global trend towards stricter emissions regulations. While presenting a gamble for GM, the move is seen as a strategic response to evolving market conditions and policy targets set by governments like California and the Biden administration.

title: GM to only sell zero-emissions models by 2035
summary: General Motors announced a bold pledge to make all its global operations and vehicles carbon neutral by 2040, including selling only zero-emission models by 2035. This move aligns with California's emission-reduction goals and places GM ahead of rivals like Ford in its carbon neutrality target. CEO Mary Barra's strategy aims to challenge Tesla's electric vehicle dominance and reshape GM's image, investing $27 billion into 30 electric vehicles by 2025.

title: CarParts.com Launches First EV, Hybrid-Focused Shopping Hub
summary: CarParts.com has introduced a dedicated shopping hub for hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and electric vehicle (EV) owners, expanding its product offerings to over 700,000 applications. The new platform aims to simplify the search for maintenance and repair parts, addressing misconceptions that EV and hybrid parts are vastly different from those for gas-powered cars. With a growing number of older EVs and hybrids on the road, CarParts.com is investing in its infrastructure to become a leading online destination for the EV community.

title: How Tesla made it to the top
summary: Tesla, co-founded by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, was initially conceived to build high-performance electric sports cars using lithium-ion batteries. Despite facing near-bankruptcy and production challenges, Elon Musk took over as CEO in 2008 and spearheaded its growth. The company differentiated itself by integrating its entire supply chain, avoiding traditional advertising, and aiming for a global transition to clean energy, ultimately becoming the world's most valuable car company, though it now faces increasing competition from other major automakers entering the EV market.

title: GM’s all-EV plan could shake the energy industry
summary: General Motors announced its plan to stop making gas-powered cars by 2035 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040, a move expected to transform the electric vehicle market and energy industry. This significant commitment will necessitate dramatic changes to the electric grid and put GM in direct competition with Tesla. The shift also marks a major policy turnaround for GM, which previously sided with the Trump administration against stricter emissions standards.

title: GM looks to sell only emission-free vehicles by 2035
summary: General Motors announced its ambitious plan to become carbon neutral by 2040 and aims to offer only zero-emissions vehicles by 2035. This transition involves a significant investment of $27 billion and a commitment to source 100% renewable energy for its global plants by 2035, accelerating its previous timeline. While the 2035 goal for zero-emissions vehicles is stated as an "aspiration," GM is heavily investing in electric vehicle manufacturing and aligning with new Biden administration climate initiatives.

title: How To Invest In Hydrogen
summary: This article explores investment opportunities in the burgeoning hydrogen economy, highlighting the distinction between "green," "blue," and "grey" hydrogen based on production methods and environmental impact. It emphasizes government support and growing consumer interest as key drivers for this sector, while also cautioning about potentially high valuations of related companies. The author provides lists of companies active in hydrogen, underscoring the importance of understanding specific applications and production processes.

title: EV firm Microvast to go public through $3 billion merger with SPAC
summary: Electric-vehicle battery maker Microvast announced it would go public through a merger with blank-check company Tuscan Holdings Corp, valuing the combined entity at roughly $3 billion. Microvast will receive $822 million in gross cash proceeds, including a $540 million private investment. The company, founded in 2006, previously powered electric buses for the 2018 Winter Olympic Games.

title: Nio Stock Could Pull Back To $50 Before Surging To $70 Long-Term
summary: Nio stock experienced a significant surge in the past year due to the electric vehicle (EV) market boom, but a pullback to around $50 is anticipated before a potential long-term rally to $70. The company reported strong Q3 earnings with increased deliveries and positive cash flow, though much of the good news may already be priced into the stock. Investors are advised to consider investing after a dip or use strategies like covered calls to hedge positions given potential volatility and overbought technical indicators.

title: Nestle, Nvidia, and the Changing Global Equity Markets
summary: The article analyzes the shifting dynamics of global equity markets over the past decade, characterized by the dominance of U.S. technology stocks like Nvidia, in contrast to traditional companies like Nestle. It highlights the increased concentration of U.S. market indexes in technology and consumer cyclical sectors, and discusses current valuation opportunities in non-U.S. markets and value sectors like energy.

title: Hyliion Looks Enticing After Falling 70% From Its 52-Week High
summary: Hyliion (HLN) stock has fallen 70% from its 52-week high, making it an enticing prospect in the electric vehicle market, especially after the hyperbolic growth of EV stocks in 2020. Unlike competitors, Hyliion focuses on complementing existing Class 8 truck fleets with its V1 Hybrid system and the future Hypertruck ERX, which don't require new infrastructure. The company's unique approach and recent stock correction present a potential long-term investment opportunity.

title: Chip shortage hits General Motors production
summary: General Motors announced it will cut production at three North American factories and half capacity at one in South Korea due to a global semiconductor chip shortage. This comes as chipmaker Qualcomm also reported that supply constraints are hampering its sales growth. The shortage is impacting several other automakers, and projections suggest the issue could last into the third quarter of the year.

title: Israeli autotech co REE set for $3.1b value flotation
summary: Israeli autotech company REE, a developer of modular electric vehicle platforms, is set to go public in the US through a merger with SPAC 10X Capital Venture Acquisition Corp. The flotation is estimated to value REE at $3.1 billion pre-money, or $3.6 billion post-money. REE's product, the REEboard, is a modular platform designed to support various electric vehicle bodies, and the company has recently announced collaborations with Mahindra and Mitsubishi.

title: Elon Musk admits Tesla has quality problems
summary: Elon Musk has acknowledged Tesla's quality issues, particularly during new model production ramp-ups, confirming criticisms from engineering consultant Sandy Munro. Munro, who initially criticized the Model 3's quality in 2018, noted significant improvements in later production runs. Musk advised customers to either buy a Tesla at the very beginning of a model's run or once production has stabilized to avoid early quality challenges.

title: Tennessee Highways Put EV Charging Stations Every 50 Miles
summary: Tennessee is launching a new initiative to install fast-charging stations for electric vehicles every 50 miles along its major highways. This $20 million program, funded by Volkswagen emission penalties and contributions from TVA and local power companies, aims to build 50 new stations over the next three to five years, more than doubling the current number. The goal is to alleviate "range anxiety" for EV drivers and support Tennessee's target of having 200,000 light-duty electric vehicles by 2028, aligning with the state's growing EV manufacturing sector.

title: Allegro Microsystems sees record revenue in first post-IPO report
summary: Allegro MicroSystems reported record revenue of $164.4 million in its first quarter as a publicly traded company, exceeding expectations and driven largely by a strong rebound in the automotive industry. Automotive revenue accounted for 69% of the total, growing 27% from the prior quarter, with additional growth from industrial revenue and new design wins expected to contribute to future sales. The company's stock, which debuted at $14 a share, closed at $29.02, reflecting investor confidence.

title: The BOTZ Are Coming. But So Are Investing Gains

The growing electric vehicle industry, supported by President Biden's clean energy agenda, provides significant tailwinds for BOTZ and its holdings.

title: Ford posts $1.3 billion loss, ups EV spending, warns of microchip shortage
summary: Ford Motor Co. reported a $1.3 billion loss for 2020 and a $2.8 billion net loss in Q4 due to coronavirus-dampened sales and production disruptions. In response, Ford is increasing its investments in electric and autonomous vehicles to over $22 billion and $7 billion respectively through 2025. The company also warned of further headwinds from a global microchip shortage impacting its most profitable vehicles.

title: Tesla to recall 36,126 Model S and X vehicles in China over touch-screen failures
summary: Tesla is recalling 36,126 Model S and Model X vehicles in China due to touch-screen failures, stemming from limited "write cycle" memory devices. This follows a similar recall in the U.S. and an investigation in Germany for the same issue, as Tesla agreed to replace the affected memory devices with a 64 GB version. China is a significant market for Tesla, where it held a 12% share of the "new energy vehicle" category in 2020.

title: Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning talk about the early days and bringing on Elon Musk
summary: Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning recount the early days of Tesla, challenging the popular belief that Elon Musk started the company. They discuss building and delivering the first Tesla Roadster, convincing the market about electric cars, and how Elon Musk became involved. Despite later contention with Musk, Eberhard and Tarpenning remain supportive of Tesla's mission and reflect positively on their contributions.

title: Solar-Powered Charging Stations Are Vital to Promoting EVs
summary: Electrify America has installed 30 new free-to-use, off-grid solar-powered EV charging stations in rural California to promote EV adoption outside major cities. These stations, sourced from Beam Global (formerly Envision Solar), are designed to address the lack of accessible EV infrastructure in rural areas. title: In Depth: The 1,000 Kilometer Target Driving China’s Electric Car Industry Into a Frenzy
summary: Chinese EV manufacturers are intensely pursuing a 1,000-kilometer driving range on a single charge to entice consumers away from gas-powered cars, with companies like Nio promising cutting-edge solid-state batteries. The article points out that focusing solely on range might overlook other critical factors like charging infrastructure and affordable mini-EVs, which are already proving popular in the market.

title: South Florida Mayors to Visit Vegas, LA Test Tunnel for Local Commuter Rail
summary: Mayors from Miami and Fort Lauderdale are traveling to the West Coast to examine Elon Musk's Boring Company tunnel technology in Las Vegas and California. The Boring Company has already expressed interest in collaborating with Fort Lauderdale officials on potential applications.

Origin Materials, a startup creating sustainable plastic from sawdust, is going public through a SPAC merger with Artius Acquisition in a $1.8 billion deal. title: Elon Musk may be betting on Bitcoin—but here’s what 50 other CFOs really think about it
summary: A survey by Gartner Finance revealed that 95% of CFOs have no plans to purchase Bitcoin in the current year, despite Elon Musk's investment. While corporate America's curiosity about Bitcoin is growing, its volatility and cash management problems deter most finance leaders, who prioritize financial stability. However, 5% of companies plan to buy Bitcoin this year, and a larger percentage anticipate doing so in the future, with board risk aversion being less of a concern than expected.

title: Chrysler, Buick make top 10 in Consumer Reports' auto brand ranking
summary: The Chrysler and Buick brands significantly improved their standing in Consumer Reports' Brand Report Card Rankings, both moving into the top 10 out of 32 brands. title: How ST is driving Tesla and Apple e-mobility and 5G ambitions
summary: STMicroelectronics' success is heavily reliant on its key customers, Tesla and Apple. For Apple, STMicroelectronics makes significant contributions to 3D imaging and sensing, including NIR image sensors and Time of Flight detectors for iPhones, though Sony's increasing presence in Apple devices poses a potential challenge for STMicroelectronics' future in the CMOS image sensor market.

title: Tesla sticker shock: Automaker slashes prices for two models
summary: Tesla has reduced prices for its Model 3 Standard Range Plus and Model Y Standard Range by 2.6% and 4.8% respectively, while increasing prices for the Performance variants of both models. CEO Elon Musk has previously stated that Tesla's cars are too expensive, and the company frequently uses price adjustments to boost deliveries. This strategy, supported by cost cuts, aims to increase volume, according to analysts.

title: Tesla cuts Model 3 prices in Japan by as much as 24%
summary: Tesla has significantly reduced the prices of its Model 3 vehicles in Japan, with cuts reaching as high as 24%. This move comes as the company attempts to boost sales in the Japanese market. The price adjustments affect various configurations of the Model 3 lineup.

summary: The article discusses the merits of convertible bonds as an investment and highlights the Principal Spectrum Tax-Advantaged Dividend Active ETF (PQDI) as a way to gain exposure to them. title: Chief executive of Japan's Honda to step down, hand reins to R&D chief
summary: Takahiro Hachigo, CEO of Honda Motor Co., will step down on April 1 and be replaced by Toshihiro Mibe, the current head of research and development. Mibe's appointment comes as Honda accelerates its efforts in electric vehicle development amid fierce competition. Analysts believe this leadership change will help Honda accelerate its electrification strategy.

title: Elon Musk explains Tesla's $1.5B bitcoin buy
summary: Elon Musk explained that Tesla's decision to buy $1.5 billion of Bitcoin was motivated by the inability to get a return on the company's cash when fiat currency yields negative real interest. He also noted that "Bitcoin is almost as bs as fiat money," agreeing with MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor. Tesla plans to accept Bitcoin for car payments and may invest further in digital assets.

summary: SolarEdge CEO Zvi Lando discusses the company's valuation spike to $18 billion, its expansion into new renewable energy sectors, and the challenge of stepping into the role previously held by the late founder Guy Sella. title: The Future of Texas (Published 2021)
summary: Texas has strong economic prospects due to its affordability, cultural appeal, diverse population, and strong educational system, leading to significant population growth and corporate relocations. The state's political actions have also hindered climate change mitigation efforts nationally.

title: Since Three-Phase Motors Mean Triple the Components, TI Banks on Integration
summary: Texas Instruments has released a highly-integrated 48V motor driver, the DRV3255-Q1, designed to reduce PCB area by up to 30% in mild-hybrid electric vehicles (MHEVs). This single IC integrates components typically found in three separate driver circuits for three-phase motors, aiming to lower BOM, cost, and improve signal integrity. The innovation seeks to accelerate MHEV adoption by making them more affordable, safer, and greener while addressing the increasing demand for electrification.

title: Battery Maker Enovix to IPO in $1.1 Billion SPAC Deal
summary: Battery maker Enovix has agreed to go public through a business combination with Rodgers Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (NASDAQ: RSVA) in a deal valuing Enovix at over $1.1 billion. summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook revealed that the company has acquired approximately 100 companies over the past six years, averaging one acquisition every three to four weeks.
