title: The Parent of All Parents: Here's What Berkshire Hathaway Actually Does
summary: Berkshire Hathaway is a holding company led by Warren Buffett that owns about 70 private companies and minority stakes in 41 public stocks across various sectors. While it doesn't engage in manufacturing, it controls company shares and investment interests. Buffett is the top shareholder, and notable holdings include significant stakes in Apple and Coca-Cola, with a clear disinterest in investing in Tesla.

title: 'Buzz' ETF tracking social media sentiment launches Thursday amid Reddit manias in stocks
summary: The Van Eck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) has launched, aiming to track social media sentiment around stocks rather than price momentum. This ETF selects 75 stocks with bullish social media sentiment, based on a minimum $5 billion market cap and consistent social media mentions. While leveraging social media data, the ETF's criteria are designed to exclude the highly speculative "Reddit meme stocks" like GameStop, focusing instead on broader discussions.

title: Why Cathie Wood's once hot Ark Innovation ETF has lost all its 2021 gains
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK), which skyrocketed in 2020, has lost all its 2021 gains, declining 5.5% on Thursday and bringing its year-to-date decline to a similar amount. This pullback reflects a broader trend in tech stocks, driven by rising 10-year Treasury yields and fears of inflation leading to higher interest rates, which disproportionately affect growth stocks. The ETF's top holdings, including Tesla, Square, Roku, Teladoc, and Spotify, have seen significant declines.

title: BUZZ, the ETF of Social-Media Darlings, Drops in Trading Debut
summary: The VanEck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) began trading, aiming to capitalize on the retail-investing trend and the influence of social media buzz on stock performance. This ETF includes stocks like Tesla and DraftKings, aiming to capture the "new era of investing" where information is sourced and shared online.

title: Volvo XC40 Recharge Relies on Analog Devices Battery Management System
summary: The Volvo XC40 Recharge, an all-electric crossover SUV, utilizes Analog Devices, Inc.'s battery management system (BMS) and integrated circuits to maximize its driving range and performance. The ADI system helps the vehicle meet its EPA-predicted 208-mile range and facilitates fast charging capabilities. Beyond battery management, ADI's Automotive Audio Bus (A2B) also contributes to the vehicle's design by reducing wiring weight, which further enhances range.

title: Four Investments of Nancy Pelosi and Her Husband Reveal Much
summary: The article discusses four significant investments made by House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and her husband, Paul Pelosi, on December 22. These investments include shares in AllianceBernstein (AB) and call options in Apple (AAPL), Tesla (TSLA), and Walt Disney Co (DIS), totaling between $1,751,003 and $3,500,000. Experts weigh in on the implications of these bullish trades, noting that while the Pelosis are wealthy, their investment choices align with market opportunities, although the full scope and reasoning behind the trades are not publicly known.

title: Tech-heavy Nasdaq hits correction with 10.5% fall from peak
summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has entered correction territory, falling 10.5% from its February peak, as technology shares experienced a significant sell-off. This downturn was driven by concerns over rising bond yields and inflation fears stemming from a new $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief bill. While financial, restaurant, and travel stocks rose on reopening hopes, they couldn't offset the weight of declining big tech shares like Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla.

title: Tesla to boost Texas energy grid with secret mega-battery, report says
summary: Tesla is reportedly building a 100-megawatt mega-battery in Angleton, Texas, through a subsidiary named Gambit Energy Storage LLC, to enter the state's power market. This project aims to support the Texas energy grid, which faced near-total collapse during recent winter storms. The battery's construction comes amid increased scrutiny of Texas's energy infrastructure and Tesla CEO Elon Musk's growing presence and investments in the state.

title: ARK ETFs Erase 2021 Gains, Assets Hold
summary: Three of ARK Invest's seven ETFs, including the flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), have erased their 2021 gains as of early March, experiencing significant drops in value due to a sell-off in high-growth stocks. Despite these performance setbacks, all seven ARK ETFs have continued to register net inflows year-to-date, indicating persistent investor interest and confidence in the firm's disruptive technology themes. Assets under management for the ARK ETFs collectively reached $52.8 billion, making ARK the ninth-largest ETF issuer.

title: Steel Dynamics Inc. ranks No. 1 in Fortune metal industry list
summary: Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI) was ranked No. 1 in the metals industry category on Fortune's World’s Most Admired Companies list. This recognition, based on a poll of corporate executives, directors, and analysts, highlights SDI's strong operational and financial performance, innovation, and leadership. The article also notes SDI's new plant in Sinton, Texas, is expected to be operational this year and may supply steel to Tesla's Gigafactory for the Cybertruck.

title: Tesla loses a third of its value for the third time in a year
summary: Tesla Inc.'s stock experienced its third significant drop in a year, losing a third of its value from its January record high, primarily due to investor concerns about rising interest rates affecting high-valuation stocks. The selloff wiped off nearly $300 billion from its market capitalization, moving it behind Facebook. This decline is more pronounced than other major tech companies, and its shares have steadily fallen since announcing a bitcoin purchase, even as bitcoin’s price climbed.

title: Tesla shares bounce back following steep five-day decline
summary: Tesla shares rebounded on Tuesday after experiencing a significant five-day decline, which erased about $149 billion from its valuation. The recovery was fueled by positive news, including an analyst upgrade from New Street Research, a rally in Bitcoin, and a general shift in sentiment towards high-multiple technology stocks. Analyst Pierre Ferragu upgraded Tesla to buy, citing strong earnings momentum and demand, suggesting the stock could trade at a high multiple similar to Amazon's historical performance.

title: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF surges more than 10% for its best day ever
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK) surged over 10% for its best day ever, driven by a rebound in tech stocks like Tesla, Zoom Video, and Palantir. This rally helped recoup some recent sharp losses for the fund, which had been impacted by a market rotation out of high-growth tech into value stocks. Despite recent volatility, Wood remains confident in her disruptive strategy, viewing the sell-off as an opportunity to buy.

title: Exclusive: LG hopes to make new battery cells for Tesla in 2023 in U.S. or Europe -sources
summary: LG Energy Solution aims to produce advanced 4680 battery cells for Tesla's electric vehicles by 2023, considering manufacturing sites in the United States and Europe. While LG has made samples, it faces technological hurdles and has not yet secured orders from Tesla for these new cells, which Tesla is also developing in-house. LG currently supplies smaller cells to Tesla in China and is a major battery supplier for other automotive giants like General Motors.

title: West Michigan gets first Tesla service center in Grand Rapids
summary: Tesla is opening its first service center in West Michigan, located in Grand Rapids, following a settlement with the state that allows the company to sell and service its vehicles directly to customers. This new facility, which will also handle sales and delivery, is part of Tesla's expansion after previously being restricted from direct sales and service in Michigan. Michigan residents previously had to travel out-of-state for Tesla purchases and service.

title: If You Invested $1,000 In Tesla 10 Years Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Now
summary: This article evaluates the return on a hypothetical $1,000 investment in Tesla Motors (NASDAQ: TSLA) made 10 years ago. It highlights Tesla's growth from its IPO to becoming a major electric vehicle manufacturer, detailing its stock performance, market capitalization milestones, and recent fluctuations. The article illustrates the substantial profit an early investor would have accrued despite the stock's volatility.

title: BHP moves nickel and copper HQ to Toronto as Canada emerges as new clean-tech mining hotspot
summary: BHP Group Ltd. is relocating its nickel and copper exploration headquarters to Toronto, recognizing Canada as a growing hub for clean-tech mining due to anticipated surges in demand for these metals from the electric vehicle industry. Laura Tyler, BHP's chief technical officer, highlighted Toronto's strong position for mineral exploration and innovation, aligning with the company's strategy to expand its Canadian footprint through collaborations and potential deals with junior exploration firms. The move signifies a strategic shift by BHP to capitalize on the increasing global demand for battery metals driven by the transition to a low-carbon economy.

title: Gaming platform Roblox’s stock gains after Cathie Wood buys in
summary: Shares of gaming platform Roblox Corp jumped on Thursday after its stock market debut, buoyed by Cathie Wood's ARK Next Generation Internet exchange traded fund buying more than 500,000 shares. The purchase weighted Roblox at 0.47 percent of the fund and added to the strongest opening ever for a direct stock market listing. The company's stock rose 5.3 percent in late morning trades, having been up more than 20 percent earlier in the day.

title: Promotion? Musk is ‘Technoking of Tesla’, CFO is ‘Master of Coin’
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has adopted the new title "Technoking of Tesla," and CFO Zach Kirkhorn is now "Master of Coin," according to a regulatory filing, though both retain their original executive titles. Additionally, Jerome Guillen, previously president of automotive, has transitioned to lead Tesla's heavy trucking program, a move analysts view positively as the company prepares to enter the critical heavy-trucks market.

title: DMS disrupted? Not just 2 giants now
summary: The article discusses the disruption in the Dealer Management System (DMS) market, traditionally dominated by CDK and Reynolds and Reynolds. New challengers like Tekion are emerging, with clients expressing satisfaction with their offerings. The piece suggests a shift in the competitive landscape of the DMS sector.

title: Tesla Names Jerome Guillen President of Heavy Trucking
summary: Tesla has appointed Jerome Guillen as president of its heavy trucking division, signaling a strategic focus on the electric Semi program. Guillen, formerly president of automotive, will now lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi, including charging and servicing networks, as the company plans to start deliveries by the end of 2021. This move has been viewed positively by investors, with analysts highlighting Tesla's commitment to its trucking vision.

title: ElectraMeccanica picks Mesa as site of new Arizona factory to build unusual electric cars
summary: ElectraMeccanica Vehicles Corp. has chosen Mesa, Arizona, as the location for its new assembly and engineering center, which will build its three-wheeled, single-seat SOLO electric cars. The facility is expected to create between 200 and 500 jobs and could produce up to 20,000 vehicles annually. Arizona offered a compelling incentive package and a strong workforce, making it the preferred choice over Tennessee.

title: Volkswagen aims to knock Tesla out of top spot by 2025 in major EV push
summary: Volkswagen plans to become the global electric vehicle market leader by 2025, surpassing Tesla, by increasing cost-saving efforts, standardizing technologies, and boosting EV sales to 1 million this year. The company will focus on a "platform" approach for economies of scale, expand its software division to compete with tech giants, and aims for an operating return on sales of 7% to 8% by 2025. This aggressive strategy includes significant investments in battery production and software development despite challenges posed by the pandemic and semiconductor shortages.

title: CleanSpark: Ignore the Noise and Buy the Stock in 2021
summary: CleanSpark (CLSK) stock opened significantly lower after announcing a discounted stock sale. Despite this, analysts are bullish on CLSK, with a median target price suggesting over 100% upside. CleanSpark is positioned as a dual bet on bitcoin mining and microgrids, with strong revenue growth and attractive margins across its business segments.

title: Classic Range Rover Electromod Is Powered By A Tesla Drivetrain And Can Hit 60MPH In 5.2 Sec
summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design has completed its first electric conversion, transforming a Classic Range Rover into an electromod powered by a Tesla drivetrain. This restomod can achieve 0-60 mph in 5.2 seconds and boasts a 220-mile range from its 100 kWh battery pack. The company plans to continue electrifying other Land Rovers following this successful project.

title: Which Is a Better Buy? BLNK Versus CHPT Stock
summary: This article evaluates Blink Charging (BLNK) and ChargePoint (CHPT) stock to determine which is a better investment in the rapidly growing EV-charging sector. It compares their market share, valuation multiples, and growth prospects, highlighting ChargePoint's larger footprint and more favorable valuation despite the increased competition in the space. The author concludes that ChargePoint is a better bet due to its leadership position and lower valuation.

title: KULR Partners with Andretti for EV Thermal Tech
summary: KULR Technology Group announced a long-term partnership with Andretti Technologies to bring space-proven thermal management technology from Mars Rover missions to EV motorsports. The collaboration aims to develop high-performance battery solutions with top safety ratings for racing and eventually transfer this technology to mass-market EV applications. The partnership emphasizes sustainable battery management systems and preventing thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries.

title: Leverage Shares launches 25 single stock short and leveraged ETPs
summary: Leverage Shares has introduced 25 new single-stock short and leveraged (S&L) Exchange-Traded Products (ETPs) on the London Stock Exchange, expanding its existing range. These ETPs track STOXX indices and include prominent names like Tesla and PayPal, as well as UK blue chips such as Barclays and BP. The products are physically backed and available in USD, GBP, and EUR, catering to investors looking to capitalize on market shifts and hedge exposures in volatile markets.

title: EV Makers Fall on Lordstown SEC Review, Nikola Investor Sale
summary: Electric-vehicle (EV) startups experienced a downturn due to issues at Lordstown Motors and Nikola, compounded by rising Treasury yields. Lordstown Motors (RIDE), Nikola Corp. (NKLA), Nio Inc. (NIO), Workhorse Group Inc. (WKHS), XPeng Inc. (XPEV), and Li Auto Inc. (LI) all saw declines. Tesla Inc. (TSLA) also fell after the UK reduced its purchasing bonus for EVs, disqualifying Tesla models from subsidies.

title: New Meets Old in This Tesla-Powered Range Rover Classic
summary: East Coast Defenders (E.C.D.) Automotive Design has introduced an electric conversion for Range Rover Classics, featuring a Tesla Direct Drive EV powertrain and 100-kWh battery pack. This allows the classic SUV to achieve 0-60 mph in 5.2 seconds and offers a 220-mile range. The vehicle retains its vintage exterior while boasting a luxurious, modern interior, highlighting a growing trend of electrifying classic cars.

title: What Happens When You Smash a Tesla Into a Vintage Range Rover?
summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design, a restomodding company based in Florida, is building electric Range Rover Classics using Tesla drivetrains. These modified vehicles aim to resolve the notorious unreliability of vintage Land Rovers while offering a modern electric power source and extended range. The custom-built electric Range Rovers start at around $195,000, with higher-end builds approaching $300,000.

title: The Solid-State Race: Legacy Automakers Reach for Battery Breakthrough
summary: Legacy automakers are actively pursuing solid-state battery technology through partnerships with startups to gain an advantage in the electric vehicle (EV) market. This technology promises enhanced energy density, longer range, and faster charging compared to current lithium-ion batteries. While companies like Volkswagen and GM are deeply invested in this race, Tesla is notably absent, indicating its confidence in evolving existing battery designs.

title: Musk says Tesla would be shut down if its cars spied in China, elsewhere
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, stated that his company would be shut down if its vehicles were discovered to be spying in China or anywhere else, in response to reports that China's military had banned Teslas from its facilities due to security concerns over in-car cameras. Speaking at a prominent Chinese forum, Musk emphasized the strong incentive for the company to maintain confidentiality. This development comes as Tesla faces increasing competition in China, its second-largest market.

title: How Texas is luring big businesses and billionaires away from California
summary: Texas is experiencing a significant economic boom, attracting numerous companies and wealthy individuals from California, including major tech firms like Oracle, Tesla, and Apple. This migration is fueled by factors prompting a "tremendous increase" in relocations and expansions, making Texas a burgeoning business hub. The article explores the reasons behind this trend and its potential implications for the state's future.

title: TESL Simplify Volt TSLA Revolution ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:VCAR)
summary: This article provides detailed information on the TESL Simplify Volt TSLA Revolution ETF (VCAR), including its current price, key statistics, holdings, and recent news. The ETF focuses on companies involved in autonomous driving and actively manages a portfolio of global stocks, utilizing options for leveraged performance. As of March 17, 2026, VCAR was trading at $14.35, representing a 21.7% decrease since the beginning of the year, and holds a significant portion of its assets in Tesla stock.

title: 3 Mid-Cap Global Battery Manufacturer Stocks
summary: This article examines three mid-cap global battery manufacturers: Varta AG (Germany), EnerSys (USA), and Simplo Technology (Taiwan), as potential investment opportunities given the growing demand for lithium-ion batteries. It details each company's business model, revenue streams, and market position, highlighting both their strengths and potential risks. The piece concludes by suggesting that foreign battery stocks can offer diversification for investors looking beyond domestic options.

title: EV Startups Blocked From Market by Dealerships and an Old Legal Structure
summary: EV startups like Rivian, Lucid, and Lordstown are challenging existing state laws in the U.S. that largely prohibit direct-to-consumer vehicle sales, a system maintained by established auto dealerships. These startups, along with Tesla, advocate for coexisting sales models, arguing that the traditional dealership structure is ill-suited for the nascent EV market and impedes consumer adoption. Dealership associations, however, contend that current laws protect consumers and promote competition, while legacy automakers are exploring ways to integrate online sales with their franchise models.

title: Lucid Motors Deepens Expertise with Executive Team Additions and Promotions
summary: Lucid Motors has strengthened its executive team with significant additions and promotions as it prepares for customer deliveries of its Lucid Air EV in the second half of 2021. The company appointed Michael Bell as Senior VP of Digital, Achim Pantfoerder as VP of Program Management, and Nicolas Minbiole as VP of Global Quality. Additionally, Eric Bach was promoted to Senior VP – Product and Chief Engineer, and Derek Jenkins to Senior VP – Design and Brand, demonstrating Lucid's commitment to quality and innovation.

title: Frito-Lay Replaces All Diesel Vehicles at Facility With Cleaner Tech
summary: Frito-Lay has transitioned its Modesto, California snack food facility to nearly eliminate diesel vehicles by adopting zero-emission and near-zero-emission technologies. This initiative, part of PepsiCo's broader goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by over 40% by 2030, includes electric forklifts, yard trucks, box trucks, and CNG tractors, with Tesla Semi rigs expected later in the year. The company estimates this shift has already cut greenhouse gas pollution by 53% and serves as a prototype for scaling sustainable supply chain operations.

title: Tesla Cybertruck, Semi timing crucial for stock to avoid sell-off: Piper Sandler
summary: Piper Sandler analysts Alexander Potter and Winnie Dong suggest that Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) faces a potential investor sell-off if the production timelines for the Cybertruck and Semi are not clarified soon. Despite considering Tesla a high-conviction long idea, the unpredictability of production ramps for its electric trucks, especially with increasing competition and delays at new factories in Germany and Texas, could lead to temporary stock pullbacks. While Tesla aims for some Cybertruck deliveries in late 2021 if "lucky," volume production is expected in 2022, creating uncertainty that concerns analysts.

title: ‘You can now buy a Tesla with Bitcoin’: Company’s ‘Technoking’
summary: Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk announced that Tesla electric vehicles can now be purchased using Bitcoin in the United States, with plans to expand this option globally later in the year. Musk stated that Bitcoin payments to Tesla will not be converted to conventional currency, following the company's $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin last month. This move has drawn attention from other major companies like Uber and Twitter regarding their stance on cryptocurrency transactions and investments.

title: Are ARK Invest ETFs potential money traps?
summary: This article examines ARK Invest's actively managed ETFs, highlighting their extraordinary returns in the past year and the philosophy behind their focus on disruptive innovation. It addresses concerns regarding potential liquidity issues due to growing assets under management and significant holdings in illiquid stocks, presenting ARK Invest's strategies to mitigate these risks. Ultimately, the author acknowledges the risks but suggests potential for high returns for those willing to take them.

title: Tesla can now be bought for bitcoin, Elon Musk says
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla customers can now purchase its electric vehicles using Bitcoin, with availability expanding outside the US later this year. This decision follows Tesla's significant $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and marks a major step towards mainstream acceptance for the cryptocurrency. Musk also stated that Bitcoin payments received by Tesla would not be converted to traditional currency, signifying a direct embrace of the digital asset.

title: Is liftoff of Cathie Wood’s new ARK Space ETF imminent?
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management is poised to launch its new ARK Space ETF as early as next week, capitalizing on a stellar year for her funds despite recent tech stock routs. Regulatory filings indicate a potential debut around March 29, and strong investor demand is anticipated given the success of Ark's other actively managed ETFs. The new ETF will focus on US and global companies involved in space exploration and innovation, aligning with current market interest in high-growth, long-term ideas.

title: Bitcoin selloff takes a bite out of cryptocurrency’s biggest fund
summary: The Grayscale Bitcoin Trust (GBTC) has been significantly impacted by Bitcoin's recent selloff, dropping nearly double the decline of the cryptocurrency and trading at a record discount to its underlying value. This free-fall highlights a cooling in the retail-driven crypto market, exacerbated by GBTC's fixed supply and the emergence of Bitcoin ETFs in Canada which draw institutional money.

title: China EV maker Nio halts production for 5 days on chip shortage
summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer Nio has announced a five-day halt in production due to a global shortage of semiconductor chips. This decision highlights the widespread impact of the chip scarcity on the automotive industry. Nio is one of several EV makers affected by supply chain disruptions.

title: TRMB Stock: 10 Things to Know About the ARKX ETF Top Holding
summary: Trimble (TRMB) stock is gaining attention as it is the top holding in Cathie Wood's new Ark Space Exploration ETF (ARKX), making up 8.47% of the fund. Trimble, founded in 1978, specializes in positioning, modeling, connectivity, and data analytics across various industries, holding over 2,000 patents. The ARKX ETF, a first-of-its-kind fund focusing on space exploration, is expected to boost TRMB shares as many investors follow Cathie Wood's investment choices.

title: Tesla, Toyota eye restarting SUV partnership: Report
summary: Tesla and Toyota are reportedly considering restarting their partnership to develop an all-new electric-vehicle platform, focusing on a small electric SUV. This collaboration aims to leverage Tesla's electronic control and software with Toyota's vehicle platform, potentially boosting Tesla's sales in Japan. Concurrently, Tesla CEO Elon Musk previously announced plans for a more affordable electric car, targeting a $25,000 model within three years.

title: How to Buy Cathie Wood’s ARKX ETF and Whether You Should
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Investment has launched its eighth ETF, the ARK Space Exploration ETF (ARKX), which began trading on March 30. The article discusses how to purchase ARKX and evaluates its potential given the recent performance of other ARK ETFs and the shift from growth to value stocks. It also highlights the risks associated with investing in ARKX, including sectoral shifts and exposure to various industry-specific risks.

title: PayPal launches US crypto currency checkout service
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has launched a service allowing U.S. consumers to use their cryptocurrency holdings to pay at millions of its online merchants globally. This move, which applies to Bitcoin, Ether, Bitcoin Cash, and Litecoin, aims to significantly boost the use of digital assets in everyday commerce. PayPal expects this service to transition cryptocurrencies from primarily an asset class to a legitimate funding source for real-world transactions.

title: GWM to launch hydrogen-powered SUV
summary: Great Wall Motor Co. plans to introduce its first hydrogen-powered SUV this year and will deploy these vehicles during the Winter Olympics. The company has invested 2 billion yuan over the past five years in hydrogen technology and plans to invest an additional 3 billion yuan to become a top-three seller of hydrogen-powered cars by 2025. This move aligns with China's push for hydrogen development, despite skepticism from figures like Elon Musk.

title: Vale sells New Caledonia nickel assets to Trafigura
summary: Brazilian miner Vale has completed the sale of its nickel and cobalt operations in New Caledonia to a consortium including Trafigura. The deal involves a $1.1 billion investment in the assets, with Vale maintaining a supply contract for a portion of the nickel produced. This divestment follows years of financial burdens and operational issues at the Goro mine, allowing Vale to exit New Caledonia responsibly.

title: Ta Win enters into electric vehicle market as subsidiary appointed global vendor
summary: Ta Win Holdings Bhd has expanded into the global electric vehicle (EV) market after its subsidiary, Cyprium Wire Technology Sdn Bhd (CWT), was appointed as a global vendor for Aptiv plc. CWT will use its electron beam irradiation technology to manufacture cables and automotive components for Aptiv, which services 23 of the 25 largest automotive OEMs. This strategic move is expected to open significant growth prospects for Ta Win by leveraging Aptiv's extensive global presence and meeting the increasing demand for EVs.

title: Patents on Transactions Using Cryptocurrency: Square versus PayPal
summary: This article analyzes the patent portfolios of Square Inc. and PayPal Holdings, Inc. regarding cryptocurrency transactions, particularly focusing on their ability to overcome subject matter eligibility hurdles at the USPTO. It highlights how Square's patents address issues like fluctuating exchange rates and slow transaction speeds, potentially enabling it to monopolize cryptocurrency banking in the U.S. In contrast, PayPal's patents concentrate on dispute resolution and risk assessment in crypto transactions. The author also suggests strategies for patenting blockchain-related technology to avoid eligibility rejections.

title: Why Sea Limited Stock Is Still a Buy Right Now
summary: Despite a recent tech sell-off, Sea Limited (NYSE: SE) is presented as a strong buying opportunity due to its rapid revenue growth, particularly in its e-commerce and gaming divisions, and the strong performance of its digital payment business, Sea Money. The article argues that the company was unfairly impacted by the broader tech market correction and is poised for continued growth, expanding into new regions like Latin America.

title: ElectraMeccanica Picks Mesa for New EV Assembly Plant
summary: ElectraMeccanica Vehicles Corp. announced plans to build an assembly plant in Mesa, AZ, for its Solo electric car, capable of producing up to 20,000 EVs annually. The facility will also feature an engineering technical center and testing workshops. This move highlights Arizona's growing appeal as a hub for EV manufacturing, attracting other automotive companies like Atlis Motor Vehicles Inc., Lucid Motors Inc., and Nikola Corp., as well as suppliers like UACJ Automotive Whitehall Industries Inc.

title: The LIT ETF Has Investors Raking in the Gains
summary: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) has seen significant gains due to the rising demand for electric vehicles and associated battery materials like lithium. A shortage in battery production is driving up prices for these materials, leading to strong performance for LIT. Another related ETF, Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV), is also performing well as growing demand for electric car batteries is predicted to further increase material costs.

title: Apple adding 240MWh of Tesla battery storage at California solar PV facility
summary: Apple is building a 240MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) using Tesla Megapacks at its existing 280MW California Flats solar PV plant in Monterey County. This system will support Apple's 130MW portion of the solar facility, storing excess daytime energy for later use. The initiative is part of Apple's broader commitment to power its operations with 100% renewable energy and achieve carbon neutrality by 2030, a goal also adopted by over 110 of its supply chain partners.

title: Microgrid: 3 Ways to Invest in the Microgridification Trend
summary: The article discusses the growing trend of microgrids, especially in areas like California where solar mandates and unreliable main grids are common. It explains what a microgrid is and highlights three stocks—Enphase Energy (ENPH), Generac Holdings (GNRC), and SolarEdge Technologies (SEDG)—that offer investment opportunities in this expanding sector. The author, Louis Navellier, provides analysis on each company's fundamentals, growth prospects, and current ratings.

title: Inside Factory Zero, where GM is betting big on electric vehicles
summary: General Motors is making a significant shift towards electric vehicles, investing heavily in its Factory Zero plant in Michigan to produce a new lineup of EVs. The company plans to launch 30 new electric vehicles across various price points within the next five years, aiming to cease gas-powered car production by 2035. This move positions GM in a competitive EV market, currently dominated by Tesla, as automakers globally transition to electric to combat climate change.

title: Meet the highest paid CEO in S&P 500, Paycom’s $211M man
summary: Chad Richison, the founder and CEO of Paycom Software Inc., was awarded compensation valued at $211 million in 2020, making him the highest-paid CEO in the S&P 500 based on disclosures so far. This compensation package, centered on restricted shares, could be worth over $2 billion if Paycom's stock price significantly increases, demonstrating a performance-based alignment with shareholder interests. Richison's equity award is contingent on the company's share price more than doubling and reaching specific targets within the next decade.

title: Beyond Meat opens its first production plant in China
summary: Beyond Meat has opened its first end-to-end production facility outside the U.S. in Jiaxing, China, a year after entering the Chinese market. This move aims to leverage China's supply chain resources, reduce the carbon footprint of its products, and improve cost structures for its expansion in the region. The new plant will also include R&D capabilities to develop products specifically for the Chinese market, alongside the company's existing retail presence in Starbucks, KFC, and Alibaba's Hema supermarkets.

title: Toyota SUV Buying Guide
summary: This comprehensive guide walks through Toyota's diverse 2021 SUV lineup, from the compact C-HR to the full-size Land Cruiser, detailing pricing, seating, cargo space, fuel economy, and towing capacity for each model. It highlights the pros and cons of each SUV to help buyers choose the best fit for their lifestyle and needs. The article also touches on Toyota's reputation for reliability and the varying capabilities of its SUV offerings.

title: NIO and Other Chinese EV Stocks Are Getting Crushed. Here's Why.
summary: Shares of Chinese electric vehicle (EV) companies like Nio, Xpeng, and Li Auto experienced a significant decline in trading, contributing to recent investor losses in the sector. This downturn is attributed to a new reason, adding to ongoing challenges such as interest rate fluctuations and microchip shortages that have impacted EV stocks. Even Tesla has been performing poorly.

title: Buffett-Backed BYD Doubles Rival NIO's Sales in March
summary: Chinese EV maker BYD, backed by Warren Buffett, significantly outpaced rival NIO in March sales. BYD sold 16,301 battery electric vehicles (BEVs) compared to NIO's record 7,257 BEV deliveries. The article highlights BYD's broader success in new-energy vehicles and its leadership in battery technology.

title: 8 American Car Manufacturers You've Never Heard Of
summary: This article highlights eight lesser-known American car manufacturers that are either startups in the EV/hydrogen market or niche sports car producers. It details companies like Lucid Motors, specializing in high-end EVs; Elio Motors, developing a three-wheeled autocycle; Nikola, focusing on hydrogen vehicles; and others like Karma Automotive, Callaway Cars, Panoz, Fisker Inc., and Rossion Automotive, which each carve out unique spaces in the automotive industry from luxury EVs to hand-built supercars. The article emphasizes the challenges these smaller companies face in a competitive market and their potential to drive innovation.

title: First Cobalt Appoints Michael Insulan As New VP, Commercial To Advance Offtake Strategy
summary: First Cobalt Corp. has appointed Michael Insulan as Vice-President, Commercial, to spearhead the marketing of its refined cobalt sulfate production to electric vehicle manufacturers and battery cell makers. Based in Europe, Mr. Insulan will also be responsible for marketing recycled battery materials under a proposed Phase 2 expansion. This strategic move aims to strengthen First Cobalt’s position in the rapidly growing EV markets in North America and Europe.

title: El Paso businessman Paul Foster drops on Forbes' latest billionaires list
summary: El Paso businessman Paul Foster dropped to No. 1,833 on Forbes' latest list of the world's billionaires, despite his net worth increasing from $1.4 billion in 2020 to $1.7 billion in 2021. He remains the only El Pasoan on the list, which is topped by Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk. Foster's wealth primarily comes from the sale of Western Refining and his subsequent ventures in real estate development, construction, oil and gas, and sports team ownership.

title: Betting on Small Companies Yielded Big Returns (Published 2021)
summary: This article highlights how three small-cap value funds achieved significant returns in the first quarter of 2021 by taking on higher risks. Fund managers from Kinetics Small-Cap Opportunities, Hartford Small-Cap Value, and American Century Small-Cap Value discuss their investment strategies, which include concentrated holdings, focus on free cash flow, and identifying undervalued companies in various sectors. The funds' performance significantly outpaced the S&P 500, demonstrating the potential rewards of small-cap value investing.

title: Solar Roof, big price increase
summary: Several Tesla Solar Roof reservation holders report significant price increases on their previously agreed-upon contracts, with some increases reaching $20,000 to $36,000 without changes to the design. This unexpected change is leading many customers to consider canceling their orders and explore alternative solar solutions, while also highlighting concerns about Tesla's customer service and communication on these projects.

title: Cathie Wood & Ark Invest Top 25 Stocks Right Now
summary: The article discusses Cathie Wood and her investment management firm, ARK Invest, which manages the world's largest actively managed ETF focused on disruptive innovation. It highlights ARK Invest's history, impressive returns, and investment strategy concentrating on emerging technological sectors. The piece also introduces the "Cathie Wood Stocks" website, founded by Jeremy Lefebvre, as a resource for investors to track ARKK's top 25 holdings and gain insights into institutional investing.

title: REE Automotive Signs Strategic Collaboration Agreement with Magna
summary: REE Automotive has signed a strategic collaboration agreement with Magna International Inc. to develop Modular Electric Vehicles (MEVs) for technology companies and new electric mobility players. This partnership will leverage REE's REEcorner™ technology and Magna's integration expertise to create customizable EV platforms, aiming to accelerate time-to-market for next-generation electric vehicles. They will also explore Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) opportunities in the Light Commercial Vehicle sector.

title: Chinese autonomous vehicle startup WeRide scores permit to test driverless cars in San Jose
summary: WeRide, a Chinese autonomous vehicle startup, has received a permit to test driverless cars on public roads in San Jose, California. This makes WeRide the seventh company to obtain such a permit in California, signifying a crucial step toward launching commercial robotaxi or delivery services. The company, which is well-funded and primarily operates in China, is expanding its presence and testing capabilities in the U.S. market.

title: HSBC bans customers from buying bitcoin-backer MicroStrategy shares
summary: HSBC has Banned customers of its online share-trading platform from buying or transferring MicroStrategy Inc stock, classifying it as a "virtual currency product" due to the bank's policy against direct exposure to virtual currencies. While existing shares can be held or sold, new purchases are prohibited, distinguishing HSBC's stance from other major financial firms like Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley that are embracing cryptocurrency investments. MicroStrategy, led by bitcoin proponent Michael Saylor, holds significant bitcoin reserves, totaling around 91,579 bitcoins worth about $5.5 billion.

title: The Best Business Conditions of the 21st Century?
summary: The article discusses the robust economic conditions observed in early 2021, highlighted by surging car sales, record-breaking luxury vehicle sales, and manufacturing/services PMIs reaching multi-decade highs. Author Frank Holmes, citing LPL Financial and JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon, suggests these conditions point to one of the best business environments of the 21st century, despite gold's initial poor performance. The article also touches on gold miners using increased cash flow to reduce debt, creating potential buying opportunities in the sector.

title: Tesla Says Any Data It Collects in China Is Stored in the Nation
summary: Tesla Inc. has committed to storing all data collected in China within the country's borders, responding to recent concerns regarding data security. This pledge comes after Tesla vehicles were banned from military and housing complexes due to fears that built-in cameras could collect sensitive information. Grace Tao, Tesla's China head of communications, stated that the company adheres to Chinese laws and regulations and will ensure data protection.

title: Opendoor Gains After Cathie Wood's ARK Buys Shares By Investing.com
summary: Opendoor Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: OPEN) shares rose over 4% after Cathie Wood's Ark Invest added 633,400 shares to its portfolio. The company, which went public in December 2020 through a merger, reported a significant revenue drop in 2020 but expects strong sequential growth for Q1 2021. Cathie Wood is known for her bullish calls on disruptive companies like Tesla.

title: Starting from RMB 265,000, Mustang Mach-E Manufactured in China Opens for Pre-order; Ford China Launches Direct Sales Model for Electric Vehicles
summary: Ford is launching its China-made Mustang Mach-E for pre-orders, with prices starting from RMB 265,000. The company is adopting a direct sales model for its electric vehicles in China, aiming to expand its dedicated network to cover 90% of China's electrified vehicle market this year. This move is part of Ford's strategy to go "all in" on electrification and intelligence in the region, offering advanced driver-assist features and extensive charging network access to users.

title: Coinbase listing marks latest step in crypto’s march to the mainstream
summary: Coinbase Global Inc.'s listing on Nasdaq is a significant step for cryptocurrencies moving into the financial mainstream, being the largest listing by a crypto firm yet and boosting awareness among investors. While many see it as positive for Bitcoin and the broader crypto sector, some investors caution about the volatility risks and regulatory uncertainties associated with the asset class. Coinbase's revenues are highly correlated to Bitcoin's performance, raising concerns about its long-term stability.

title: Why electric vehicles are a risky move for Polaris
summary: Polaris Inc., a major player in the off-road vehicle market, saw revenue growth in 2020 due to increased interest in powersports and outdoor activities. The company is now expanding its electric vehicle offerings, a move that some analysts view as risky. Challenges include potential performance issues with electric off-road vehicles and intense competition in the growing EV sector.

title: Audi Q4 e-Tron Takes On Tesla (|TSLA) Model Y With Entry-Priced Electric SUV
summary: Audi is launching its new Q4 e-tron, an entry-priced electric SUV, to compete directly with Tesla's Model Y in the compact crossover market. Parent company Volkswagen AG aims to use Audi's new offering to reduce Tesla's lead in electric car sales. The Q4 e-tron boasts a range of up to 520 kilometers.

title: Taiwan's Pegatron to build Tesla parts plant in Texas - report
summary: Taiwanese manufacturer Pegatron, a key supplier for Apple Inc., has reportedly selected a site in El Paso, Texas, to construct a plant that will produce components for Tesla Inc. The company stated that specific details regarding its overseas plant investments are still in the planning stages, though it had previously announced intentions to build a U.S. factory. Pegatron views electric vehicles as a significant growth area for its business.

title: Wolverine Worldwide Taps Kathleen Wilson-Thompson to Board
summary: Wolverine Worldwide has appointed Kathleen Wilson-Thompson to its board of directors, effective May 5, increasing the board to 12 members. Wilson-Thompson, who recently retired as EVP and global chief human resources officer at Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc., brings extensive experience from large consumer-focused businesses like Kellogg Co. and currently serves on the board of Tesla Inc. Her appointment is expected to help drive Wolverine Worldwide's Global Growth Agenda with her leadership experience.

title: Mattel Unveils First-of-its-Kind, CarbonNeutral® Matchbox® Tesla Roadster Die-cast Vehicle Made from 99% Recycled Materials to Serve as Brand Blueprint
summary: Mattel announced its "Drive Toward a Better Future" initiative, aiming for all Matchbox die-cast cars, playsets, and packaging to be made from 100% recycled, recyclable, or bio-based plastic by 2030. As part of this commitment, Mattel is launching the Matchbox Tesla Roadster, a CarbonNeutral® die-cast vehicle made from 99% recycled materials, available in 2022. The broader Matchbox brand will incorporate more eco-friendly materials, enhanced consumer recycling through product design, and an overall eco-friendly play theme.

title: Mattel Unveils First-of-its-Kind, CarbonNeutral® Matchbox® Tesla Roadster Die-cast Vehicle Made from 99% Recycled Materials to Serve as Brand Blueprint
summary: Mattel has announced the launch of a CarbonNeutral® Matchbox® Tesla Roadster, made from 99% recycled materials. This new die-cast vehicle aims to serve as a blueprint for the brand's future sustainability initiatives. This initiative highlights Mattel's commitment to eco-friendly production within its toy lines.

title: NFT Inc. reimagines urban and rural living with flying car ASKA
summary: NFT Inc. is launching preorders for its electric flying car, ASKA, aiming to succeed where other startups have failed in bringing a drive-and-fly vehicle to market. The SUV-sized ASKA, priced at $789,000, is designed for door-to-door transportation and is anticipated for delivery in 2026, contingent on regulatory developments. The company believes ASKA will transform urban and suburban life by providing greater mobility and is prioritizing safety with hybrid gasoline-electric power and semi-autonomous technology for new pilots.

title: Wolverine appoints Kathleen Wilson-Thompson to its Board of Directors
summary: Wolverine Worldwide has appointed Kathleen Wilson-Thompson to its Board of Directors, effective May 5, 2021. Wilson-Thompson, who previously served on the board of Tesla and was Executive Vice President and Global Chief Human Resources Officer at Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc., brings extensive experience from large consumer-focused businesses. Her appointment is expected to help drive Wolverine Worldwide's global growth agenda.

title: If Copper is the New Oil, This ETF Is Looking Golden
summary: The article highlights copper's growing importance, with Goldman Sachs dubbing it the "new oil" due to increasing demand driven by infrastructure plans, electric vehicles, and renewable energy. The Global X Copper Miners ETF (COPX) is presented as an investment option to capitalize on this trend, offering targeted exposure to copper mining companies. Projections suggest significant price increases for copper in the coming years.

title: Oracle plans to bring 8,500 jobs, $1.2 billion campus to Nashville
summary: Oracle Corporation plans to invest $1.2 billion in Nashville, bringing 8,500 jobs with an average salary of $110,000 to the city. This development would be the largest in Tennessee's history, involving significant public infrastructure contributions from Oracle without burdening taxpayers. The new campus will transform Nashville's East Bank, creating a major technology hub.

title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX wins $2.9-billion NASA contract for moon spacecraft
summary: NASA has awarded Elon Musk's SpaceX a $2.9 billion contract to develop a spacecraft for returning astronauts to the moon as early as 2024, bypassing competitors like Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin. This contract is part of NASA's Artemis program, aiming for a sustained lunar presence and eventually missions to Mars. SpaceX will need to conduct a test flight before human missions, deepening its collaboration with NASA.

title: Tesla Runs on Faith, Exxon Runs on Discipline. Only One Is Right
summary: This article contrasts the leadership styles and visions of Elon Musk of Tesla and Darren Woods of Exxon Mobil regarding the future of energy. Musk is portrayed as a publicity-driven Technoking with diverse ventures, while Woods is presented as a low-profile, disciplined CEO. The piece suggests that despite their companies having "similar belief premiums," their approaches are fundamentally incompatible.

title: AutoX Selects Arbe's 4D Imaging Radar Platform for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
summary: Arbe announced that AutoX has selected its 4D Imaging Radar Platform for integration into 400,000 Level 4 autonomous vehicles, including RoboTaxis, over the next five years. This partnership aims to enhance safety and performance by utilizing Arbe's ultra-high resolution radar systems, which offer 100 times more detail than other market radars. The collaboration emphasizes an effort to elevate safety standards for L4 autonomous vehicles, particularly in dense urban environments like those in China.

title: Battle Motors Acquires Crane Carrier Company Launching Path to Class 7 and 8 Vocational Truck Electrification
summary: Battle Motors, a leader in EV technology, has acquired Crane Carrier Company (CCC), a significant move towards electrifying Class 7 and 8 vocational trucks. This acquisition combines CCC's 75 years of commercial vehicle manufacturing with Battle Motors' EV expertise to introduce full electric severe-duty trucks to the market, set to launch this summer. The combined entity plans to significantly expand production capabilities in New Philadelphia, Ohio, boosting the local economy and accelerating the transition to sustainable energy in the vocational truck sector.

title: NatWest will refuse to serve business customers who accept cryptocurrencies
summary: NatWest has announced it will not serve business customers who accept cryptocurrency payments, deeming them "high risk" due to the volatile and unregulated nature of crypto assets. This decision positions NatWest against other major banks and could impact companies looking to integrate digital currency payments. The bank emphasized its cautious approach, citing concerns about financial crime and the potential for consumers to lose all their invested cash.

title: Enrique Casas Cofradía '23 Leverages Pacific's Strengths, Lands EV Internship
summary: Enrique Casas Cofradia, a Pacific University student double-majoring in physics and business administration, secured a paid Pioneering Diversity Internship with the Eversource Energy Center at the University of Connecticut. His internship focuses on electric vehicle adoption rates and their economic impact on the power grid. Cofradia, who is passionate about renewable energy, used his interdisciplinary studies to prepare for a career in the electric vehicle sector.

title: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest piles into UiPath, trims Tesla
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest purchased shares of automation software provider UiPath (PATH.N) during its stock market debut, while simultaneously reducing its holdings in Tesla (TSLA.O). The firm's ETFs bought approximately 2.7 million UiPath shares and also invested in Coinbase Global Inc (COIN.O). ARK Invest's Innovation ETF sold 163,981 shares of Tesla.

title: Tesla’s bad week in China was months in the making
summary: Tesla Inc. faced significant backlash in China, its second-biggest market, stemming from a customer protest over malfunctioning brakes and its subsequent handling of the incident. The company's initial "no compromise" stance and a comment by its VP questioning the customer's motives led to widespread criticism from state media, highlighting a struggle to adapt its corporate culture to the Chinese market. This incident reflects broader challenges for foreign brands in China and precedes past concerns over quality and earlier scrutiny by the Chinese military regarding vehicle cameras.

title: Honda Targets 100% EV Sales in North America by 2040, Makes New Commitments to Advances in Environmental and Safety Technology
summary: Honda has announced ambitious goals for North America, aiming for 100% electrified vehicle sales by 2040, with interim targets of 40% by 2030 and 80% by 2035. The company also committed to achieving carbon neutrality and zero traffic collision fatalities involving its products globally by 2050, introducing a new EV platform ("e:Architecture") and enhancing its advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). These initiatives encompass advancements in battery technology, fuel cell development, and increased use of renewable energy in its operations.

title: Honda aims for 100% electric vehicles by 2040, says new CEO
summary: Honda Motor Co.'s new CEO, Toshihiro Mibe, announced the company's goal to make electric vehicles (EVs) and fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) 100% of its sales by 2040. This strategy aligns with the Japanese government's carbon-free goals, with interim targets of 40% EV/FCV sales by 2030 and 80% by 2035 in major markets. Honda plans to invest approximately 5 trillion yen in R&D over the next six years to support this transition.

title: Is MicroVision (MVIS) Really the Great Buy Reddit Makes It Out To Be?
summary: MicroVision (MVIS) stock surged after becoming a hot topic on Reddit’s WallStreetBets forum, with its price increasing by 144 percent year-to-date and 5,200 percent over the last year. Despite one analyst giving it a significantly lower price target, the article suggests MVIS is a good long-term investment due to its exposure to the growing lidar technology market. Retail investors are also speculating on a potential short squeeze given the stock's high short interest.

title: ‘That’s crazy!’: Tesla CEO Musk gives carbon removal $100m boost
summary: Elon Musk has launched a $100 million prize competition to encourage the development of new carbon capture technologies. The initiative aims to address the pressing need for scalable and affordable methods to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and oceans, thereby combating global warming. This four-year challenge, described as the largest incentive prize in history, seeks viable solutions capable of removing 1,000 tonnes of CO2 annually with long-term sequestration.

title: Tesla Inc To Setup India Headquarters In Mumbai: Report
summary: Tesla Inc. is reportedly establishing its India headquarters in Mumbai, specifically in the Lower Parel-Worli area, with plans for a 40,000 sq ft office. The company will also set up its production base in Karnataka and is preparing to launch its first electric cars in India with three models. Tesla has already begun hiring key personnel for its Indian operations.

title: Elon Musk: Climate is daunting, but I’m more worried about AI
summary: Elon Musk has launched a $100 million climate contest for carbon removal, which he views as an "insurance policy" against potential nonlinear climate change, rather than a solution for imminent doom. Despite funding this initiative, Musk stated his primary concerns are artificial intelligence and population collapse, considering climate change a manageable problem. The XPRIZE competition seeks scalable, low-cost carbon removal technologies, with initial funding for student teams and milestone prizes, culminating in a $50 million grand prize for gigaton-scale carbon removal.

title: Procter & Gamble Is One of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies | TIME
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) was recognized as one of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies due to its significant performance during the pandemic. The company saw a banner year with $71 billion in sales, a 6% increase, driven by high demand for its household products like Charmin and Tide. Additionally, P&G repurposed its manufacturing capabilities to produce hundreds of thousands of face shields for healthcare workers.

title: Tesla Inc. Is One of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies
summary: Tesla Inc. has been recognized as one of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies for its significant impact on the automotive and renewable energy sectors. In 2020, Tesla became the world's most valuable car company and a leader in electric energy generation and storage with its Powerwall, Powerpack, and Solar Roof divisions. The company is highlighted for its glamorous cars and its cooler commitment to clean, renewable energy.

title: Tesla beats quarterly revenue expectations on robust demand
summary: Tesla Inc. reported its seventh consecutive quarter of profit, exceeding revenue expectations due to strong demand for its Model 3 sedan. The company reiterated its multi-year outlook for 50% growth in deliveries and is expanding operations across three continents with new factories in Texas and Berlin. Despite a positive quarter, Tesla faces increased competition from both established automakers and new EV startups.

title: GM named one of Time's 'Most Influential Companies'
summary: General Motors Co. was recognized by Time Magazine as one of the 100 Most Influential Companies for its efforts in engineering a greener future with electric vehicles. GM was the only Detroit Three automaker on the list, cited alongside Volkswagen and Tesla for their commitment to electrifying the auto industry. Despite significant investment in EVs and a goal to sell 1 million globally by 2025, GM faces challenges in convincing investors it's as valuable an EV leader as Tesla.

title: Model 3 Charging Hubbell HBL2810 Receptacle
summary: A Tesla Model 3 owner sought advice on charging their vehicle using a Hubbell HBL2810 receptacle in an apartment parking stall. Forum members recommended using a two-adapter solution or a custom adapter from EVSE Adapters to convert the L21-30 outlet for Tesla's Mobile Connector. The owner later confirmed that a custom L21-30 to Gen 2 adapter from EVSE Adapters worked effectively, providing about 200V charging.

title: Biden wants to build 500,000 charging stations. Where we stand and how we get there
summary: President Biden has proposed a significant investment of at least $15 billion to establish 500,000 electric vehicle charging stations across the nation by 2030. Currently, there are approximately 102,000 public charging outlets at about 42,000 stations, with a large concentration in California. The initiative aims to expand this infrastructure considerably over the next decade.

title: Tesla accused of environmental rule violations in U.S. and Germany
summary: Tesla is facing accusations of environmental rule violations in both the U.S. and Germany. In the U.S., the EPA alleges Tesla failed to prove compliance with federal emissions standards for hazardous air pollutants, particularly concerning vehicle surface coating at its Fremont plant. Meanwhile, German authorities fined Tesla 12 million euros for allegedly not fulfilling obligations regarding the take-back of old customer batteries.

title: Morgan Stanley, Veteran Broker Dinged $800k Over Amazon Short
summary: Morgan Stanley and veteran broker Jacob G. Shapira have been ordered to pay nearly $800,000 in damages to Israeli company Mikedmat Dena Inc. following unsuitable and unauthorized trades, including shorting Amazon stock. The FINRA arbitration panel found Shapira liable for trades made between 2015 and 2020. Shapira has a history of customer disputes, with several prior complaints alleging unsuitable and unauthorized trading.

title: GM to invest $1 billion in Mexico for electric vehicle production, angering UAW members
summary: General Motors announced plans to invest over $1 billion in its Ramos Arizpe production complex in Mexico to produce electric vehicles starting in 2023. This decision has angered United Auto Workers Vice President Terry Dittes, who called it a "slap in the face" to union members and U.S. taxpayers. Dittes argues that government subsidies for EVs should not go to companies using labor outside the U.S.

title: GM Mexico's $1 billion EV investment called 'slap in the face' by UAW
summary: General Motors Mexico announced a $1 billion investment to transition its Ramos Arizpe plant to build electric vehicles by 2023, drawing strong criticism from the United Auto Workers (UAW). The UAW called the investment a "slap in the face" to American workers and taxpayers, especially given President Biden's push for American-made EVs and government subsidies to the auto industry. GM defended its decision, citing its global operations and significant EV investments within the U.S., while U.S. Rep. Debbie Dingell also emphasized the need for EV manufacturing in America.

title: Is Saudi Arabia going to rev up a homegrown EV maker?
summary: Saudi Arabia is exploring the establishment of its own domestic electric-vehicle maker, aiming to diversify its oil-reliant economy and boost local manufacturing. The Public Investment Fund (PIF), which previously invested in Tesla and currently holds significant gains from Lucid Motors, is behind these efforts. The initiative highlights the kingdom's commitment to industrial growth and expanding its automotive infrastructure.

title: Ark Invest: How to choose & buy Ark ETFs in Singapore, Money News
summary: This article details Ark Invest ETFs, explaining their focus on disruptive innovation and providing an overview of all 8 available Ark ETFs. It specifically analyzes the Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK), outlining its pros and cons, and offers guidance on how Singaporean investors can buy Ark ETFs.

title: Vietnam's answer to Tesla has U.S. in its electric sights
summary: VinFast, the automotive arm of Vietnam's largest conglomerate Vingroup, is aggressively targeting the U.S. electric vehicle market. The company plans to offer electric SUVs and a battery leasing model, aiming for a U.S. stock market listing and a valuation potentially as high as $60 billion. VinFast is a relatively new player, currently the fifth-largest car brand in Vietnam, and hopes to compete with established leaders like Tesla and General Motors.

title: EXCLUSIVE Tesla, under scrutiny in China, steps up engagement with regulators
summary: Facing scrutiny over safety and customer service complaints in China, Tesla is increasing its engagement with mainland regulators and expanding its government relations team. This shift in strategy demonstrates the company's recognition of the challenges in its second-biggest market. This increased interaction includes attending policy discussions and recruiting government relations managers, a notable change from their previous limited presence in such closed-door meetings.

title: KraneShares Electric Vehicles and Future Mobility Index ETF (NY: KARS)
summary: This article provides a stock quote and performance data for the KraneShares Electric Vehicles and Future Mobility Index ETF (KARS). It details recent trading activity, key financial metrics, and a compilation of news headlines related to electric vehicles and the ETF's holdings. The article also includes frequently asked questions about KARS, such as its public trading status, exchange, ticker symbol, current price, and market capitalization.

title: EBay says open to accepting to cryptocurrencies in future, exploring NFTs
summary: EBay Inc. announced its openness to accepting cryptocurrency as a form of payment and is exploring ways to integrate non-fungible tokens (NFTs) onto its platform. While there are no immediate plans, the company is actively monitoring the evolving cryptocurrency landscape and the growing popularity of NFTs, similar to other major companies like Tesla and PayPal that have embraced virtual currencies. EBay CEO Jamie Iannone confirmed these explorations, noting the company's long-standing connection to collectibles.

title: Judge orders Tesla to provide documents involving Elon Musk’s compensation
summary: A Delaware judge has ordered Tesla to provide communications involving Elon Musk's compensation plan from 2018. This ruling stems from a lawsuit filed by shareholders who accuse Musk and the board of breaching their fiduciary duties and engaging in unjust enrichment related to a plan that could pay Musk over $50 billion.

title: CoStar To Employees: Come Back To The Office And Get A Tesla
summary: CoStar is incentivizing its vaccinated employees to return to the office with a variety of prizes, including a new Tesla, $10,000 cash, and an all-expenses-paid trip to Barbados. This initiative, launched alongside a company-wide vaccine rollout, aims to boost office occupancy, which has risen from 4 percent to 20 percent since the program began. CEO Andrew Florance stated that these creative incentives are part of an ongoing effort to adjust to new workplace realities post-pandemic, as other companies also explore various strategies to encourage office returns.

title: SolarEdge Shipped 1.69 GW AC Solar Inverters In Q1/2021
summary: SolarEdge reported GAAP revenues of $405.5 million in Q1/2021, a 6% decline year-over-year but a 13% sequential increase. Its solar products business contributed $376.4 million, with 1.69 GW AC products shipped, 45% commercial and 55% residential, with the US market being a significant contributor. The company faces increased ocean freight costs and is navigating chip shortages, with analysts anticipating a stronger performance beyond FY21.

title: S&P Dow Jones brings bitcoin, ethereum to Wall St with cryptocurrency indexes
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices launched new cryptocurrency indexes, including the S&P Bitcoin Index, S&P Ethereum Index, and S&P Crypto Mega Cap Index, to track the performance of digital assets. This move aims to further mainstream cryptocurrencies by integrating them into Wall Street trading. The company plans to expand the list of covered coins and allow clients to create specialized benchmarking tools, utilizing data from Lukka.

title: Tesla Inc. (TSLA) Q1 2021 Earnings Call
summary: This article provides details about Tesla Inc.'s (TSLA) Q1 2021 earnings call, which took place on April 26, 2021. It lists the corporate participants, including Elon Musk and Zach Kirkhorn, and the attending analysts. The article also indicates that the full earnings call transcript is available for reading via a provided link.

title: GM expects to offer personal self-driving vehicles to consumers this decade
summary: General Motors (GM) CEO Mary Barra anticipates that the automaker will offer personal autonomous vehicles to consumers later this decade, following the showcase of a Cadillac self-driving concept car. While the technology is initially expensive and tested for ride-hailing, GM is also expanding its Super Cruise system for advanced driver assistance. This move opens possibilities for subscription revenue and fully autonomous capabilities, despite the challenges faced by the industry in commercializing self-driving cars.

title: California #50 (again) in Chief Executive Mag’s Best & Worst States For Business 2021
summary: For the 17th consecutive year, California has been ranked last at #50 in Chief Executive Magazine's "Best and Worst States for Business" survey. The article highlights that high taxes, burdensome regulations, and business closures during the pandemic have driven major companies like Tesla, Hewlett Packard, and Oracle out of the state. Other states like Texas and Florida top the list due to favorable tax policies, regulatory climates, and their handling of business operations during the COVID pandemic.

title: E-Commerce Giant MercadoLibre Discloses $7.8M Bitcoin Buy
summary: Latin American e-commerce company MercadoLibre announced a $7.8 million Bitcoin purchase in its latest earnings report, integrating the cryptocurrency into its treasury strategy. This move follows previous bitcoin-related initiatives by the company, including a bitcoin-only real estate platform and integrating bitcoin payments in 2015. While smaller than investments by MicroStrategy or Tesla, it signifies a notable step towards mainstreaming Bitcoin as a payment and reserve asset.

title: Tesla tells regulator that full self-driving cars may not be achieved by year-end
summary: Tesla has informed a California regulator that it may not achieve full self-driving technology by the end of the current year, despite CEO Elon Musk's previous optimistic statements. A memo from the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) indicates that Tesla's current technology is at Level 2, requiring human supervision, and that Musk's earlier claims were extrapolations. The DMV emphasized the dangers of public misunderstanding regarding the limits of such technology, especially as incidents involving Tesla vehicles are under investigation.

title: Die lubricant solutions for next generation large die casting machines
summary: This article discusses how innovative lubricant technology, specifically water-free electrostatic systems like Lubrolene from Quaker Houghton, is supporting the new generation of large die casting machines in the automotive industry. These solutions address the challenges of manufacturing larger, lighter, and more complex vehicle parts by improving quality, productivity, reducing costs, and extending tool life. The technology helps achieve better lubricant deposition, reduces environmental impact, and offers significant cost savings compared to traditional water-based lubricants.

title: China tech giants bet US$19 billion on global electric car frenzy
summary: Chinese tech giants like Huawei, Xiaomi, and Baidu are pouring nearly US$19 billion into electric and self-driving vehicle ventures, aiming to capitalize on the high-tech shift in the automotive industry. This aggressive push establishes China as a major battleground for EV innovation, with companies making strategic tie-ups and unveiling their own car-making plans. Despite the hyper-competitive market and significant capital requirements, these tech companies are focused on making intelligent vehicles, with their main revenue expected to come from post-sale services and software rather than just car sales.

title: New self-driving cars will have sensors that aren't so ginormous
summary: Pony.ai, a Chinese autonomous vehicle startup, has partnered with Luminar to unveil a new self-driving car design that integrates sensors more sleekly into the vehicle's roof, making them less bulky than current models. Despite their slimmed-down appearance, the vehicles can still detect objects up to 500 meters away. While this design is an aesthetic improvement, the article emphasizes that the primary challenge in autonomous vehicles remains making them consistently reliable and safe in complex urban environments, a problem many companies are still grappling with.

title: Walmart, Tesla Added to S&P ESG Index, While Victoria's Secret-Owner and Facebook Get the Boot
summary: The S&P 500's ESG Index underwent its annual adjustments, adding 45 stocks including Tesla, Disney, Walmart, and Etsy, while dropping 21 companies such as Facebook, Victoria's Secret-owner L Brands, and Costco. Tesla was included due to its clean energy efforts, and Walmart for improvements in human rights. Facebook was removed for deteriorating environmental reporting, and L Brands for poor ESG performance compared to peers.

title: US Tesla owner killed in fiery crash was initially driving car
summary: A preliminary report by the US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) indicates that the owner of a Tesla Model S, who died in a fiery crash, was driving the car when it left his house. Surveillance footage shows the owner entering the driver's seat before the vehicle drove away. While the report doesn't confirm if he was driving at the exact moment of impact, it suggests the possibility, supporting Tesla's claim that its driver assistance technology was not engaged.

title: EXCLUSIVE Tesla puts brake on Shanghai land buy as U.S.-China tensions weigh - sources
summary: Tesla has reportedly canceled plans to acquire land for expanding its Shanghai plant into a global export hub due to ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs on imported Chinese electric vehicles. The company intends to limit the proportion of its global production from China and did not bid on a nearby land plot previously considered for expansion. Despite this, Tesla's Shanghai factory is "developing as planned" and it is reportedly still considering increased capacity on its existing site and other component production facilities.

title: Cathie Wood’s misery mounts as ARKK ETF’s assets drop below $20BN
summary: Cathie Wood's flagship Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK) has seen its assets drop below $20 billion, the lowest since January, due to a broad tech selloff. The fund has declined for nine of the past 10 sessions, with investors pulling over $500 million in May. Bearish sentiment is growing, reflected in record put contracts and high short interest, as the stock rotation out of expensive tech names impacts the fund's performance.

title: GM Wants Its $7,500 EV Tax Credit Back
summary: General Motors CEO Mary Barra is advocating for the reinstatement of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit, arguing that GM is being penalized for being an early adopter in the electric vehicle market. The credit currently phases out after an automaker sells 200,000 EVs, a threshold GM and Tesla have already reached. Barra and other GM executives believe this creates an uneven playing field, disadvantaging companies that invested in EVs early, while newer entrants still benefit from the incentive.

title: 7 ESG Stocks That Could Come Under Fire if the SEC Gets Its Way
summary: The SEC is increasing its scrutiny of ESG (environmental, social, and governance) claims and reporting, which could lead to increased regulations and potentially impact the performance of several ESG-focused stocks and ETFs. This article highlights seven such entities, including the SPDR S&P 500 ESG ETF, Beyond Meat, Tesla, and Microsoft, explaining why they might face challenges under heightened regulatory oversight. The author notes that stricter reporting standards could reveal weaknesses or question the current "ESG-friendly" positioning of these companies.

title: Tesla’s Musk halts use of bitcoin for car purchases
summary: Tesla will no longer accept Bitcoin for car purchases, announced CEO Elon Musk, due to environmental concerns over the energy-intensive "mining" process, which often relies on fossil fuels. This decision, coming less than two months after Tesla began accepting Bitcoin, caused the cryptocurrency's value to drop. Despite the halt, Tesla will retain its Bitcoin holdings and Musk reaffirmed his belief in cryptocurrencies, planning to use them once more sustainable energy sources for mining are adopted.

title: Elon Musk Says Tesla Has Suspended Accepting Bitcoin for Vehicle Purchases - WSJ
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced the company has suspended accepting Bitcoin for vehicle purchases due to concerns about the rapidly increasing use of fossil fuels, particularly coal, for Bitcoin mining and transactions. Musk stated that Bitcoin would be used for transactions again once its mining transitions to more sustainable energy sources. The decision highlights ongoing debates about cryptocurrencies' environmental impact and their viability for widespread payments.

title: How to Get Better Gas Mileage
summary: Amid concerns of gas shortages due to the Colonial Pipeline cyberattack, this article provides six tips from AAA and Universal Technical Institute experts on how drivers can conserve fuel when their tanks are low. It also offers advice on creating fuel-saving habits through regular car maintenance.

title: EXCLUSIVE Tesla in talks with China’s EVE for low-cost battery supply deal -sources
summary: Tesla is reportedly in advanced talks with Chinese battery maker EVE Energy Co to add them to its Shanghai factory supply chain, aiming to secure a supply of cheaper lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. This move would make EVE the second LFP battery supplier to Tesla in China, after CATL, as Tesla seeks to cut costs and diversify its battery sources amidst rising competition and regulatory pressures in the Chinese market. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has previously indicated a shift towards iron-cathode batteries for standard range cars due to nickel supply concerns.

title: ElectraMeccanica breaks ground on Mesa manufacturing facility
summary: ElectraMeccanica Vehicles Corp. has broken ground on its first U.S. assembly facility and engineering technical center in Mesa, Arizona, marking the third EV manufacturing groundbreaking in Arizona since 2019. The facility, an investment of over $35 million, will provide local assembly for the brand's SOLO electric vehicle and is expected to be completed by Spring 2022. This expansion highlights Arizona's booming electric vehicle industry and will bring hundreds of jobs to the Mesa community.

title: Biggest deal in Korea: Hanon Systems stake sale draws KKR, Carlyle, TPG
summary: The sale of a near-70% stake in South Korean auto parts supplier Hanon Systems Corp. has commenced, attracting major private equity firms like KKR, Carlyle, and TPG, with an expected valuation of around 7 trillion won ($6.2 billion), potentially making it Korea's largest M&A deal. The high price tag, coupled with potential consortiums involving LG Electronics and Carlyle, presents both significant opportunities and hurdles for interested bidders. Hanon's robust client portfolio and position in the growing EV thermal management market are attractive, but concerns exist regarding its valuation compared to industry peers and current market conditions.
