title: Greenidge Commits to Being 100% Carbon Neutral for Its Bitcoin Mining Facility Starting June 2021
summary: Greenidge Generation Holdings Inc. announced its commitment to offset all greenhouse gas emissions from its Bitcoin mining facility starting June 1, 2021, through accredited offset credits. The company also plans to invest a portion of its mining profits in renewable energy projects and will continue participating in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI). This move comes amidst growing environmental concerns regarding Bitcoin mining, as highlighted by recent actions from Tesla and legislative proposals in New York.

title: A year after Trump’s visit, Biden finds a different Ford
summary: President Biden is set to visit Ford Motor Co. to highlight the company's electric vehicle advancements, particularly the F-150 Lightning, contrasting with former President Trump's 2020 visit that focused on COVID-19 related manufacturing. This shift underscores a dramatic change in political and automotive industry priorities toward EVs within a year, driven by Ford's accelerated electrification strategy under new leadership and Biden's infrastructure plan. The article also touches on market reception, regulatory changes, and how Ford's EV strategy compares to competitors like GM.

title: Tesla SUV Buying Guide
summary: This buying guide from Cars.com provides an overview of Tesla's two SUV models, the Model Y and Model X, focusing on their features, pricing, and performance. It highlights Tesla's unique operational style of continuous software updates and frequent product configuration changes, and discusses key elements like the Autopilot system, range, and interior design for both models. The article also touches upon the federal tax credit eligibility, noting that Teslas no longer qualify, and offers pros and cons for each SUV.

title: Katia Uriarte Reports: 1-on-1 Interview with Port Of Corpus Christi CEO Sean Strawbridge
summary: Port of Corpus Christi CEO Sean Strawbridge discusses the port's growth, economic resiliency, and future outlook in a 1-on-1 interview. He highlights the port's role as the nation's leading crude oil exporter and the expected arrival of Tesla suppliers to the region, utilizing products from Steel Dynamics. Despite a slight decrease in the first quarter of 2021, Strawbridge remains optimistic about continued growth and diversification beyond oil and gas.

title: What 'regulatory credits' are — and why they're so important to Tesla
summary: Regulatory credits incentivize automakers to produce electric vehicles, which Tesla, as an all-electric carmaker, receives for free and sells to other manufacturers for profit. This income has significantly contributed to Tesla's profitability, but investor Michael Burry views its reliance on these credits as a red flag, leading him to take a short position against the company. Tesla's CFO stated that while regulatory credit sales may remain strong for a few more quarters, they are not expected to be a material part of the business long-term, and some major customers like Stellantis may soon no longer need to purchase them.

title: ZF and Mobileye Safety Technology Chosen by Toyota
summary: Toyota Motor Corp has selected ZF and Mobileye to develop advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) for its upcoming vehicle platforms. This collaboration will integrate Mobileye’s EyeQ4 vision computing system-on-chip with ZF’s Gen 21 mid-range radar technology to enhance safety and driver convenience. This agreement represents a significant expansion for both Mobileye and ZF in providing advanced safety solutions to the automotive industry.

title: 7 Stocks Equipped to Handle America’s Electric Vehicle Charging Needs
summary: The article highlights seven stocks poised to benefit from the growing electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure market, which is projected to reach $56.9 billion by 2026. It emphasizes that while EV manufacturers receive significant attention, the essential infrastructure for charging, like charging stations and more powerful batteries, is crucial for widespread EV adoption. The article profiles companies such as ChargePoint, Blink Charging, Plug Power, Tesla, Siemens AG, British Petroleum, and Nio, detailing their contributions and positioning within the evolving EV ecosystem.

title: Bitcoin Price Plunge 'Feels Like Capitulation,' Says Galaxy's Mike Novogratz
summary: Mike Novogratz, CEO of Galaxy Digital, stated that Bitcoin's recent price dip below $40,000 felt like a "capitulation" event, where investors sell off assets rather than holding onto them. He attributed the downturn to factors like the U.S. tax deadline and Elon Musk's comments regarding Bitcoin's environmental impact and Tesla's acceptance of BTC payments. Novogratz predicted the market would consolidate and find a bottom between $36,000 and $38,000.

title: Baidu Awards Contract to Hesai for Customized Lidar Sensor That Will Power Its Self-Driving Cars
summary: Baidu has contracted Hesai Technology to develop a customized lidar sensor for its fifth-generation self-driving vehicles, aiming for mass production in Q3 this year. The new lidar will offer higher accuracy and a wider detection radius while costing nearly 50% less than current models. This initiative supports Baidu's plan to diversify revenue through robotaxi services and selling autonomous driving systems.

title: Tesla's bitcoin value dives; Musk signals hold with ‘diamond hands’ tweet
summary: Tesla's bitcoin holdings have sharply decreased in value to $1.26 billion, nearly matching its original purchase cost, following a cryptocurrency price plunge due to a Chinese government crackdown. Despite the financial dip and a 3% drop in Tesla's shares, CEO Elon Musk implied the company would not sell, using the "diamond hands" meme. This event highlights the volatility shareholders face from Tesla's cryptocurrency investments, especially with Musk's influential comments and regulatory actions impacting the market.

title: Crypto crash: Bitcoin, Ether, Dogecoin prices all nosedive
summary: Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin experienced significant price drops, with Bitcoin falling nearly 22% to $35,000, Ethereum sinking over 40%, and Dogecoin losing 45%. This nosedive follows weeks of warnings from critics about unsustainable crypto asset movements and was exacerbated by Elon Musk's social media posts and a statement from the People's Bank of China. The crash wiped out substantial market value and left many new entrants to the crypto market facing their first major selloff.

title: Ford’s electric F-150 pickup can power your home for 3 days. Should Houston oil and gas be worried?
summary: Ford unveiled its all-electric F-150 Lightning pickup truck, which starts at just under $40,000, offers a 230-mile range, and can power a home for three days during a blackout. This development is seen as a significant step in the energy transition, potentially impacting Houston's oil and gas industry, as electric vehicle adoption accelerates. Analysts predict EV prices will become competitive with gas-powered vehicles by 2023, with 280 million EVs on roads globally by 2040.

summary: Discussion thread among Tesla Motors Club members about a new Tesla Service Center opening in Madison, Wisconsin. Initial speculation was confirmed by a sales advisor, with details on location and opening timeframe. Later posts confirm signage is up and service appointments are starting.

summary: Tesla drivers are pushing the boundaries of the Autopilot system, with some users posting videos online demonstrating misuse like driving from the back seat. The article highlights the tension between Tesla CEO Elon Musk's promises of self-driving cars and the irresponsible actions of some owners.

summary: Nvidia Corp announced a four-for-one stock split to make its shares more affordable for investors, causing its stock to rise by 3%. This move follows similar splits by Apple and Tesla last year, with Nvidia's split requiring stockholder approval in June and effective mid-July.

title: Solid Power Goes Beyond Solid-State Cells: It’s An SSB Platform
summary: Solid Power's technology extends beyond just solid-state batteries, functioning as an "All-Solid-State Platform" compatible with various cathode materials, including current NMC 811. This platform promises significantly higher energy density (up to 560 Wh/kg) and allows for the use of low-cost, high-energy cathodes that could eliminate cobalt or nickel, potentially cutting cathode active material costs by 90 percent. Such advancements could lead to electric vehicles with double the range or significantly lighter battery packs.

title: S&P 500 ekes out a small gain in light trading, boosted by reopening plays
summary: U.S. stocks saw slight gains, with the S&P 500 climbing 0.2% driven by companies linked to economic reopening, such as Carnival and Royal Caribbean. Ford's increased investment in electric vehicles also boosted its shares, while Bitcoin's comeback contributed to positive risk sentiment. Trading was light ahead of the Memorial Day weekend, as investors also watched for developments on an infrastructure bill and major bank testimonies.

title: Deploying eTRUs Means Early Adopter Albertsons Reduces Emissions
summary: Albertsons is converting its transport refrigeration units (TRUs) to electric (eTRUs) at its Tracy, California distribution center, in partnership with Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E), to reduce emissions and save operating costs. This initiative is an early adoption of hybrid eTRU technology, which runs on electricity when plugged in and diesel on-road, aligning with future zero-emission mandates from the California Air Resources Board (CARB) and Governor Gavin Newsom. The project has resulted in projected annual savings of $62,000, a 77% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, and a 98% reduction in NOx emissions, serving as a model for other fleets transitioning to electric refrigeration.

title: China's EV maker Li Auto expects monthly sales to reach 10,000 cars in Sept
summary: Chinese electric vehicle maker Li Auto anticipates reaching monthly sales of 10,000 cars by September and plans to expand its sales network. The company, which currently offers one model, the Li ONE, aims to nearly double its April sales figures of 5,539 units. Li Auto also intends to invest 3 billion yuan in R&D this year and is exploring international markets and various fundraising options.

title: Ford boosts electrification spending, expects 40% of global sales to be EVs by 2030
summary: Ford is significantly increasing its investment in electrification, projected that 40% of its global sales will come from electric vehicles by 2030. This strategic shift highlights the company's commitment to transitioning towards an EV-dominated future within the automotive industry.

title: Ford's pitch to Wall Street: More aggressive EV push, new commercial vehicle business
summary: Ford Motor Co. announced a growth plan focused on electric vehicles, a new commercial vehicle business (Ford Pro), and digitally connected services. The company plans to invest over $30 billion in electrification by 2025 and expects 40% of its global vehicle volume to be fully electric by 2030. This strategy aims to shift Ford's business model to an "always-on" relationship with customers, generating new revenue streams beyond initial vehicle purchases.

title: Bitcoin and Ethereum are now, decentralized apps are the future
summary: Olaf Carlson-Wee, founder of Polychain Capital, believes decentralized web applications (DAOs) will be the next major trend in crypto, following the success of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and DeFi. He envisions decentralized versions of popular social media and chat apps owned by communities via crypto tokens, starting with simpler applications like photo hosting or messaging apps before moving to more complex platforms. Carlson-Wee also notes the rapid growth of decentralized exchanges (DEXes) like Uniswap, highlighting their collision course with regulators due to potential money laundering concerns.

title: Stock of the week - NVIDIA (27.05.2021)
summary: NVIDIA (NVDA.US) reported record first-quarter fiscal 2022 results, exceeding revenue and EPS expectations, driven by strong performance in Gaming, Data Center, and Professional Visualization platforms. The company also announced an upbeat Q2 forecast and a 4-for-1 stock split, which is seen as a bullish signal for investors. The growth is significantly boosted by the gaming sector during the pandemic and the increasing demand for its graphics cards by cryptocurrency miners.

title: Luxury Goods Sales Projected to Recover to 2019 Levels This Year
summary: A new report from Bain & Company projects global luxury goods sales to fully recover to 2019 levels this year, with a 30% probability of exceeding $340 billion. This optimistic forecast is driven by strong economic rebounds in China and the United States, propelled by swift vaccine distribution and increased disposable income. The article highlights the U.S. Global Investors' Global Luxury Goods Fund (USLUX) as an attractive way to capitalize on this recovery, benefiting from the spending habits of affluent consumers, particularly in Asia.

title: People Moves: Island Insurance Names Kuioka COO, The Liberty Company Insurance Brokers Adds Newman in California
summary: Island Insurance Co. has promoted Scott Kuioka to senior vice president and chief operating officer. Kuioka will also retain his roles as chief investment officer and chief risk officer, overseeing several key departments. Additionally, The Liberty Company Insurance Brokers appointed Lenny Newman as a vice president in their San Francisco Bay Area office, where he will specialize in trucking and lawyer’s professional liability.

title: Li Auto Admits Its Self-Driving Tech Is Sub-Par, and Its Stock Jumps
summary: Despite announcing a net loss and admitting its self-driving technology is inferior to competitors, Li Auto Inc.'s stock soared by 14.16% on Wednesday. The Chinese EV maker posted a 360 million yuan loss in Q1, reversing a previous profit, but its revenue more than trebled year-on-year. The strong investor response suggests continued belief in Li Auto's potential, even as it struggles with profitability and the global semiconductor shortage affecting its stock price alongside rivals like Nio and Xpeng.

title: Snowflake becomes latest tech company to leave Silicon Valley
summary: Cloud software company Snowflake has joined a growing list of tech firms departing Silicon Valley, announcing it no longer has a corporate headquarters and instead operates with a globally distributed workforce. While still maintaining a large office in Silicon Valley, the company designated its Bozeman, Montana office as its principal executive office due to its CEO and CFO being based there. This move reflects a broader trend among major tech companies to leave Silicon Valley, citing high costs, taxes, and perceived anti-business sentiment.

title: Despite What You’ve Heard, Not All Tech Products Are Manufactured Overseas
summary: While many tech products like phones and computers are built overseas, a significant number of tech items and components are manufactured in the United States, particularly in Texas. Companies like Apple, Ericsson, Samsung, Texas Instruments, and Starlink have production facilities in the state, involving semiconductors, computers, consumer electronics, home audio, and electric vehicles. Despite consumer preference for American-made goods, most are unwilling to pay more than a 10% premium for them.

title: Consumer Reports drops 'top pick' rating for Tesla Model 3
summary: Consumer Reports and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety have revoked top safety ratings for Tesla's Model 3 and Model Y vehicles following Tesla's decision to remove radar sensors in favor of a camera-based Autopilot system. The change impacts vehicles built after April 27 and may initially limit some features, though Tesla anticipates software updates will restore full functionality. Additionally, Tesla has introduced a camera-based driver monitoring system to address concerns about inattentiveness while Autopilot is engaged.

title: An ASX guide to Cathie Wood and ARK Invest ETFs
summary: This article provides an ASX guide to Cathie Wood and ARK Invest ETFs, explaining Wood's rise to fame, particularly through her bullish stance on Tesla, and the performance of ARK's flagship ARKK ETF. The piece also discusses the recent underperformance of ARK funds, attributing it to fears of inflation and rising bond yields, and speculates on the future prospects for ARK.

summary: The SEC reportedly admonished Elon Musk for violating the terms of his 2019 settlement agreement regarding his Tesla-related tweets. The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC was concerned about Musk's tweets in which he declared Tesla's stock price "too high" and discussed solar rooftop production figures without prior attorney approval. Despite confronting Musk and Tesla, the SEC did not file a motion to compel enforcement of the agreement.

title: Explainer: Tesla drops radar; is Autopilot system safe?
summary: Tesla has transitioned its Autopilot system to a camera-only approach, eliminating radar sensors, which raises concerns about safety and performance in various conditions. While Tesla CEO Elon Musk believes the vision-only system is safer due to less "noise" from radar, many in the industry and safety groups are skeptical, emphasizing the benefits of combining multiple sensor types, like cameras, radar, and lidar. Safety ratings bodies are re-evaluating their labels for newly configured Tesla vehicles.

title: A spotlight on Beam Global's profit model for EV charging
summary: Beam Global is implementing a unique, off-grid model for EV charging infrastructure that relies on corporate sponsorships for revenue rather than direct energy sales. This approach, piloted in San Diego, aims to make EV charging more accessible and resilient, bypassing traditional grid limitations and reducing deployment costs. The company seeks to expand nationally, driven by federal contracts and growing demand for sustainable transportation solutions.

title: G.M. will increase production of cars and trucks as the chip shortage eases. (Published 2021)
summary: General Motors announced plans to increase vehicle production and expects significantly better financial results for the first half of the year as the global semiconductor shortage begins to ease. The company will boost production of heavy-duty pickups and ship previously incomplete midsize pickups, indicating a recovery from the chip-related plant idlings earlier in the year. Other automakers like Ford and Tesla have also been impacted by the chip shortage.

title: Help for EV drivers stuck without a charge
summary: The article discusses solutions for electric vehicle drivers who find themselves stranded without power. It highlights portable chargers and truck-mounted units as ways to provide roadside assistance for EVs. Companies like Lightning eMotors and Blink are developing these mobile charging solutions.

title: AI for stock picking, and beyond
summary: Qraft Technologies, a Seoul-based financial technology startup, is gaining recognition for its AI-enhanced ETFs, which have shown success in stock picking, particularly by offloading Tesla shares before sharp declines. The company's AI solution utilizes deep learning modules to identify profitable patterns and extract investment strategies, leading to outperformance against benchmarks and attracting interest from Korean financial institutions. Qraft aims to further expand its AI applications within the finance industry, including active fixed-income and thematic ETFs, and personalized financial product recommendations.

title: Musk says Tesla cancels the longest-range Model S Plaid+
summary: Elon Musk announced via Twitter that Tesla has canceled the production of the longest-range Model S Plaid+. He stated there was "no need" for the Plaid+ as the standard Plaid model is "just so good." The Plaid+, originally intended to have a 520-mile range and utilize next-generation 4680 battery cells, had its production pushed back to 2022 before its cancellation.

title: Tesla Heavy Trucking Exec Jerome Guillen Departs
summary: Jerome Guillen, Tesla's president of heavy trucking and a key executive, has left the company after a decade. His departure is considered a significant loss by analysts, although Tesla stated that his contributions will remain. Guillen was instrumental in the Model S program and the ramp-up of Model 3 production, and his exit adds to a pattern of high-level executive turnover at Tesla.

title: Tilling AI: Startup Digs into Autonomous Electric Tractors for Organics
summary: Ztractor, founded by Bakur Kvezereli, is an autonomous electric tractor startup utilizing NVIDIA's Jetson edge AI platform to address labor shortages, pesticide issues, and energy costs in organic farming. The company offers tractors equipped with numerous sensors and cameras that collect data to improve crop conditions, increase yields, and enhance efficiency, positioning the agricultural machine industry for an "electric revolution" similar to the automotive sector. Ztractor's technology, which enables tasks like precision weeding and soil preparation, aims to make organic farming more competitive and sustainable.

title: Here are Tuesday's biggest analyst calls of the day: Netflix, Apple, AMC, Dave & Buster's & more
summary: This article summarizes major analyst calls made on Tuesday, June 8, 2021, featuring companies like Netflix, Apple, AMC, and Dave & Buster's. Notable reiterations include Bank of America on Amazon (buy) and MKM on AMC (sell), with analysts providing brief justifications for their ratings.

title: Tesla's China-made vehicle sales surge 29% in May - auto association
summary: Tesla Inc. sold 33,463 China-made electric cars in May, a 29% increase from April, according to the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA). China's new electric vehicle sales overall surged 177% in May. Tesla faces increasing competition and scrutiny in China regarding customer complaints and security concerns, leading the company to boost engagement with regulators and store data locally.

title: Apple in talks with Chinese suppliers for EV batteries: Report
summary: Apple is in early-stage discussions with Chinese battery suppliers CATL and BYD for its planned electric vehicle. A key condition from Apple is that potential suppliers build manufacturing facilities in the United States, but CATL is reportedly hesitant due to political tensions and cost concerns. The report also indicates Apple's interest in cheaper lithium iron phosphate batteries and targets a 2024 launch for its self-driving passenger vehicle.

title: The Secret IRS Files: Trove of Never-Before-Seen Records Reveal How the Wealthiest Avoid Income Tax
summary: ProPublica has obtained a vast cache of IRS data revealing how the wealthiest Americans, including Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, and Warren Buffett, legally pay minimal federal income taxes despite their immense wealth. The investigation highlights a "true tax rate" much lower than that of ordinary Americans, often achieved by leveraging asset growth, low salaries, and strategic borrowing. The findings challenge the fairness of the U.S. tax system and come amidst renewed calls for tax reforms targeting extreme wealth.

title: Samsung SDI mulls EV battery JV in US; partnership with global automaker
summary: Samsung SDI is considering launching an electric vehicle battery production joint venture in the US with a global automaker, following moves by its Korean rivals LG Energy Solution and SK Innovation. This strategic expansion aligns with President Biden's green energy policies and would solidify the presence of all three major Korean battery manufacturers in the US market. Potential partners for Samsung SDI include Stellantis and BMW, and the company is open to supplying other customers like Tesla.

title: Ferrari turns to chip firm for its new CEO as the industry looks to reinvent itself
summary: Ferrari has appointed Benedetto Vigna, head of STMicroelectronics' sensors group, as its new chief executive. This move is seen as highly unexpected given Vigna's background outside the automotive or luxury sectors, but reflects Ferrari's need to adapt to the electric vehicle era. Jefferies analyst Philippe Houchois suggests this appointment signals an intent to "reinvent" Ferrari amidst the industry's shift towards electric vehicles.

title: Electric vehicle stocks: the competition is heating up
summary: The electric vehicle (EV) industry is experiencing a boom with significant growth predicted for the coming years, driven by climate change concerns. While Tesla currently leads the market, competition is intensifying from traditional automakers like Volkswagen, General Motors, and Ford, as well as Chinese manufacturers and new EV start-ups. Investors are advised to take a diversified approach, potentially using thematic investment products, due to the high level of competition.

title: Elon Musk reveals Tesla's new car, the Model S Plaid
summary: Elon Musk unveiled the Tesla Model S Plaid, the company's fastest car to date, at an event in Fremont, California. Musk emphasized the car's role in promoting sustainable energy and highlighted its advanced entertainment system, comparing it to a PlayStation5.

title: 'This car crushes' Musk says, as Tesla launches faster Model S 'Plaid'
summary: Tesla launched a high-performance version of its Model S, dubbed 'Plaid', aiming to revitalize interest in the sedan and compete with luxury EV rivals. CEO Elon Musk emphasized the car's speed and safety, stating it's "faster than any Porsche, safer than any Volvo." The Model S Plaid features rapid acceleration, a longer range, and an enhanced entertainment system, though its launch coincided with a price increase and the cancellation of a higher-range variant.

title: How to speed up deep learning model training in the automotive sector
summary: This article discusses a solution developed by Run:AI, Microsoft, and NetApp to accelerate deep learning model training in the automotive sector, specifically for lane detection. summary: Elon Musk recently debuted the Tesla Model S Plaid, highlighting its "crazy fast" speed at a customer event held at the company's factory in Fremont, California. title: Next-Generation Dodge Muscle Car Rumored With Demon-Slaying Electric Powertrain
summary: Rumors suggest that the next-generation Dodge muscle car, replacing the Demon, could feature an electric powertrain. This shift is driven by increasing EV demand, impending bans on new ICE vehicles in Europe, and stricter CAFE standards. While no concrete evidence yet exists for a purely electric Demon successor, industry analysts believe plug-in hybridization, combining a supercharged V8 with an electric motor, is a plausible interim step.

title: All EV Roads Lead to Lithium Miners & Battery Producers
summary: The electric vehicle (EV) market's growth hinges on upstream lithium miners and battery producers, despite current attention on downstream OEMs. Historically low lithium prices have deterred production capacity expansion, potentially leading to supply bottlenecks as EV demand accelerates. Increased investment in lithium mining and battery manufacturing is crucial to prevent shortages and ensure global EV availability, with governments and companies recognizing this critical supply chain challenge.

title: Oh, So They Do Make Electric Trucks After All
summary: Oshkosh Defense, initially criticized for its supposed lack of EV experience after securing the USPS fleet contract, has demonstrated its capabilities by delivering its first electric fire truck and unveiling a new electric platform. This development suggests a brighter future for an all-electric Postal Service fleet, with Oshkosh leveraging decades of electrification experience. The article also highlights the potential for hydrogen fuel cell technology and the role of congressional funding in accelerating the electrification timeline.

title: Tesla chief Elon Musk tweets and Bitcoin jumps, again
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the company would resume accepting Bitcoin transactions once there is confirmation that Bitcoin miners use approximately 50 percent clean energy with a positive future trend. Following this tweet, Bitcoin's price surged nearly 10 percent. Musk's past statements and actions regarding Bitcoin have caused significant fluctuations in its value, leading to calls for regulatory investigation.

title: Understanding MSCI ESG Ratings: Definition, Methodology, and Examples
summary: MSCI ESG ratings provide a comprehensive measure of a company's commitment to socially responsible and ESG investment standards, evaluating resilience to long-term ESG risks. These ratings, ranging from AAA to CCC, assess environmental impact, social responsibility, and corporate governance. The article details MSCI's methodology, including data sources and scoring, and uses Tesla as a case study to illustrate how these ratings help investors understand a company's ESG performance.

title: Pony.ai Becomes First Company to Test Driverless Vehicles on Public Roads in Both the U.S. and China
summary: Pony.ai has become the first company to conduct daily fully driverless testing on public roads in both the U.S. (Fremont and Milpitas, CA) and China (Guangzhou). This milestone follows authorization from the California Department of Motor Vehicles for a fleet of six driverless vehicles. Pony.ai plans to resume its Robotaxi service to the public in Irvine, CA, in summer 2021 and roll out the fully driverless service to the public in 2022, while also contributing to COVID-19 relief efforts in both countries.

title: KraneShares Electric Vehicles & Future Mobility ETF (Ticker: KARS) Adopts Bloomberg Thematic Index
summary: Krane Funds Advisors, LLC announced that its KraneShares Electric Vehicles & Future Mobility ETF (KARS), with over $200 million in AUM, now tracks the Bloomberg Electric Vehicles Index. This makes KARS the first asset manager to track a Bloomberg thematic equity index. title: GM ups spending on EVs and autonomous vehicles by 30% to $35 billion by 2025 on higher profits
summary: General Motors announced a significant increase in spending on electric and autonomous vehicles, boosting its investment by 30% to $35 billion through 2025.
