title: G.M. will increase investment in electric vehicles by 30 percent and build more battery plants. (Published 2021)
summary: General Motors announced a significant acceleration in its electric vehicle plans, increasing investment to $35 billion by 2025 and projecting the construction of two more battery plants in the U.S. This strategic shift is a response to increasing EV adoption and competitive moves from rivals like Ford and Volkswagen, with GM aiming to sell one million EVs annually by 2025 and transition to an all-electric lineup by 2035. The company also reported an improved operating profit forecast for the first half of the year due to better chip supplies and strong demand.

title: Kia, Uber form electric mobility partnership in Europe
summary: Kia Corp. and Uber Technologies Inc. have partnered to boost electric vehicle adoption in Europe. Kia will offer its Niro crossovers and Kia Soul EVs to Uber drivers in 20 European markets through various financial deals. This collaboration aims to help Uber reach its goal of operating 100,000 EVs in Europe by 2025 and become a zero-emission mobility platform across the continent by 2030, aligning with Kia's "Plan S" strategy for eco-friendly vehicle sales.

title: Workhorse Group Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Workhorse Group Inc. (WKHS) stock dropped 3.02% to $14.45 on Thursday, underperforming the broader market. Despite the NASDAQ Composite Index rising, Workhorse's shares fell, closing significantly below its 52-week high. The company also underperformed against competitors like Tesla and Toyota, though it fared better than Ferrari.

title: Chinese startup Pony.ai to offer driverless robotaxi service by 2022 in California
summary: Chinese startup Pony.ai, which operates in both China and the United States, is testing its autonomous vehicles in California and Guangzhou with the goal of launching a fully driverless robotaxi service by 2022. The company, valued at $5.3 billion, is the eighth to receive authorization for driverless testing in California, working towards commercial operation permits. Pony.ai has secured over $1 billion in funding, including investment from Toyota, and has partnerships with major automakers and suppliers.

title: Toyota claims it’s too early to focus only on EVs
summary: Toyota reiterated its strategy that includes internal-combustion engines in hybrids, stating it's too early to exclusively focus on electric vehicles (EVs). Executive fellow Shigeki Terashi emphasized choice for consumers, while CTO Masahiko Maeda noted that current EV technologies aren't convenient for everyone. Toyota also highlighted its focus on the full lifecycle carbon emissions of EVs, including production and scrapping, and has advanced its carbon-neutral manufacturing goals to 2035.

title: Ford survey hints at specifics in F-150 Lightning package pricing
summary: Ford conducted a survey revealing potential pricing and package specifics for the F-150 Lightning, though these are not final. The survey results, shared on Reddit, suggest that Extended Range models will start near $80,000 before federal tax credits, with the Pro Extended version potentially being the best value. The article highlights the significant market excitement for the F-150 Lightning and its competitive landscape against Tesla's Cybertruck and Rivian's R1T.

title: 10 Most Popular Cars on YouTube
summary: New research by CarInsurance.ae reveals the 10 most popular car models on YouTube, with Tesla dominating the list despite not leading in sales volume. Tesla has four models included, securing the top spot with the Model 3, and demonstrating significant online conversation around the brand. Other manufacturers like Mazda, Lamborghini, Honda, Toyota, Audi, and BMW also feature in the rankings.

title: Ex-Tesla president sold stocks worth $274 million since June 10 -SEC filing
summary: Jerome Guillen, former Tesla executive and president, who left the company in early June, has sold approximately $274 million worth of shares through exercised stock options since June 10, according to an SEC filing. The sales, totaling 451,118 shares, have raised "eyebrows for investors," according to Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives, who advises watching for further sales. Guillen's departure, as one of Tesla's top four leaders, has reportedly triggered market concerns regarding future Tesla vehicle programs like the Semi trucks and 4680 cells.

title: Bill Gates Says Every Leader Should Read This Book This Summer
summary: Bill Gates recommends "Lights Out: Pride, Delusion, and the Fall of General Electric" as essential summer reading for leaders. The book, written by Wall Street Journal reporters, details GE's decline, offering cautionary lessons on leadership, particularly regarding the dangers of fixating on short-term profits. Gates emphasizes that focusing solely on quarterly earnings can lead to systemic weaknesses, contrasting GE's approach with companies like Amazon and Tesla that prioritized long-term growth over immediate analyst expectations.

title: GM Stock Value Drops 4 Percent During Week Of June 14 – June 18, 2021
summary: General Motors (GM) stock value decreased by 4.44 percent during the week of June 14-18, 2021, closing at $58.76 per share. This drop follows a three percent dip the previous week, despite earlier gains attributed to better-than-expected microchip shortage impact mitigation and the announcement of an all-electric Chevrolet Silverado pickup. Factors influencing the stock include continued microchip shortage issues, production cuts, and the company's aggressive pivot towards electric vehicles and autonomous driving technologies.

title: Sustainable equity ETFs cut Tesla, Microsoft, and Netflix
summary: Two of Australia's largest sustainable international equity ETFs, BetaShares Global Sustainability Leaders (ETHI) and VanEck Vectors MSCI International Sustainable Equity (ESGI), have divested from Tesla, Microsoft, and Netflix due to failures in ESG screens. These divestments highlight the active decisions passive sustainable funds can make based on rigorous environmental, social, and governance criteria, contrasting with Vanguard's Ethically Conscious International Shares ETF (VESG) which continues to hold these companies. The article examines the different screening methodologies used by these funds and their impact on holdings, performance, and diversification.

title: Tesla signs deal with new home builder to outfit whole community with solar, Powerwall, and chargers
summary: Tesla has partnered with new home builder Alset EHome to install solar panels, Powerwalls, and EV chargers in a new community near Houston, Texas. This agreement initially covers 20 homes, with plans to expand to 100 Ehome deliveries in 2021 and 650 more in the pipeline, aiming to establish Tesla's energy division in the new home market. Alset EHome emphasizes sustainability, integrating solar and energy storage into their homes, which they believe will serve as a model for the future of housing.

title: Electric Vehicles Will Dominate China's Automotive Market in 10 Years
summary: Electric vehicles are predicted to dominate China's automotive market within the next decade, with Chinese car brands aiming for significant market share. Executives from major Chinese electric car companies forecast that new energy vehicles will account for over 70% of new car sales by 2030. The KraneShares Electric Vehicles and Future Mobility Index ETF (KARS) is positioned to benefit from this growth, tracking companies involved in EV production and related technologies.

title: First of its kind $80 million graphite plant coming to Alexander City, hiring 100
summary: Alabama is set to become a national leader in graphite production with the establishment of a new $80 million advanced graphite processing plant in Alexander City, which will create 100 jobs. This facility, operated by Westwater Resources and Alabama Graphite, will be the first large-scale plant of its kind in the U.S., supplying a critical component for electric vehicle batteries. Governor Kay Ivey highlighted the project's importance for Alabama's auto manufacturing industry and national security, noting its environmentally friendly processing methods compared to current Chinese reliance.

title: Chipotle Launches Rewards Exchange With New Video Game And Tesla Model 3 Giveaway
summary: Chipotle announced the launch of its updated Rewards Exchange program, offering members more reward options beyond just free entrees. To celebrate, Chipotle introduced a new video game called "Chipotle Race to Rewards Exchange" on June 23, where players can win a 2021 Tesla Model 3 and other prizes. The game aims to showcase how quickly loyalty members can earn rewards under the new system, which includes points redeemable for free food items and donations to non-profit partners.

title: Chipotle Launches Rewards Exchange With New Video Game And Tesla Model 3 Giveaway
summary: Chipotle is celebrating the launch of its updated Rewards Exchange program, which now offers diverse redemption options beyond free entrees, by introducing a new video game called "Chipotle Race to Rewards Exchange." The game, live for 48 hours, challenges players to earn points for a chance to win a 2021 Tesla Model 3 and other prizes, while also allowing the first 500,000 daily players to earn points for free chips. This initiative aims to engage its nearly 23 million Rewards members and highlight the faster ways they can now earn rewards.

title: Arcimoto to Showcase Fun Utility Vehicle and Deliverator at 2021 Electric Mobility Symposium at Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in San Diego on June 24
summary: Arcimoto, in collaboration with TESIAC, Beam, and JuiceBar, will showcase its Fun Utility Vehicle (FUV) and Deliverator at the 2021 Electric Mobility Symposium at Marine Corps Air Station Miramar on June 24. This event aims to demonstrate future-proof, smart city, shared mobility options and infrastructure for both public and private sectors, including military bases. The partners will highlight how their combined technologies can create an efficient, affordable, and sustainable EV ecosystem, addressing challenges in EV adoption and the development of self-driving shared fleets.

title: GlobalFoundries to open new fab in Singapore
summary: GlobalFoundries is investing $4 billion to build a new semiconductor fabrication plant in Singapore, aiming to expand its manufacturing capacity amidst a global chip shortage. The facility, expected to roll out its first production wafers in Q1 2023, will create 1,000 high-value jobs and strengthen Singapore's position in advanced manufacturing. This expansion is designed to meet surging demand driven by 5G, IoT, and cloud computing.

title: Gov. Ivey: Westwater Resources Plans First U.S. Graphite Processing Plant in Alabama
summary: Governor Kay Ivey announced that Westwater Resources Inc. plans to build the first-of-its-kind advanced graphite processing plant in Coosa County, Alabama, with an initial investment of $80 million and subsequent $124 million to make Alabama a leader in graphite production. This facility will produce an essential material for batteries in electric vehicles and electronics, creating at least 100 full-time jobs and reducing U.S. dependence on foreign graphite sources, particularly from China. The project also includes significant state and local incentives, workforce development, and an environmentally sustainable processing method.

title: EVs Will Rule the World By 2040. Tesla Stock Isn't the Only Winner.
summary: Piper Sandler predicts that electric vehicles will dominate the global automotive industry by 2040, indicating a significant shift from internal combustion engines. This transition is expected to benefit not only Tesla but also other established automakers and EV startups. However, the article surprisingly suggests that Chinese EV companies like NIO might face challenges despite the overall growth in the EV market.

title: Tesla Unveils Top AV Training Supercomputer Powered by NVIDIA A100 GPUs
summary: Tesla has unveiled its in-house supercomputer, powered by 5,760 NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, to train deep neural networks for its Autopilot and self-driving capabilities. This system achieves an industry-leading 1.8 exaflops of performance, making it one of the top five supercomputers globally. The supercomputer is crucial for processing massive datasets from Tesla's fleet of over a million vehicles, allowing for continuous iteration and refinement of their autonomous driving AI.

title: Tesla tops American-made list. Can EV rivals catch up?
summary: A new report by Cars.com's American-Made Index shows that Tesla's vehicles, particularly the Model 3, top the list for having the most American parts, manufacturing, and labor, surpassing traditional automakers. This highlights the potential for electric vehicles to boast high domestic content and fuels the debate on the relationship between EVs and U.S. manufacturing. The findings come amid a push by major automakers to build battery plants in North America, signaling a potential shift towards more domestically sourced American auto fleets.

title: Con Edison to combine battery storage and EV chargers at same site in New York
summary: Con Edison has partnered with Centrica Business Solutions to develop an energy hub in Brooklyn, New York, combining 18 350kW EV chargers and a battery energy storage system (ESS). This project is claimed to be the first of its kind in New York City, aiming to provide affordable and abundant energy, especially during peak urban hours. The hub is expected to be fully installed by summer 2022, with Con Edison planning to share its findings to guide future charging infrastructure development.

title: 2021 Cars.com American-Made Index: Ranking by Class
summary: Cars.com's 2021 American-Made Index ranks 90 vehicles, providing a breakdown of the most American-made cars by class, including three-row SUVs, two-row SUVs, pickup trucks, sports cars, cars under $25,000, and electric/hybrid models. The article aims to assist shoppers interested in purchasing U.S.-made products by categorizing and listing vehicles based on their AMI ranking within specific segments. It highlights notable vehicles in each category and discusses the methodology for inclusion in the index, particularly for electrified models.

title: 2021 Cars.com American-Made Index: What About the Least American Cars?
summary: This article explores vehicles that rank low on Cars.com's 2021 American-Made Index, highlighting models with foreign assembly or low U.S./Canadian parts content. It reveals that nearly half of cars sold in America are assembled abroad and lists major automakers by their share of U.S. light-duty sales from domestic assembly, with Tesla at 100%. The piece aims to inform consumers about the origin of cars beyond just the American brands.

title: 2021 Cars.com American-Made Index: Which Cars Are the Most American?
summary: The 2021 Cars.com American-Made Index ranks 90 vehicles based on five criteria, with Tesla's Model 3 taking the top spot for the first time. The index highlights the top American-made cars, emphasizing criteria like assembly location, parts content, and U.S. manufacturing workforce, while also discussing the impact of factors like the chip shortage and trade pacts. The article also provides detailed methodology for the index, including disqualifiers and how various vehicle types are evaluated.

title: Virtual power plant coming to Maui and other islands
summary: A new virtual power plant project is launching on Maui, Oahu, and Hawaii island, utilizing solar-powered home batteries from 6,000 homeowners. Implemented by Swell Energy Inc. in partnership with Hawaiian Electric, the program aims to provide 25 megawatts of solar power and 80 MW of batteries, reducing energy bills for participants and supporting Hawaii's goal of 100 percent clean energy by 2045. The initiative was a major topic at the Hawaii Energy Conference, highlighting innovative solutions for a decentralized energy grid.

title: Tesla Model 3 Snags No. 1 Spot on Cars.com's 2021 American-Made Index®; First All-Electric Vehicle to Top the List in Its 16-Year History
summary: The Tesla Model 3 has become the first all-electric vehicle to top Cars.com's American-Made Index in its 16-year history, securing the No. 1 spot for 2021. This ranking, which also features the Tesla Model Y at No. 3, reflects increased consumer focus on buying American-made vehicles, with 72% of shoppers considering U.S. economic impact as a significant factor in their purchase decisions. The index, based on factors like assembly location, parts sourcing, and U.S. factory employment, also highlights strong showings from Ford, Jeep, Honda, Chevrolet, and Toyota.

title: WeRide raises $310M in Series C funding for autonomous vehicles
summary: WeRide, a Chinese developer of Level 4 autonomous vehicles, successfully raised $310 million in Series C funding, bringing its total funding in recent months to over $600 million and its valuation to $3.3 billion. The funding round saw participation from major entities including Alliance Ventures and China Structural Reform Fund, supporting WeRide's expansion of its robotaxi services in China and advancement of driverless technology. WeRide operates a robotaxi service in Guangzhou and aims to accelerate the commercialization of its driverless robotaxis and Mini Robobus.

title: T-REX 2X Long SpaceX Daily Target ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:SPAX)
summary: The T-REX 2X Long SpaceX Daily Target ETF (SPAX) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests primarily in small-cap US-listed SPACs. Launched on June 22, 2021, and managed by Robinson, the ETF aims to capture price spikes in its holdings. As of August 7, 2026, SPAX was trading at $8.39, representing a significant decrease from its year-start price of $20.2750.

title: Volvo plans to add lidar as standard equipment in electric XC90 SUV next year
summary: Volvo Cars announced plans to make lidar sensors standard equipment in its electric XC90 SUV starting next year, a strategic move to enhance safety and autonomous driving. This decision positions Volvo differently from rivals like Tesla, which rely solely on cameras. Luminar Technologies Inc. will supply the Iris lidar and Sentinel software for this integration.

title: Honda’s First Electric Crossover, The GM-Built Prologue, Arrives In 2024
summary: Honda is set to introduce its first electric crossover, the GM-built Prologue, in early 2024, marking a significant shift towards electrification. This collaboration with General Motors will utilize GM's Ultium electric platform, with Honda designing the body, interior, and chassis tuning. While Honda plans to eventually launch its own e:Architecture-based EVs and research solid-state batteries, it will first ramp up its hybrid offerings, aiming for a substantial increase in hybrid sales before a full transition to zero-emission vehicles by 2040 in North America.

title: Chinese EV battery maker CATL extends deal with Tesla
summary: Chinese electric vehicle battery manufacturer CATL has announced the extension of its battery supply agreement with Tesla Inc until December 2025. CATL will continue to supply battery cells to Tesla for its Model 3 sedans and Model Y SUVs produced in Shanghai. This deal solidifies CATL's position as a key supplier alongside Panasonic Corp and LG Energy Solution for Tesla.

title: Breaking Down 'BLOK': Inside This ETF's Portfolio
summary: The Amplify Transformational Data Sharing ETF (BLOK) demonstrated its active management prowess by capitalizing on crypto market volatility in May, mitigating losses despite its high correlation to Bitcoin. BLOK strategically narrowed its holdings and increased exposure to digital platforms and exchanges, which typically thrive during periods of extreme market fluctuations. The ETF, with over $1 billion in AUM, focuses 80% of its portfolio on companies involved in blockchain technology but does not directly invest in cryptocurrencies.

title: Autonomous vehicles hit fast lane in China
summary: Autonomous vehicle technology is rapidly advancing in China, with major investments from tech companies and carmakers. Companies like Baidu's Apollo and Pony.ai are already deploying robotaxis in cities, and SAIC plans to follow suit. While development and testing are costly, investor optimism and strategic partnerships are helping to reduce costs and accelerate commercialization, with a focus on L4 autonomous functions in the near future.

title: Builder Alset EHome Partners With Tesla to Construct Community of Ehomes
summary: Alset EHome, a property developer, has partnered with Tesla to install solar panels, Powerwalls, and EV chargers in 20 new homes in the Northpark community in Porter, Texas, with plans for more. This collaboration aims to create a sustainable housing ecosystem, including a Tesla vehicle with each Ehome, and expand to over 5,000 Ehomes in the next three to five years. The initiative supports a vision of communities built on sustainable carbon footprints and clean energy.

title: Sunrise brief: Arevon opens 100 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage facility in California
summary: Arevon Asset Management has opened a 100 MW/400 MWh Saticoy battery energy storage system in Ventura County, California, acquired in partnership with Capital Dynamics and S&B USA Energy. The article also touches on other significant developments in the renewable energy sector, including Partners Group taking a stake in Dimension Renewable Energy, Koch unit investing in Lithion Battery, and Canadian Solar winning an 86 MW solar energy auction in Japan. Additionally, AltaSea plans a 2.2 MW solar array at the Port of Los Angeles, and Captona expands its fuel cell portfolio.

title: Chinese EV Maker Xpeng to raise $1.8 bln in Hong Kong listing
summary: Chinese smart electric vehicle maker Xpeng Inc. plans to raise $1.8 billion through a dual primary listing in Hong Kong. The company will sell 85 million shares at HK$165 each to fund expansion of its product line-up and development of advanced smart car technologies, including autonomous driving. Xpeng, which competes with Tesla and Nio in China, chose a dual primary listing to allow qualified Chinese investors to participate.

title: Tech ETFs: 3 Top Alternatives to Cathie Wood's ARKK
summary: This article identifies three top tech ETFs as alternatives to Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), which has experienced significant volatility. The recommended ETFs are the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT), SPDR S&P Software & Services ETF (XSW), and iShares Evolved U.S. Technology ETF (IETC), highlighting their strong returns and varying expense ratios. It details their performance, expense ratios, and key holdings, presenting them as well-managed options for investors seeking exposure to technology stocks.

title: Thermal cameras are the new eyes for automated driving features
summary: Thermal cameras are being developed to improve the ability of automated driving systems to detect pedestrians, especially at night or in adverse conditions, where current radar and visible camera systems are often ineffective. Teledyne FLIR Systems' "blended thermal/visible technology" can detect humans and animals based on heat energy, addressing a critical blind spot in current safety features. This sensor fusion promises to enhance pedestrian safety and the overall perception capabilities of future cars.

title: Advisor Ross Gerber Launches Active 'Roaring '20s' ETF
summary: Advisor Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management, has launched an actively managed ETF called the AdvisorShares Gerber Kawasaki ETF (GK). This new ETF will focus on nine investment themes Gerber believes will thrive in the post-COVID economy, offering investors access to his stock-picking expertise in a tax-efficient structure. Gerber emphasizes that the ETF is designed as a core growth fund for long-term investors, not a "get-rich-quick" scheme, and aims to provide a smoother ride than more volatile single-theme funds.

title: Tesla top-of-range car caught fire while owner was driving, lawyer says
summary: A recently delivered Tesla Model S Plaid reportedly burst into flames while its owner was driving, with the electronic door system failing, according to the driver's lawyer. The incident, involving a $129,900 car delivered just three days prior, has prompted an investigation and a call to ground the Model S Plaid until the cause is determined. Tesla had no immediate comment, while the NHTSA is gathering information about the incident.

title: GM forms strategic investment for U.S.-sourced lithium as part of EV push
summary: General Motors announced a strategic investment in Controlled Thermal Resources Limited to secure U.S.-sourced lithium from southern California's Salton Sea. This move aims to establish a domestic supply chain for crucial EV battery minerals, reducing dependence on foreign sources like China, and is part of GM's broader electrification strategy to make future EVs more affordable and increase their range. This investment highlights the automaker's commitment to its $35 billion EV and autonomous technology development budget through 2025.

title: General Motors invests in company extracting lithium from the Salton Sea
summary: General Motors has invested a multimillion-dollar sum in Controlled Thermal Resources (CTR), a company focused on extracting lithium from the Salton Sea. This investment is crucial for GM's goal of selling only zero-emissions vehicles by 2035, as lithium is a key component for EV batteries. The Salton Sea is believed to hold a significant portion of the global lithium supply, and CTR's direct extraction method is touted as more environmentally friendly than traditional mining.

title: Tesla’s Lidar Flirtation Is More Proof That Microvision Has Potential
summary: This article discusses Microvision's potential in the lidar technology market, especially in light of Tesla's apparent reconsideration of lidar for its autonomous vehicles. Despite Microvision being a former penny stock with limited revenue, author Louis Navellier believes its long-range lidar solution positions it for significant growth if adopted by the auto industry. The piece highlights Tesla's previous dismissal of lidar and its recent exploration of the technology, which could boost lidar-related stocks like MVIS.

title: Air intake filter - yes or no?
summary: Tesla Model 3 owners discuss the pros and cons of adding aftermarket air intake filters under the hood. While some users find them helpful for keeping debris out of the cabin filter, others report significant airflow restriction and potential issues with mold growth. Many contributors explore alternatives like screens or modified filters to minimize airflow reduction.

title: Pallinghurst makes billion-dollar bet on Quebec as global battery hub
summary: European private equity investor Pallinghurst Group is making a billion-dollar bet on Quebec becoming a key global battery hub, investing over US$500-million in projects like Nemaska Lithium Inc. and Nouveau Monde Graphite. This investment supports Quebec's ambitious vision to establish a lithium-ion battery industry, leveraging its carbon-free hydropower despite past challenges in the sector. Pallinghurst's co-managing partner, Arne Frandsen, emphasizes the province's political willingness, strong rule of law, and cheap clean energy as critical factors for their commitment.

title: Qraft’s AI-Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Momentum ETF Surpasses $50M in AUM
summary: Qraft AI ETFs announced that its AI-Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Momentum ETF (AMOM) has exceeded $50 million in assets under management, demonstrating nearly 1,500% growth since August 2020. The fund leverages AI technology to identify high alpha factors and optimize its strategy, leading to consistent outperformance against its benchmark. This milestone highlights the increasing investor interest in AI-driven fund management amidst market volatility.

title: REE Automotive, a leader in electric vehicle technology, and 10X Captal to join forces
summary: REE Automotive, a company specializing in zero-emissions electric mobility, announced its plan to merge with 10X Capital, a special purpose acquisition company. This business combination will lead to REE Class A ordinary shares and warrants being listed on NASDAQ under "REE" and "REEAW" respectively. The merger aims to accelerate the development and market introduction of REE's REEcorner technology and modular EV platforms, with deliveries expected to begin in 2022 and production ramping up in 2023.

title: Lendesk Launches Innovative Tool Enabling Mortgage Brokers to Submit Applications Directly to Lenders and Win Tesla Model 3
summary: Lendesk Technologies, a part of Rocket Companies, has launched Lender Connect, an innovative tool within its Finmo platform that allows mortgage brokers to submit applications directly to over 240 lenders. This new feature streamlines the mortgage process by including automated compliance checks and integrating with Lender Spotlight to match clients with the best loan products. To celebrate the launch, Lendesk is offering brokers who use Lender Connect an entry to win a Tesla Model 3 and free tax documents until September 10.

title: Chinese EV maker Xpeng shares close flat in HK debut as it eyes global rollout
summary: Chinese electric vehicle maker Xpeng Inc. closed flat at its $1.8 billion Hong Kong dual primary listing, with shares ending at HK$165, in line with the listing price, after an initial rise. The company announced plans to develop future models on a new product platform designed for international markets, aiming to roll it out within two years. Despite the flat debut, an analyst mentioned the debut "looks a little weak" due to broader market conditions, suggesting a potential slowdown in capital extraction rates seen in prior years.

title: Tesla Hates Lidar. This Tesla Lover Loves It.
summary: Despite Tesla CEO Elon Musk's disdain for lidar technology, a noted Tesla bull from New Street Research has issued a Buy rating for lidar stock Aeva Technologies. This development highlights increasing bullish sentiment on Wall Street for lidar, a technology considered crucial for self-driving cars, even as lidar stocks have recently faced challenges.

title: Whatever Happened To European Corporate Competitors?
summary: This article examines the decline of European corporate giants on the global stage compared to American and Asian firms. It highlights how Apple's market cap dwarfs entire European stock indices and notes that no European firm has been in the global top ten since 2015. The author attributes this decline to Europe's risk-averse business culture, lack of innovation in digital tech, and less integrated market, despite similar GDP growth to the US.

title: Chinese EV Maker XPeng Makes Debut in Hong Kong
summary: Chinese EV maker XPeng debuted on the Hong Kong stock exchange, raising $1.8 billion with a dual-primary listing. This move brings the company closer to Chinese investors and provides insurance against potential delisting from U.S. markets due to stricter audit regulations. The dual-primary listing allows XPeng to maintain trading independent of its U.S. status and makes it eligible for the Stock Connect program.

title: Chip Shortage Pushes China Auto Sales Down 12% in June
summary: China's auto sales dropped by 12.4% in June compared to the previous year, primarily due to the global semiconductor shortage impacting auto production. Despite the decline, overall sales for the first half of the year were up 25.6%, and new energy vehicle (NEV) sales saw significant growth, jumping 139%. Automakers like Nio, Xpeng, and BYD are expanding NEV manufacturing as the government promotes greener vehicles.

title: Ford drops use of 'chairman' title, adopts other gender-neutral language
summary: Ford Motor Company has officially replaced the title "chairman" with "chair" and adopted other gender-neutral language in its bylaws, effective July 8. General Motors also made a similar change in May, adjusting Mary Barra's title from chairman and CEO to chair and CEO. This move reflects a broader trend among major corporations and institutions to promote inclusivity and adapt to changing societal norms.

title: The race for renewable energy is just getting started
summary: The article discusses the accelerating shift towards renewable energy, highlighting global investments exceeding $500 billion in 2020. Authored by Gregg Guerin of First Trust, it explores five key drivers including declining costs, investment shifts, government support, smart grid infrastructure, and low-carbon policies. The piece also delves into investment opportunities in EVs, energy storage, and the potential of green hydrogen as a future energy source.

title: Is Nvidia Stock A Buy Now Before Its Stock Split? (NASDAQ:NVDA)
summary: NVIDIA has announced a stock split effective July 20, which historically can lead to short-term price movements. While growth and valuation are long-term drivers, NVIDIA is well-positioned for future growth but its shares are currently historically expensive. The article explores whether NVIDIA is a buy before its upcoming stock split, considering both its growth prospects and current valuation.

title: Tesla setting up ‘solar neighbourhood’ in 10,000 home Texas residential development
summary: Tesla Energy is partnering with Brookfield Asset Management and Dacra to equip a new 10,000-home development in Austin, Texas, called Easton Park, with its V3 solar roof tiles and Powerwall 2 residential battery storage systems. This "solar neighbourhood," provisionally named SunHouse, aims to cover daily energy needs, reduce grid demand, and provide backup power, while offering Tesla an opportunity to scale installations of its solar roof technology. The project addresses growing demand for energy security and sustainability, especially in Texas, which experienced a severe energy crisis earlier in the year.

title: Musk tells SolarCity trial that Tesla would 'die' if he wasn't CEO
summary: During a trial concerning Tesla's 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, Elon Musk testified that Tesla would "die" if he wasn't CEO, despite asserting the board controls the company. The lawsuit alleges Musk strong-armed the board into the $2.6 billion deal for SolarCity, founded by his cousins, to bail out his investment. Musk denied financial gain from the merger, stating it aimed to combine Tesla's battery business with SolarCity's energy generation.

title: Elon Musk spars with attorney during Tesla-SolarCity trial
summary: Elon Musk concluded his testimony in the trial concerning Tesla's 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, maintaining his composure despite combative questioning from the plaintiffs' lawyer. Investors and pension funds allege that Musk and Tesla's board breached their fiduciary duties in the $2 billion buyout of the struggling solar provider. Musk, who was the chairman and largest shareholder of both companies, is the sole defendant in the trial.

title: Qraft's AI-powered ETFs wow Wall Street with winning stock picks
summary: Qraft Technologies, a South Korea-based fintech startup, has gained Wall Street's attention with its AI-powered exchange-traded funds (ETFs) listed on the NYSE. These AI-enhanced ETFs, QRTF and AMOM, have delivered favorable returns by using AI to forecast stock movements and adapt to market conditions. Notably, the AMOM ETF divested all its Tesla stocks before a market dip, highlighting the AI's predictive capabilities and attracting significant investment.

title: Wednesday's Top Analyst Upgrades and Downgrades: Carnival, Conagra, Duke Energy, Estee Lauder, Gap, Lululemon, Tesla and More
summary: This article details a list of top analyst upgrades and downgrades for various companies on Wednesday, July 14, 2021, providing insights into stock performance and price targets. It also briefly discusses the broader market context, including inflation data and investors' reactions to second-quarter earnings. Companies mentioned include Carnival, Conagra, Duke Energy, Estee Lauder, Gap, Lululemon, and Tesla.

title: Why is Tesla incorporated in Delaware?
summary: This article explains why a disproportionate number of companies, including Tesla, Amazon, and Google, are incorporated in Delaware despite not being headquartered there. Key reasons include flexible corporate law, the efficient Court of Chancery, favorable tax treatment for out-of-state income, and a long-standing state focus on business formation. The article also touches on the challenges this presents for regional data and business coverage.

title: Tesla's Elon Musk admits Cybertruck could be a 'flop'
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has acknowledged that the Cybertruck, despite his personal affection for its design, could potentially "flop" because of its unconventional nature. Musk made this admission in response to an opinion piece suggesting the vehicle might miss sales expectations. Tesla plans to begin volume production of the Cybertruck in 2022, with a base price of $39,900.

title: Rivian delays much-hyped electric bakkie
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc. is delaying the production of its electric pickup truck, the R1T, by two months to September, and its electric SUV, the R1S, from August to an unspecified time in the fall. These delays are primarily due to supply-chain bottlenecks, particularly a semiconductor shortage, which has broadly impacted the automotive industry. CEO R.J. Scaringe noted the compounding effects of the pandemic on facility construction, equipment installation, and component supply.

title: Tesla Launches Full Self-Driving Subscription
summary: Tesla has introduced a subscription service for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature, which is a Level 2 semi-autonomous system. The subscription costs $199 per month for cars with Basic Autopilot and $99 per month for those with Enhanced Autopilot, though some vehicles may require a hardware upgrade for an additional $1,500. Tesla emphasizes that FSD is not yet fully autonomous and requires an attentive driver.

title: Chinese electric carmaker Xpeng prices its new sedan at $24,700 undercutting Tesla
summary: Chinese electric carmaker Xpeng has priced its new P5 sedan as low as 160,000 yuan ($24,694), aggressively undercutting Tesla's Model 3 in China. The P5 is Xpeng's third production model and features Lidar technology for semi-autonomous driving. This move comes amid increasing competition in China's burgeoning electric vehicle market, with Xpeng aiming to boost sales in a new price segment.

title: General Motors CEO Mary Barra is steering the way to an all-electric future
summary: General Motors CEO Mary Barra is spearheading the company's transition to an all-electric future by aiming to exclusively offer EVs and end production of fossil fuel vehicles by 2035. Under her leadership, GM plans to introduce 30 new EVs by 2025 with a US$35 billion investment, showcasing a strong commitment to combating climate change and transforming the automotive industry. Barra's vision also emphasizes diversity, accountability, and an agile culture within GM to achieve these ambitious environmental and business goals.

title: Moderna Joins Top S&P 500 Firms as Stock Value Triples
summary: Moderna Inc. has joined the S&P 500 index, marking its transformation into a major vaccine maker. Its stock has surged over 207% in 2021, making it the best-performing stock in the S&P 500 by a significant margin. This move comes as the company continues to supply Covid-19 vaccines globally.

title: Bitcoin surges past $32,000 after Elon Musk says he owns the coin
summary: Bitcoin experienced a resurgence, climbing past $32,000 after Elon Musk confirmed his ownership of the cryptocurrency, along with Dogecoin and Ethereum, during a conference. This rebound occurred despite recent declines and increased regulatory scrutiny, with analysts suggesting that a sustained move above $32,000 is crucial for a stronger recovery. The article discusses the reasons behind its volatility and expert opinions on its future trajectory.

title: Tesla signs deal with world’s largest nickel miner to secure resource for battery production
summary: Tesla has partnered with BHP, the world's largest nickel miner, to secure a supply of nickel for its battery production, addressing the surging demand for raw materials in electric vehicle manufacturing. The agreement also includes collaboration on sustainable battery supply chain logistics using blockchain technology and explores the use of Tesla's energy storage products by BHP. This move supports Tesla's efforts to ramp up its own battery cell production and secure necessary resources for its expanding EV market.

title: CarMax On Used-Car Buying Spree As Market Madness Continues
summary: Amidst skyrocketing used-car prices and a new-car chip shortage, CarMax is aggressively buying used vehicles, increasing purchases by 236% this year. This strategy allows them to maintain inventory and charge a premium while competitors face barren lots. The article suggests high prices for both new and used cars could persist due to continued chip shortages, cheap financing, and strong trade-in values.

title: Plug Power recruits Tesla executive to oversee manufacturing
summary: Plug Power has hired David Mindnich, a former Tesla senior director of operations, to lead its global manufacturing as the company prepares to significantly expand its manufacturing workforce. This strategic recruitment aims to oversee the growth of its fuel cell and electrolyzer production capabilities. The company plans to increase its manufacturing employees from 450 to over 1,000 within the next two years.

title: Here Comes Ticker Change: Lucid Motors Will Officially Become Lucid Group (LCID) Next Week
summary: Lucid Motors will officially become Lucid Group (LCID) next week following the approval of its merger agreement with Churchill Capital Corp. IV (CCIV). This development clears the path for LCID shares to list on NASDAQ and for deliveries of the Lucid Air EV to commence in a matter of weeks, addressing earlier investor concerns about share dilution. The company plans aggressive expansion, including a new SUV and increased manufacturing capacity, aiming for significant sales in the luxury EV market.

title: It's Looking Like a Fine Time to Consider Covered Call ETFs
summary: The article suggests that covered call ETFs, specifically the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call ETF (QYLD), are an attractive investment option for income-focused investors, especially given potential market volatility. QYLD offers a substantial yield by selling covered calls on Nasdaq-100 components and can provide monthly income. While covered call strategies may underperform in rapidly rising markets, they tend to outperform in flat, down, or slightly up markets, making QYLD a credible long-term income alternative.

title: It's Looking Like a Fine Time to Consider Covered Call ETFs
summary: The article discusses the increasing appeal of covered call ETFs, such as the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call ETF (QYLD), for income-starved investors amidst market volatility. QYLD offers a substantial yield and provides monthly income, making it an attractive option for long-term investors looking for alternative income streams in various market conditions. Analysts suggest covered call strategies tend to outperform outright stock ownership in flat, down, and slightly up markets.

title: Faraday Future promises FF 91 electric crossover by next year
summary: Faraday Future, after years of financial struggles and unfulfilled promises, has secured nearly $1 billion in funding through a SPAC merger and is now listed on NASDAQ as FFIE. The company promises to deliver its FF 91 electric crossover in 2022, with two versions available for reservation, including a limited $180,000 Futurist Alliance Edition. Despite past setbacks, Faraday Future has ambitious production targets for future models, aiming for over 300,000 vehicles by 2025.

title: Musk says India plant likely if Tesla succeeds in importing cars there
summary: Elon Musk stated that a Tesla manufacturing plant in India would likely be established if the company successfully navigates the process of importing its cars into the country. This suggests that the establishment of a production facility hinges on an initial period of market entry through imports. The move could open up the Indian market for Tesla and potentially lead to local manufacturing.

title: XPeng builds technology subsidiary in Hainan province
summary: XPeng Inc. has established a new technology subsidiary in Hainan province, Hainan Xiaopeng Motors Technology Co.,Ltd., with a registered capital of 20 million yuan. This entity will focus on AI-based application software development, pre-owned vehicle brokerage, and sales of new cars and charging piles. This move follows XPeng's establishment of two sales service subsidiaries in Hainan earlier in 2021 and aligns with its expansion strategy as a key rival to Tesla in the Chinese market.

title: Lucid Motors stock pops in debut, CEO’s goal is affordable electric vehicles
summary: Lucid Motors debuted on the Nasdaq after completing its reverse merger, with its stock rising 10.6% on its first day of trading. CEO Peter Rawlinson expressed his goal to make electric vehicles, including the entry-level Pure Air, more affordable by aiming for a price point around $70,000. Rawlinson, a former chief engineer for Tesla's Model S, plans to expand Lucid's factory in Arizona to add a line for its Project Gravity electric SUV.

title: Lucid Motors Shares Rise 11% in First Trading Day After SPAC Merger
summary: Lucid Group's shares rose 11% on its first trading day after completing a SPAC merger. The electric-vehicle startup, which plans to begin production later this year, closed at $26.83. This development marks Lucid as the latest EV company to go public via a blank-check merger.

title: Tysons Corner Center proposes using parking spaces for auto sales
summary: Tysons Corner Center is proposing to use existing parking spaces for vehicle sales, catering to the evolving automotive industry, particularly electric vehicles. Property owner Macerich has submitted applications to Fairfax County seeking approval to designate up to 240 parking spots for up to eight tenants, allowing vehicle sales from retail showrooms. This move aims to help the mall remain viable and adapt to market changes, as EV manufacturers like Tesla and Lucid operate with smaller showrooms and direct customer sales, reducing the need for large on-site vehicle inventories.

title: Amazon denies accepting Bitcoin, sends it tumbling
summary: Amazon.com Inc denied a media report suggesting it would accept Bitcoin payments by year-end, causing the cryptocurrency to tumble below $37,000. Earlier speculation, fueled by a job posting for a digital currency lead, had driven Bitcoin past $40,000. The company stated that while interested in the space, the specific plans for cryptocurrencies were not true.

title: Chinese EV makers plunge as investors watch Beijing's regulatory squeeze tighten across industries
summary: Chinese electric vehicle makers Nio, Xpeng, Li Auto, and Niu Technologies saw their stock prices plunge on Tuesday due to investor concerns over Beijing's intensifying regulatory crackdown across various industries. While no new regulations were specifically directed at EV makers, the sell-off is part of a broader trend affecting US-listed Chinese stocks. This regulatory scrutiny began with the cancellation of Ant Group's IPO and has since impacted tech and education sectors, wiping out significant market value.

title: Joby Completes Flight of More Than 150 Miles with Electric Vertical Take-Off Air Taxi
summary: Joby Aero Inc. successfully completed a 150-mile flight on a single charge with its full-size electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) prototype, including vertical take-off and landing. This milestone demonstrates the viability of current battery technology for convenient, emissions-free air travel, with commercial passenger service anticipated to start in 2024. The flight lasted over an hour, covering 154.6 statute miles and validating the efficiency of their aircraft design and battery system.

title: Tesla to shift retail strategy, report says
summary: Tesla is reportedly planning to change its retail strategy. The article, published on July 28, 2021, indicates a shift in how the automaker will handle its physical retail locations.

title: Big investors are divesting from fossil fuels – should you?
summary: The article explores the dilemma for Australian investors regarding fossil fuels: whether to invest in undervalued energy names or join the growing trend of divestment. It presents arguments from both "bulls" who see continued demand from Asian markets and "bears" who warn of stranded assets due to renewable energy advancements and tightening regulations. The piece discusses the potential for energy companies to transition to green futures and the financial risks involved for investors.

title: 💡 Optimist's Edge: Big batteries are the missing piece of the energy puzzle
summary: This article argues that large battery storage is an integral and increasingly vital part of our energy system, countering initial skepticism from figures like former Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison. It highlights the successful implementation of Tesla's Hornsdale Power Reserve in South Australia, demonstrating how big batteries prevent blackouts, save consumers money, and balance the grid. The article also discusses the rapid decline in battery costs and the significant investment opportunities in this sector.

title: Tesla hikes electric car prices in U.S.; holds line in China
summary: Tesla is implementing divergent strategies in the U.S. and Chinese automotive markets. In the U.S., Tesla has raised prices multiple times for its Model 3 and Model Y to boost profit margins, while in China, it has maintained stable pricing and introduced more affordable options to drive sales amidst intense local competition. The company's U.S. price hikes contributed to record quarterly profits, but its market share in China has slipped due to competition and regulatory pressures.

title: Saudi-backed Tesla electric car rival Lucid completes Nasdaq listing
summary: Lucid Motors has successfully completed its Nasdaq listing, merging with Churchill Capital Corp IV to become Lucid Group, Inc. and trading under the ticker "LCID." The transaction brought in $4.4 billion, which the company plans to use for accelerating growth and increasing manufacturing capacity. Lucid has over 11,000 paid reservations for its luxury electric vehicle, the Lucid Air, and expects to begin deliveries in the second half of 2021.

title: Russo and Steele Collector Automobile Auctions partners with USA Today Network Ventures
summary: USA TODAY NETWORK Ventures has partnered with Arizona-based Russo and Steele Collector Automobile Auctions to offer premier automobile collector auction events. This collaboration will expand Russo and Steele's reach to enthusiasts and enable USA TODAY NETWORK Ventures to enter the automobile event industry. The partnership will kick off at Monterey Collector Car Week in California and include events in Scottsdale, Arizona, and Amelia Island, Florida.

title: BHP enters into nickel supply agreement with Tesla Inc
summary: BHP has signed a nickel supply agreement with Tesla Inc., providing nickel from its Western Australian Nickel West asset, which is noted for its sustainability and low carbon emissions. This partnership aims to support the growing demand for electric vehicles and collaborate on making the battery supply chain more sustainable, including using blockchain for raw material traceability and exploring energy storage solutions to reduce carbon emissions. Both companies will also work together on promoting sustainability within the resources sector and aligning with partners who share their principles.

title: Apple Is Now an Antifragile Company
summary: This article argues that Apple has transformed into an "antifragile" company under Tim Cook's leadership, meaning it improves under stress rather than just resisting it. The company's resilience stems from its robust supply chain management, significant cash reserves, and diversified product and service portfolio, which allowed it to thrive amidst the challenges of 2020. While potential threats like government regulation, future leadership changes, and geopolitical issues remain, Apple's recent performance suggests a strong footing for continued success.

title: Nio delivered fewer cars than Xpeng and Li Auto did in July
summary: In July, Chinese EV start-up Nio delivered fewer vehicles than its rivals, Xpeng and Li Auto. Li Auto led with a record 8,589 deliveries of its Li One SUVs, followed by Xpeng with 8,040 vehicles. Nio reported 7,931 deliveries for the month, although its year-to-date total still surpasses those of its two competitors.

title: Why all roads of industry lead to purposeful innovation and a platform economy
summary: The article discusses how the platform economy is transforming various industries, enabling faster innovation, increased collaboration, and better customer service. It highlights how companies adopting a platform mindset can overcome traditional business model inefficiencies and leverage interconnected tools, especially in sectors like AEC. The piece emphasizes the creation of value through compelling platform capabilities and the strategic decision of either building one's own platform or integrating with existing ones, citing examples like Tesla and Netflix.

title: Chad Blair: Honolulu Appears Overrun With Teslas. That's Good News For EVs
summary: The article discusses the increasing presence of Teslas in Honolulu, highlighting their growing market share among luxury cars and their potential contribution to Hawaii's 100% clean-energy goal by 2045. It acknowledges the debate surrounding Tesla and its CEO Elon Musk, from their success in EV sales to criticisms regarding safety and business practices. The author also touches upon Hawaii's efforts to electrify state fleets and the broader trend towards electric vehicles among major automakers.

title: Roanoke’s Major Player in U.S. Electrical Power Industry Celebrates Half Century of Service
summary: Roanoke-based Virginia Transformer Corporation (VTC) celebrated its 50th anniversary, marking its growth from a small power transformer producer to the largest U.S.-based power transformer OEM. CEO Prabhat K. Jain announced two new corporate initiatives: an employee financial aid fund and a scholarship award for employees' children, aimed at attracting and retaining talent. VTC, an American-owned, Minority Business Enterprise, has supplied transformers for major clients like Tesla, NASA, and Walt Disney, and continues to be a key player in updating the U.S.'s aging energy infrastructure.

title: Why Have SPAC Valuations Skyrocketed?
summary: An FTI Consulting analysis reveals three key trends contributing to skyrocketing SPAC valuations: an increasing reliance on forward revenue multiples, longer projection periods, and significantly higher projected growth rates. This comes as the SEC cautions against the use of optimistic projections, with many recent SPAC mergers involving less mature, pre-revenue companies trading at multi-billion dollar valuations based on these extended, high-growth projections. The analysis suggests that successful de-SPAC mergers will require reasonable financial projections, robust operating models, and clear communication with stakeholders.

title: General Motors Launches Dedicated Battery Recycling Site
summary: General Motors has introduced a dedicated website, recyclemybattery.com, to provide information on how to safely disable, remove, store, and ship battery packs from its hybrid and electric vehicles for recycling. This initiative aims to address the growing need for EV battery recycling as the number of electric vehicles on the road is projected to reach 245 million by 2030. GM has also partnered with Li-Cycle to recycle battery material scrap from its manufacturing processes, aiming to reintroduce important materials like cobalt, nickel, and lithium back into new battery production.

title: Documentary shines a light on lithium mining and conflicts in Argentina
summary: A new documentary titled "In the name of lithium" highlights the conflicts arising from lithium mining in Argentina, focusing on indigenous communities in Salinas Grandes, Jujuy province. The film, which took five years to make, explores the environmental and social impacts of lithium extraction, particularly concerning water usage. Communities fear that the extensive water required for mining will deplete their resources, impacting their livelihoods and the local ecosystem.

title: Tesla Rival Li Auto Launches $2 Billion Hong Kong Share Sale
summary: Electric-car maker Li Auto Inc. has launched a nearly $2 billion stock offering in Hong Kong, following other U.S.-listed Chinese companies seeking investments closer to home. This move proceeds despite a recent selloff in offshore-listed Chinese stocks due to official actions against various sectors. The company, a Nasdaq-listed EV manufacturer, is pushing ahead with the share sale amidst market volatility.

title: Internet of Things Companies List 2026: Best Companies to Trade
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of the best Internet of Things (IoT) companies to consider for trading in 2026, explaining the concept of IoT and its everyday applications. It details specific companies like Skyworks Solutions, Cisco, and Impinj, along with the Global X IoT ETF (SNSR), while also addressing the potential downsides and security concerns related to widespread IoT adoption. The article aims to guide investors on how to gain exposure to the growing IoT sector.

title: ETF of the Week: Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF (BITQ)
summary: This article highlights the Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF (BITQ), which tracks companies generating most of their revenue from crypto business activities, as a top performer. The article discusses recent crypto market catalysts, including rumors of Amazon accepting crypto payments and statements from Elon Musk regarding Tesla's Bitcoin holdings and Jack Dorsey on Twitter's crypto integration. BITQ is presented as a way for investors to gain exposure to the crypto economy through "pure-play" companies like Coinbase, Silvergate Capital, and MicroStrategy, without directly owning cryptocurrencies.

title: Biden sets goal of making half of U.S. auto industry electric by 2030
summary: President Biden signed an executive order aiming for 50% of all US vehicles sold by 2030 to be electric, supported by major automakers who highlighted the need for significant government funding. This non-binding target is part of his broader climate change strategy, backed by proposed new vehicle emissions standards. The initiative has garnered support from various manufacturers, though some, like Tesla, were notably absent from the discussions.

title: Tesla Cybertruck steel supplier’s $1.7-billion TX facility is coming to form
summary: Steel Dynamics, a key supplier for the Tesla Cybertruck's steel, is making significant progress on its $1.7 billion facility in Sinton, Texas. The plant, located relatively close to Gigafactory Texas, is expected to begin operations in Fall 2021, ensuring a smooth steel supply for Cybertruck production. Tesla plans to "redo" the steel from the Sinton plant, hinting at unique modifications for the Cybertruck's exoskeleton.

title: Tesla: Model Y body structure will differ between Calif., Tex. factories
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that Model Y vehicles produced at the new Austin, Texas, and Berlin, Germany, factories will feature a different body structure than those made in Fremont, California. The new plants will produce Model Ys with cast front and rear bodies and a "structural pack" utilizing 4680 battery cells for mass and cost reduction. While the Fremont plant's Model Y has only a cast rear body, Musk emphasized "substantial improvements" in manufacturing simplification for the new facilities, with production expected to begin later this year.

title: Jefferson: Tunnels with Teslas — coming soon to San Antonio?
summary: Elon Musk's Boring Company is in talks with San Antonio officials to potentially build an underground transportation loop using Tesla vehicles to alleviate traffic congestion and reduce pollution. While the company has made progress on some projects like the Las Vegas Convention Center loop, others in major cities have stalled. Discussions are early, but a potential route linking the San Antonio International Airport to downtown is being considered, with possible expansion to a larger network.

title: Why the SPDR S&P Kensho Clean Power ETF could breakout
summary: The SPDR S&P Kensho Clean Power ETF (CNRG) experienced a significant downturn in 2021 despite initial strong performance, primarily due to supply chain issues in solar energy and policy uncertainties. However, with encouraging Q2 results from key holdings like Enphase Energy and progress on US infrastructure bills, the ETF is showing signs of recovery. Analysts remain bullish on solar stocks and clean energy due to falling renewable energy costs, technological innovation, and increasing global acceptance.

title: Joby Aviation Announces Closing of Business Combination with Reinvent Technology Partners to Become Publicly Traded Company
summary: Joby Aviation announced the completion of its business combination with Reinvent Technology Partners, making it a publicly traded company on the NYSE under the ticker "JOBY." The transaction values Joby at $4.5 billion enterprise value and is expected to fund the company through initial commercial operations of its all-electric aircraft for aerial ridesharing. Joby leadership cited its technological advantage and progress toward FAA certification as key differentiators in the eVTOL market.

title: Joby Aviation Announces Closing of Business Combination with Reinvent Technology Partners to Become Publicly Traded Company
summary: Joby Aviation announced the closing of its business combination with Reinvent Technology Partners, making it a publicly traded company on the NYSE under the ticker "JOBY" as of August 11, 2021. This milestone positions Joby as the first U.S.-based eVTOL company on the public market, with approximately $1.6 billion in proceeds expected to fund through initial commercial operations. The company's leadership in the sector is highlighted by its technological advancements, progress toward FAA certification, and strategic partnerships.

title: Joby Aviation Goes Public
summary: Joby Aviation has become the first U.S.-based eVTOL company to go public, listing on the NYSE through a $6.6 billion reverse merger with SPAC Reinvent Technology Partners. The company aims to launch an emissions-free aerial ridesharing service by 2024, with aircraft capable of transporting a pilot and four passengers at speeds up to 200 mph with a 150-mile range. Joby recently achieved a 150-sm flight range on a single charge and holds strategic partnerships with companies like Toyota and Uber.

title: Global Synthetic Graphite Market To Reach Around Us$ 7 Bn By 2026; Increase In Demand For Graphite Electrodes To Drive Market
summary: The global synthetic graphite market is projected to reach approximately US$ 7 billion by 2026, growing at a CAGR of over 5% from its US$ 4 billion valuation in 2017. This growth is primarily driven by increasing demand for synthetic graphite in metallurgy, electronics, and especially in the production of graphite electrodes for electric arc furnaces and lithium-ion batteries. Asia Pacific is expected to lead this expansion due to its significant demand for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Domino’s Pizza, Pinterest, GoDaddy e AMC: confira os 33 BDRs que estreiam na B3 nesta 2ª feira
summary: On August 16th, 33 new BDRs, including Domino's Pizza, Pinterest, GoDaddy, and AMC Entertainment, began trading on the B3. These BDRs allow Brazilian investors to access global company stocks, with significant growth in investor numbers and trading volumes since regulatory changes in 2020. The article highlights top-performing BDRs and the increasing interest of Brazilian investors in this market segment.

title: Tesla Stock: A Look At Their Plant, Property & Equipment (NASDAQ:TSLA)
summary: This article examines Tesla's plant, property, and equipment (PPE) as detailed in their Q2 2021 earnings report. It highlights a significant increase in PPE, driven by large-scale capital projects including new factories and product lines, following their first billion-dollar quarterly profit. The author, a CPA, analyzes these developments for investors.

title: Palladium Rally Threatened by Automakers’ Pivot to Platinum
summary: The palladium rally, which has seen prices more than triple since mid-2018, is facing significant threats due to increasing platinum substitution by automakers and the long-term rise of electric vehicles. Automakers are increasingly opting for the cheaper platinum in catalytic converters for gasoline engines, driven by technological advancements and palladium’s high prices. This shift, coupled with the eventual dominance of electric vehicles, poses an existential threat to palladium demand.

title: Xos unveils mobile charging station for EV fleets
summary: Xos, Inc., an electric commercial vehicle manufacturer, has introduced Xos Hub, a mobile charging station designed for EV fleets. This portable unit can charge up to five vehicles simultaneously and holds up to 3 MWh of energy storage, addressing the bottleneck of charging infrastructure for EV adoption. The company also offers an "infrastructure-as-a-service" platform for comprehensive EV fleet support.

title: Moderna Achieves a Tesla-Like Aura With Investors
summary: Moderna's rapid valuation increase due to its Covid-19 vaccine is drawing comparisons to Tesla's market performance. Both companies have seen their market capitalization soar, joining the S&P 500 index despite valuations that defy conventional analysis. The article explores the parallels between these two seemingly disparate companies and their investor appeal.

title: It’s official: Joby goes public
summary: Joby Aviation has officially gone public on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol JOBY, completing its business combination with special purpose acquisition company Reinvent Technology Partners (RTP). The transaction values Joby at $4.5 billion, with approximately $1.6 billion in funding secured to support its initial commercial operations. Joby expects its eVTOL aircraft, which has already logged over 1,000 test flights, to enter service as early as 2024.

title: Why do Tesla cars keep crashing into emergency response vehicles? Federal safety agency is investigating
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched a formal investigation into Tesla's Autopilot system after 11 crashes involving Tesla vehicles hitting stationary emergency response vehicles, resulting in 17 injuries and one death. The probe covers 765,000 Tesla cars built between 2014 and 2021. Critics argue that Tesla's marketing of Autopilot as hands-free undermines safety, while the company has faced scrutiny for driver attention monitoring and its "Full Self-Driving" claims.

title: Tesla says Elon Musk's 2020 compensation was nil
summary: Tesla Inc. reported that CEO Elon Musk's total compensation for 2020 was nil, a decrease from $23,760 in 2019, while CFO Zachary Kirkhorn's compensation rose significantly to $46.6 million. Musk's pay package is tied to Tesla's market capitalization and financial growth targets, and he has recently qualified for options worth over $30 billion from his 2018 package. The company also notably assigned Musk the title "Technoking of Tesla" and Kirkhorn "Master of Coin" in a recent regulatory filing.

title: 'Big Short' Michael Burry Bets Against Tesla Stock, Cathie Wood's Ark
summary: Michael Burry, known for his "Big Short" bet, has increased his bearish position against Tesla, with put options on 1.1 million shares. Additionally, his firm, Scion Asset Management, placed a new wager against Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF, purchasing put options on 235,500 shares. Burry has previously criticized Tesla's valuation and Wood's investment strategy, drawing parallels to historical market bubbles.

title: EGEB: Here are the 3 biggest trends in rooftop solar and battery storage
summary: An analysis by EnergySage, an online US solar marketplace, revealed three key trends in rooftop solar and battery storage between July 2020 and June 2021: solar prices decreased, battery storage prices increased, and solar loan rates became more consumer-friendly. Separately, India achieved a significant milestone by reaching 100 gigawatts of clean energy capacity, positioning itself as a global leader in renewable energy despite its government's stance on net-zero emissions.

title: U.S. opens formal probe into Tesla Autopilot system
summary: The U.S. government has launched a formal investigation into Tesla's Autopilot system following 11 crashes since 2018 where Teslas on Autopilot hit parked emergency vehicles, resulting in 17 injuries and one fatality. The probe covers 765,000 Tesla vehicles and will assess the technology's ability to monitor driver engagement and detect objects. This action signals a tougher stance by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on automated vehicle safety, though Tesla maintains drivers must be ready to intervene at all times.

title: US probe into Tesla’s Autopilot woes includes 765,000 vehicles
summary: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched a formal safety probe into Tesla's Autopilot system, covering 765,000 vehicles. This investigation follows 11 crashes since 2018 where Teslas using Autopilot or Traffic-Aware Cruise Control hit emergency vehicles with active warning signals, resulting in 17 injuries and one fatality. The probe aims to assess the technologies that monitor and enforce driver engagement, as authorities emphasize that currently no commercially available vehicles are capable of fully autonomous driving.

title: Opinion: Bullish optimism boosting ‘unicorn’ stocks is more like delirium — and a harsh dose of reality is coming
summary: The article argues that the current bullish optimism surrounding "unicorn" stocks is akin to delirium, suggesting that a harsh dose of reality is imminent for these highly valued private companies. It draws a parallel to the early, uncertain stages of now-successful tech giants, highlighting that most "half-baked ideas" fail, and entrepreneurs often operate without hard evidence. The piece implies that the market is overvaluing these companies and that their current high valuations are unsustainable.

title: Cathie Wood says Michael Burry doesn't understand innovation space after he bets against ARK fund
summary: Cathie Wood responded to Michael Burry's bet against her flagship ARK Innovation ETF, stating she believes he doesn't understand the fundamentals of the innovation space.
