title: Cohen & Steers brings on head of ESG
summary: Cohen & Steers has appointed Khalid Husain as its head of ESG. This move is significant for the company, indicating a focus on environmental, social, and governance factors within its operations. The article notes this alongside other financial industry news regarding private credit, endowments, and pension funds.

title: Endeavor Adds Post House Capital CEO Jacqueline Reses to Board of Directors
summary: Endeavor Group Holdings Inc. has appointed Jacqueline Reses, CEO of Post House Capital, to its board of directors, increasing the number of women on its seven-member board to three. This move ensures Endeavor complies with California's Senate Bill 826, which mandates a minimum number of women on the boards of publicly traded companies in the state. Reses brings extensive experience in corporate finance, technology, and various other board positions.

title: How to Buy Bitcoin...Without Buying Bitcoin
summary: This article explores six alternative methods for investors to gain exposure to Bitcoin without directly purchasing the cryptocurrency. It outlines strategies such as investing in companies that hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets, utilizing Grayscale Trusts, investing in crypto trading platforms, and exploring blockchain-focused ETFs. Additionally, it highlights opportunities to earn Bitcoin through shopping rewards programs and dedicated Bitcoin credit cards.

title: This EV Brand Aims to Dethrone Tesla in China
summary: Chinese automaker Nio aims to challenge Tesla's dominance in the EV market in China by offering competitive pricing, advanced technology, and innovative services like battery swapping. Nio's ET7 premium sedan is designed to undercut the Tesla Model S in price while offering comparable or superior range and features. The company also ranked higher than Tesla in a recent initial quality survey for battery electric vehicles.

title: Tesla unveils chip to train A.I. models inside its data centers
summary: Tesla has unveiled a custom D1 chip designed for training artificial-intelligence networks in its data centers, which is part of its Dojo supercomputer system. An employee stated it will be the fastest AI-training computer, aiming to process extensive computing work for models that recognize items from car camera feeds. Tesla also continues to offer and develop its "Full Self-Driving Capability" for vehicles, despite criticism regarding its level of autonomy and recent investigations.

title: Musk says Tesla likely to launch humanoid robot prototype next year
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla plans to launch a "Tesla Bot" humanoid robot prototype next year, designed to perform dangerous, repetitive, or boring tasks. The robot is intended to address labor shortages and be affordable. This announcement comes amid scrutiny over Tesla's "Full Self-Driving" system and its safety amid recent accidents, which Musk did not address directly, but expressed confidence in its future safety.

title: Raiders of the Lost ARK Innovation ETF
summary: This article discusses the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) in the context of recent market drama, specifically a reported feud between Michael Burry and Cathie Wood. The author explains ARKK's focus on disruptive innovation and debates its diversification, ultimately expressing a positive long-term outlook but caution about its current valuation and entry point due to market bubble concerns. The recommendation is to buy ARKK if its price falls to $100 or below.

title: Tesla and Elon Musk’s Dancing Robot Bordered on Self-Parody
summary: During Tesla Inc.'s artificial intelligence showcase, CEO Elon Musk introduced a human performer dressed as a robot who danced to electronic music after engineers explained the technical details of the company's self-driving technology. This presentation style, juxtaposing advanced engineering with a dancing human, prompted observers to comment on its self-parodying nature. The event highlighted Tesla's AI advancements while also showcasing a more theatrical side of its corporate presentations.

title: GM's $2 billion Chevy Bolt fire recall casts shadow over electric vehicle market
summary: General Motors has expanded its recall of Chevrolet Bolt electric vehicles due to concerns over battery fires, now including all 142,000 units sold, at an estimated cost of nearly $2 billion. This issue, caused by manufacturing defects in LG Chem-supplied batteries, mirrors problems seen in Hyundai's Kona EV and raises industry concerns about the potential impact of such incidents on the burgeoning electric vehicle market. Despite the low incidence rate of EV fires compared to gasoline-powered cars, the industry fears that these incidents could deter consumers as billions are invested in the transition to electric power.

title: Insight: A secret weapon for self-driving car startups: Humans
summary: Self-driving car startups like Cruise and Pony.ai are using human safety operators in their driverless vehicles in California, highlighting the ongoing challenges in achieving fully autonomous driving. Major players such as Waymo and even Tesla acknowledge the need for human oversight, either through in-car operators, remote monitoring, or roadside assistance, to ensure safety and build public trust. The continued reliance on human involvement suggests a scaling down of initial full autonomy ambitions to generate revenue sooner, a shift from the previous "dirty little secret" of human assistance.

title: Musk says Tesla's self-driving software update 'not great'
summary: Elon Musk stated that Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta version 9.2 is "actually not great" but that the Autopilot/AI team is working to improve it rapidly. The company is aiming for a single software stack for both highway and city streets, which requires extensive neural network retraining. This comes as Tesla faces scrutiny from U.S. safety regulators and calls for investigation into its marketing of self-driving features.

title: Home Depot improves inventory depth with focus on high-velocity SKUs
summary: Home Depot is enhancing its inventory by focusing on high-demand products and chartering its own ships to navigate supply chain disruptions. This strategy, prioritizing "highest velocity SKUs" like electrical and plumbing fixtures, has led to a 24% increase in customer transactions over $1,000, despite an overall 6% drop in transactions. The company's efforts, including working closely with suppliers to narrow product focus, resulted in a 26% year-over-year inventory value increase and an 8% net sales increase in Q2.

title: Michael Saylor’s MicroStrategy Buys 3,907 More Bitcoin as Total Investment Nears $3 Billion
summary: MicroStrategy, led by Michael Saylor, announced the purchase of an additional 3,907 bitcoin for approximately $177 million in cash during its third quarter. This acquisition brings the company's total bitcoin holdings to 108,992, acquired at an average price of $26,769 per bitcoin, with an aggregate purchase price nearing $3 billion. MicroStrategy continues its strategy of buying and self-custodying bitcoin indefinitely, positioning itself as a leader in the space.

title: China’s Tough Data Rules Could Hit High-Flying Auto Stocks. XPeng Isn’t Worried.
summary: A Barron's article discusses the potential impact of Beijing's data regulations on Chinese auto stocks listed in the U.S. Despite these looming regulations, a top official from the electric vehicle manufacturer XPeng expressed no concern. XPeng, a Chinese rival to Tesla, is seemingly confident in its position amidst the changing regulatory landscape.

title: Review | Tesla’s wild ride, steered by Elon Musk
summary: This article is a review of the book "Power Play: Tesla, Elon Musk, and the Bet of the Century" by Tim Higgins. It highlights that Elon Musk is both crucial to Tesla's success and a potential liability. The review touches on Tesla's early days, including efforts to recruit employees and its initial stock price.

title: Soon, Tesla's Model S Plaid Might Receive an Equally Bonkers Luxury EV Answer
summary: Lucid Motors' Air Dream Edition is poised to challenge the Tesla Model S Plaid, offering a luxury EV alternative. Lucid went public on Nasdaq and secured $4.4 billion for development, including expanding its factory and accelerating the Project Gravity SUV. The Air Dream Edition will come in two versions, Performance (1,111 hp for speed) and Range (933 hp for maximizing range), directly competing with the Plaid in the high-performance EV market.

title: Self-Driving Cars Still Require Human Operators
summary: Despite billions in investment, self-driving cars largely still require human oversight, either as in-vehicle safety operators, through remote supervision, or by close driver monitoring. Companies like Pony.ai and Cruise are gradually reducing direct human presence but acknowledge the ongoing need for human intervention to ensure safety and build public trust. Technical and legal difficulties, along with recent safety investigations, highlight the complexities of fully autonomous vehicle development.
source: VOA - Voice of America English News

title: Piedmont, Sayona complete Canadian lithium miner buy
summary: Piedmont Lithium and Sayona Mining have finalized their acquisition of North American Lithium (NAL), proceeding with plans to establish a significant lithium production hub in Quebec's Abitibi region. The companies intend to merge NAL with Sayona's Authier and Tansim projects and are conducting studies for reactivating NAL's spodumene concentrate operations and for manufacturing lithium chemicals in Quebec. This initiative aims to position Quebec as a key lithium hydroxide producer, leveraging its proximity to major EV markets.

title: Big Tesla Exposure Could Give This ETF a Boost
summary: The First Trust NASDAQ Clean Edge Green Energy Index Fund (QCLN) holds a significant 8.45% allocation to Tesla, making it one of the largest ETF owners of Tesla stock. This exposure positions QCLN to potentially benefit from the rapid growth of electric vehicles and Tesla's broader clean energy initiatives. As the automotive industry transitions to battery electric vehicles, Tesla's market share and profitability, along with its ancillary businesses like energy generation and storage, could drive value for the ETF.

title: J.D. Power 2021 Initial Quality Study: Ram on Top, Wireless Phone Connectivity Spells Trouble
summary: The J.D. Power 2021 Initial Quality Study revealed that while overall new-vehicle quality improved, infotainment systems, particularly wireless phone connectivity, remain the most problematic area for owners. Ram topped the rankings for the first time with a score of 128 problems per 100 vehicles, significantly better than the industry average of 162, while Chrysler, Volkswagen, and Audi were at the bottom. The study emphasizes that initial quality issues often relate to technology usability rather than manufacturing build quality.

title: Chunghwa Telecom eyeing partnership with Starlink
summary: Chunghwa Telecom is exploring partnerships with low Earth orbit satellite service providers, including Elon Musk's Starlink project, to expand internet coverage beyond 5G. This move aims to diversify services and enhance network reach, particularly in remote areas, although regulatory approval from the National Communications Commission is required before services can be offered. The company also highlighted government subsidies for 5G infrastructure development for qualifying telecoms.

title: Upcoming electric trucks: Cybertruck, F-150 Lightning, Hummer EV compared
summary: This article compares three highly anticipated electric trucks: the Tesla Cybertruck, Ford F-150 Lightning, and GMC Hummer EV. It delves into the background, current status, and known specifications of each vehicle, highlighting their unique features and market positioning. The comparison aims to inform potential buyers and enthusiasts about the emerging electric truck segment.

title: The Lucid Air Dream Edition Will Offer Both Range and Horsepower
summary: Lucid is launching two versions of its limited-run Air Dream Edition electric car: a "Performance" variant with 1,111 horsepower and a "Range" variant with 933 horsepower, emphasizing range. Recent real-world tests showed impressive range, with one car achieving 517 miles on a single charge, surpassing the 405-mile range of the Long-Range Tesla Model S. Despite a high price point mirroring Tesla's initial strategy, industry experts believe Lucid's range capabilities could significantly alleviate consumer "range anxiety."

title: 7 Robotics Stocks to Buy for Elon Musk’s Big ‘Tesla Bot’ Bet
summary: This article highlights seven robotics stocks that are poised for lucrative returns, driven by the increasing demand for robotics across various industries and tech giants like Tesla and Amazon. It discusses the market growth projections for industrial robotics and provides detailed analysis, financial data, and future outlook for each recommended stock, including ABB, AeroVironment, Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF, Intuitive Surgical, iRobot, Oceaneering International, and Raytheon Technologies. The author emphasizes that these companies leverage automation and AI to enhance efficiency and address evolving market needs.

title: Tesla's China output halted for days in August on chip shortage - Bloomberg News
summary: Tesla temporarily halted some operations at its Shanghai factory for about four days in August due to the global semiconductor shortage, primarily affecting its Model Y production. This incident reflects the broader impact of the chip shortage on the automotive industry, with other major manufacturers like Toyota also announcing significant production cuts. Bloomberg News reported that production at the Chinese factory has since returned to normal.

title: Amid Tesla’s Autopilot Probe, Nearly Half the Public Thinks Autonomous Vehicles Are Less Safe Than Normal Cars
summary: A new Morning Consult poll reveals that 47% of US adults believe autonomous vehicles (AVs) are less safe than human-driven cars, despite a slight increase in public interest in riding them since 2018. This comes as the federal government investigates Tesla for crashes involving its "Autopilot" feature, though a significant portion of the public remains unaware of the probe. While trust in AVs is low, interest in purchasing them within the next decade rose slightly after respondents learned about the Tesla incidents.

title: GM temporarily shuts down North American factories because of chip shortage
summary: General Motors announced temporary production halts at six North American factories due to the ongoing global chip shortage, affecting its most profitable vehicles like pickup trucks and SUVs. This is the second time GM has faced such shutdowns, with the company estimating a $1.5 billion to $2 billion loss in earnings due to lost production this year. Other major automakers, including Volkswagen, Ford, and Toyota, are also struggling with the semiconductor supply issue.

title: China set to sell 1.7 million NEVs between Jan-Aug, nearly tripling on-year
summary: China is projected to sell 1.7 million new energy vehicles (NEVs) in the first eight months of the year, nearly tripling sales from the same period last year. This growth is driven by government promotion of greener vehicles and expanding manufacturing capacity by NEV makers like Nio, BYD, and Tesla. Despite a global auto chip shortage, China's total auto sales are expected to exceed 16 million units in the same period, with authorities planning to curb blind construction of NEV projects and secure supplies of key metals.

title: Alphabet, Tesla and Amazon are among the most favourite stocks held by US-focused mutual funds. Here are top 10 stocks
summary: This article identifies Alphabet, Tesla, and Amazon as top stock holdings among U.S.-focused mutual funds available to Indian investors. It details 10 such mutual funds, highlighting their investment strategies, underlying assets, and historical performance. The funds provide Indian investors exposure to leading US companies and geographical diversification.

title: Tesla sold 44,264 China-made vehicles in August, local deliveries up
summary: Tesla sold 44,264 China-made vehicles in August, with local deliveries significantly increasing to 12,885 cars from 8,621 in July. The company also exported 31,379 vehicles from its Shanghai factory. This increase follows Tesla introducing cheaper versions of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in China amidst growing competition.

title: The Generator Company to Watch
summary: Louis Navellier highlights Generac Holdings, Inc. (GNRC) as a compelling investment due to the increasing demand for generators spurred by natural disasters and an unreliable power grid. Generac, a leader in home backup generators, is also expanding its clean energy solutions with products like PWRcell, positioning itself favorably amid the transition to green energy. The company reported strong Q2 2021 results, exceeding sales and earnings expectations, and raised its full-year guidance, indicating significant growth potential.

title: Self-Driving Cars? Naw, Sign Me up for a Future Where We All Ride Intelligent Robotic Unicorns
summary: XPeng, a Chinese electric vehicle maker, has revealed a prototype of a rideable robotic unicorn, presenting an alternative to traditional autonomous cars. This robotic unicorn aims to provide both transportation and companionship, incorporating AI features for navigation and emotional interaction, inspired by Boston Dynamics' earlier work on quadrupedal robots. While currently scaled for children, XPeng hopes to scale it for adults, offering a potentially whimsical future for personal transportation.

title: MicroVision Will Be a Winner if It Can Make Lidar Cheap
summary: MicroVision (MVIS) stock has seen significant volatility, behaving like a meme stock, primarily due to its development of a lidar system for the automotive sector. The company aims to produce an effective lidar system with an average selling price under $1,000, significantly cheaper than historical costs, despite competition already offering similar low-cost solutions. While Tesla's CEO Elon Musk has publicly dismissed lidar, reports suggest Tesla is experimenting with it, and a contract win with automakers, especially Tesla, would be a major boost for MVIS.

title: When Hands-Free Ain’t Free: What’s the Cost of Self-Driving Tech?
summary: The article discusses the growing trend of subscription models for advanced driver-assist features from manufacturers like Tesla, Ford, and General Motors. It details the capabilities and pricing of systems such as Tesla's Full Self-Driving, Ford and Lincoln's BlueCruise/ActiveGlide, and GM's Super Cruise. The author questions the value proposition of these semi-autonomous systems, noting their limitations and significant costs, and suggests that potential buyers consider their personal driving habits before investing.

title: Ford hires former Lowe's, Home Depot executive as chief digital and information officer
summary: Ford Motor Co. has appointed Mike Amend, formerly of Lowe's Companies Inc., as its new chief digital and information officer to lead the company's technology and software platforms. This strategic hire aligns with CEO Jim Farley's vision to transform Ford through electrification and advanced technologies, leveraging Amend's experience in e-commerce and digital growth from his previous roles at Lowe's, JCPenney, and Home Depot. Amend will work alongside Hau Thai-Tang and recent hire Doug Field to drive Ford's technological initiatives and develop new software solutions.

title: China Has ‘Too Many’ EV Companies. What It Means for NIO and Tesla Stock.
summary: China's industry and information technology minister announced plans to encourage market consolidation within its burgeoning electric-vehicle sector. This move comes as the country aims to streamline its EV industry, which has seen rapid growth due to policies promoting greener transportation. The consolidation efforts could significantly impact major EV players like NIO and potentially Tesla's operations in the Chinese market.

title: Cathie Wood’s Ark slips out of top 10 ETF issuers
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management has dropped out of the top 10 ETF issuers, now ranking 11th with approximately $42.4 billion in assets, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. This slip comes amidst inflationary fears and rising competition from firms like WisdomTree and Dimensional Fund Advisors. Despite a strong performance in 2020, Ark's flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) has fallen over 5% this year as long-term tech bets face headwinds.

title: EV Traction Motor Market Top Key Players - Siemens AG, Nidec
summary: The global EV traction motor market, valued at $3.1 Billion in 2020, is projected to reach $7.5 Billion by 2025. This growth is driven by significant investments from major automotive players like VW and GM into electric vehicle production and platforms, as well as ongoing innovations in motor technology by companies such as Siemens and Mahle. The market is currently consolidated due to existing OEM Supplier contracts and substantial internal production efforts.

title: Lucid Air official range, Rivian R1T production, Xpeng P5 pricing and plans: Today’s Car News
summary: The article reports on key developments in the electric vehicle market, including the Lucid Air achieving a 520-mile EPA range rating, surpassing Tesla. It also covers Rivian commencing production of its R1T electric trucks and Xpeng releasing pricing for its P5 sedan, which is poised to challenge the European market with a sub-$25,000 starting price.

title: Solar Panel Complaints: Unreturned Calls, Canceled Appointments
summary: The News4 I-Team investigated numerous complaints from solar panel customers experiencing issues like roof leaks, poor customer service, unreturned calls, and unexpected costs for panel removal and reinstallation. Homeowners faced challenges with companies like Sunrun and Tesla, leading to extended delays and financial burdens. Experts advise thoroughly understanding contracts before committing to a 20-year solar agreement, especially regarding warranties, moving contingencies, and end-of-term ownership.

title: Tesla to reverse solar price hike for some customers, legal filing says
summary: Tesla is reportedly reversing solar price hikes for some customers who signed contracts before April 2021, according to a legal filing. This move comes after customers, including lead plaintiff Matthew Amans, sued the company over sudden and significant price increases. Tesla had previously raised prices and mandated the purchase of Powerwall systems, contributing to customer frustration.

title: DFAX Stock Price | Dimensional World ex U.S. Core Equity 2 ETF
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Dimensional World ex U.S. Core Equity 2 ETF (DFAX), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NYSE), and key financial metrics. It also covers the ETF's historical performance, dividend yield, expense ratio, and top holdings, offering a comprehensive overview for potential investors.

title: Insight: A life and death question for regulators: Is Tesla's Autopilot safe?
summary: U.S. regulators are intensifying investigations into Tesla's Autopilot feature following numerous crashes, some fatal, that raise concerns about the system's safety and potential for driver misuse. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is scrutinizing 12 crashes, many occurring in limited visibility conditions, while the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) criticizes Tesla's focus on innovation over safety. This reopens a debate on Autopilot's capabilities, especially given Tesla's reliance on cameras alone for its semi-autonomous technology, which experts say can be unreliable in challenging conditions.

title: GM's new business model turns carmaker into software company: 'A potential game-changer'
summary: General Motors is transitioning into a software company that also makes cars, viewing its vehicles as platforms to deliver subscription services for recurring revenue. This new business model is attracting technology talent and is expected to expand beyond traditional automotive services into areas like insurance and even powering other modes of transport such as planes and trains. GM aims to leverage its scale while fostering an agile, startup-like approach to software development.

title: Samsung to make Tesla’s HW 4.0 self-driving auto chip
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. has won the contract to manufacture Tesla Inc.'s next-generation hardware 4 (HW 4.0) chip for its autonomous driving technology, beating out TSMC. Samsung plans to mass-produce the HW 4.0 chip using 7-nanometer processing technology, ensuring higher production yields and stable functions for Tesla's upcoming vehicles like the Cybertruck. This partnership strengthens Samsung's position in the global foundry market as it competes with TSMC and expands its collaborations with other tech giants like Google and Amazon.

title: Tysons Corner gets a Halloween pop-up, a Uniqlo-like lifestyle retailer, and more changes
summary: Tysons Corner Center has introduced several new tenants and changes, including a seasonal Extreme Halloween pop-up store and the highly anticipated opening of Miniso, a Chinese lifestyle retailer similar to Uniqlo. The mall also welcomed Middle Eastern eatery Marhaba and saw furniture store Lovesac temporarily relocate for renovations. Additionally, luxury fashion store Aritzia and kitchen tools company ZWILLING are scheduled to open this winter, among other upcoming additions.

title: Tesla to sell auto insurance in Texas next month
summary: Tesla is expanding its auto insurance product to Texas in October, with CEO Elon Musk indicating potential worldwide expansion despite regulatory challenges. The company aims to offer real-time insurance based on actual driving history, a feature Musk hopes will address high premium concerns from Tesla owners. Tesla Insurance launched in California in 2019, with rates reportedly influenced by driving behavior data.

title: Cars.com’s 2021 Car Seat Fit Report Card
summary: Cars.com's 2021 Car Seat Fit Report Card compiles a year's worth of Car Seat Checks across 51 vehicles, evaluating how well different cars accommodate various child safety seats. The report identifies vehicles that received top "A" grades across all categories, making them ideal for families with car seats. It also provides a detailed breakdown of car seat installation performance by vehicle type, including two-row SUVs, three-row SUVs, minivans, pickup trucks, EVs/PHEVs/Hybrids, sedans, and hatchbacks.

title: Some Apple, Tesla suppliers suspend production in China amid power pinch
summary: Several Apple and Tesla suppliers in China have suspended production due to stricter energy consumption policies and tight coal supplies, impacting their supply chains during the peak season for electronics. While some Taiwanese manufacturers temporarily halted operations, major chipmakers like UMC and TSMC reported no impact on their China facilities, and Foxconn experienced only a "very small" adjustment to its non-Apple production. This comes as China's heavy industry faces contraction, affecting the country's economic growth rate.

title: Ford Will Build 4 Factories in a Big Electric Vehicle Push (Published 2021)
summary: Ford Motor announced a massive $11.4 billion investment to build three battery factories and an electric truck plant in the U.S., creating 11,000 jobs. This move signifies the company's significant commitment to electric vehicles, aiming to produce over one million EVs annually and contribute to global climate change efforts. The investment is Ford's largest in its 118-year history, reflecting a broader industry pivot towards electrification due to environmental concerns and competition from Tesla.

title: Agnico Eagle, Kirkland Lake create new gold giant in $10bn merger
summary: Canadian gold miners Agnico Eagle Mines and Kirkland Lake Gold announced a C$13.5 billion ($10.7bn) merger, creating a new gold giant with a market capitalization of about $24 billion and a mineral reserve base of 48 million ounces of gold. The deal is expected to generate $2 billion in synergies over the next 10 years and positions the combined entity to produce 3.4 million ounces of gold this year. This merger could trigger further consolidation in the gold industry, with analysts anticipating a new wave of M&A activity focused on jurisdictional synergies and growth generation.

title: Brain-science products roll out despite ethical, validity concerns
summary: Japanese companies are increasing their research into "brain technology," developing products for marketing, health, and concentration, some of which are already on the market. However, significant ethical and validity concerns persist, as many products lack robust scientific evidence and questions arise about the intrusiveness of technologies that delve into human brain activities. Experts are working to establish frameworks to assess the trustworthiness of these products to build public confidence and guide industry development.

title: Ford making its biggest single manufacturing investment ever to build electric vehicle factories
summary: Ford Motor Co. and SK Innovations are investing $11.4 billion to build two new electric vehicle manufacturing campuses in Kentucky and Tennessee, creating over 10,000 jobs. This represents Ford's largest-ever single manufacturing investment, aiming for 40% of its global sales to be fully electric vehicles by 2030. The facilities will include three battery plants and a factory for electric pickup trucks, with a focus on carbon neutrality and waste reduction.

title: Preparing for the next big thing
summary: LKQ Corp. has proactively acquired Green Bean Battery to prepare for the growing electric vehicle (EV) market by gaining expertise in EV battery refurbishment and repurposing. This strategic move aims to establish LKQ's foothold in the EV sector well in advance of a significant shift from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. The article highlights how the automotive recycling industry is adapting to the unique challenges and opportunities presented by EVs, including differences in materials and the emergence of new markets for high-voltage batteries.

title: Lucid to start deliveries of electric cars with range exceeding Tesla's in October
summary: Lucid Group Inc. announced it will begin delivering its luxury electric sedans in late October, featuring a driving range that surpasses Tesla's. The company has started production of its Lucid Air cars and aims to significantly ramp up capacity, challenging Tesla in the premium EV market. Lucid's CEO highlighted the battery technology advantage and the need to reduce costs for wider EV adoption.

title: Cathie Wood’s Ark Investment sells $270M worth of Tesla stake
summary: Cathie Wood’s Ark Investment Management sold over 340,000 shares of Tesla, worth nearly $270 million, across three of its exchange-traded funds. This move comes as a bond selloff impacted rate-sensitive technology stocks, leading to outflows from Ark's growth-focused funds. Despite the sale, Tesla remains Ark's largest holding, with Wood predicting its shares will reach $3,000.

title: Billionaire Orlando Bravo Owns Bitcoin And Is Very Bullish
summary: Billionaire Orlando Bravo, cofounder of private equity firm Thoma Bravo, has publicly stated his personal investment in Bitcoin and his bullish outlook on its future. He believes that increasing institutional adoption will significantly drive up Bitcoin's value in the coming years. Thoma Bravo, with over $83 billion in assets, recently participated in a funding round for the Bitcoin exchange FTX.

title: I drove the Lucid Air. It's the future of cars.
summary: The author test-drove the Lucid Air Dream Edition, highlighting its meticulous production process, exceptional interior comfort, and advanced technology that differentiate it from competitors like Tesla. While acknowledging minor areas for refinement, the article concludes that the Lucid Air represents a significant leap forward in automotive design and an exciting blueprint for the future of electric vehicles.

title: Jabil expects to hit over $8B in net revenue in Q1 of 2022
summary: Jabil Inc. (NYSE: JBL) reported strong financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year, with net revenue of $7.4 billion and $29.3 billion respectively, despite supply chain challenges. Looking ahead to Q1 2022, the company projects net revenue between $8 billion and $8.6 billion, driven by its diversified business model and opportunities in vehicle electrification, connected healthcare, and infrastructure development. Jabil continues to work with major clients such as Amazon, Tesla, Apple, and Johnson & Johnson.

title: Driver in China successfully sues Tesla for fraud
summary: A Chinese driver, Han Chao, successfully sued Tesla Inc. for fraud in a Beijing court over the purchase of a used Model S that had undergone major repairs. The court ordered Tesla to refund the car's cost and pay three times the purchase price in damages, totaling over 1.5 million yuan. This ruling adds to Tesla's recent negative publicity in China and is seen as a significant win for consumer rights against large corporations.

title: With help from Tesla, nearly 80% of Norway's new car sales are electric
summary: Electric car sales in Norway reached nearly 80% of total new car sales in September, largely due to strong demand for Tesla's mid-sized models. Tesla's Model Y and Model 3 were the top-selling vehicles, benefiting from Norway's tax exemptions on fully electric cars. However, proposed luxury taxes by the incoming government could impact sales of high-end electric models from manufacturers like Tesla, Porsche, Audi, and Mercedes-Benz.

title: Upstart activist Engine No. 1 takes stake in GM, supports EV transition plan
summary: Activist investor firm Engine No. 1 has acquired a stake in General Motors, signaling support for the automaker's electric vehicle transition plans. The firm believes GM's aggressive approach to EVs, including a commitment to exclusively electric vehicles by 2035, positions it for significant growth and potential stock tripling within five years. This investment contrasts with their previous hostile campaign against Exxon, as Engine No. 1 praises GM's management for embracing future changes.

title: Tesla must pay $137 million to ex-worker over hostile work environment, racism
summary: A San Francisco federal court ordered Tesla to pay former worker Owen Diaz $137 million for enduring a hostile work environment and racist abuse. The case progressed because Diaz had not signed Tesla's mandatory arbitration agreement, which typically forces employees to resolve disputes privately. Shareholder activist Nia Impact Capital has urged Tesla's board to analyze the impact of these mandatory arbitration agreements, expressing concern that they may facilitate harassment and other workplace issues.

title: Investors argue Musk should repay $9.4 bln to Tesla for SolarCity deal
summary: Tesla investors are arguing that Elon Musk should repay $9.4 billion to Tesla for benefits received from the 2016 SolarCity deal, proposing he return Tesla shares acquired through the transaction. They allege Musk did not recuse himself from negotiations and failed to disclose SolarCity's dire financial state. Musk, conversely, asserts the deal created a vertically integrated clean energy company at a fair price and was approved by shareholders.

title: Tesla is ordered to pay former worker $137 million for racism at plant
summary: A federal jury in San Francisco has ordered Tesla to pay a Black former elevator operator $137 million in damages. The worker, Owen Diaz, endured racial taunts and offensive graffiti at Tesla's Northern California plant, which the company allegedly ignored. The verdict includes $6.9 million for emotional distress and $130 million in punitive damages, sending a strong message to Tesla regarding its treatment of employees.

title: LG Energy Strikes Battery-Metal Deal With Sigma Lithium
summary: LG Energy Solution has entered a six-year "take-or-pay" agreement with Sigma Lithium Corp. to secure up to 100,000 tons of battery-grade lithium annually. This deal aims to meet the escalating demand for electric vehicle batteries, with commercial deliveries planned to start next year. The partnership also includes yearly negotiations for additional lithium supply and ensures the stability of Sigma's cash flows.

title: General Motors secures supply for silicon carbide chips for its next-gen EVs
summary: General Motors (GM) has announced a deal with Wolfspeed Inc. to secure silicon carbide (SiC) chip supply for its future electric vehicles, to be used in GM's new Ultium Drive units. SiC chips offer improved energy efficiency and heat dissipation compared to traditional silicon, and other EVs like Tesla's Model 3 and NIO also use them. This agreement helps GM manage chip supply amid semiconductor shortages, a crucial step given the higher chip requirements for EVs.

title: GM aims to build Netflix-sized subscription business by 2030
summary: General Motors announced its ambitious goal to generate $25 billion in annual revenue from in-car subscription services by 2030, putting it in the same league as Netflix. The automaker expects nearly $2 billion in revenue from these services this year, driven by its current base of 4.2 million subscribed vehicles and the upcoming Ultifi software platform. GM plans to monetize features like OnStar, Maps+, and fleet management solutions, projecting a serviceable addressable market of $80 billion by 2030.

title: Cathie Wood's Flagship Fund Dumps Almost All of Its Nintendo Stake
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF has significantly reduced its stake in Nintendo, now holding only about 1,500 ADRs worth $82,000. This move comes as analysts express a lack of bullish sentiment regarding Nintendo's new Switch console update, citing a absence of 4K display capabilities and increasing competition. Wood began offloading Nintendo shares in July, and the stock has since dropped 32% year-to-date.

title: GM Details Plan to Double its Revenue, Drive Even Higher Margins
summary: General Motors announced a detailed plan to double its annual revenue and expand margins to 12-14% by 2030, driven by an aggressive shift towards EVs, connected services, and new businesses. The strategy hinges on the Ultium and Ultifi platforms, projecting significant growth in EV revenue, software and services, and autonomous vehicle commercialization through Cruise. GM also plans increased investment in EV charging infrastructure and the launch of new ventures like BrightDrop and Future Roads.

title: BYD, Levo Mobility announce deal for electric trucks equipped with vehicle-to-grid technology
summary: BYD and Levo Mobility have partnered to integrate Nuvve's vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology into BYD battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and plan to deploy up to 5,000 BEVs over the next five years. This collaboration aims to accelerate transportation electrification by enabling BEVs to discharge energy back to the power grid, helping to balance electricity demand and generate revenue for fleet owners. Levo Mobility will offer a turnkey solution, including BEVs, charging infrastructure, and energy management, for a fixed monthly payment.

title: Tesla Racism Verdict of $137 Million Could Be Halved if the Company Appeals
summary: A $137 million verdict against Tesla for racism at one of its plants could be halved if the company appeals, according to legal experts. While former contract worker Owen Diaz was awarded $6.9 million for emotional distress, the punitive damages of $130 million are significantly higher than typical and may be reduced by an appeals court. Despite a potential reduction, the jury's decision sent a strong message to Tesla about the severity of racial harassment, an issue that has plagued the company for years.

title: GE Renewable Energy signs MoU with General Motors to develop supply chain of rare earth and other materials to support EV and renewable energy growth | GE News
summary: GE Renewable Energy and General Motors announced an MoU to evaluate opportunities for improving the supply chain of rare earth materials, magnets, copper, and electrical steel for electric vehicles and renewable energy equipment. The collaboration will initially focus on establishing a North American and European vertically integrated magnet manufacturing supply chain. Both companies aim to secure a low-carbon footprint, ESG-friendly, and cost-competitive supply of these critical materials.

title: Robinhood Enters the Realm of Proxy Voting
summary: Robinhood's acquisition of Say Technologies aims to simplify proxy voting and increase shareholder engagement, particularly among individual investors. This move, alongside efforts by companies like JPMorgan and startups YourStake and OpenInvest, is part of a broader trend to make proxy voting and ESG investing more accessible and impactful. The article highlights how technology is breaking down barriers to participation, addressing the complexities of the voting process, meeting investors on familiar platforms, and helping them understand the impact of their choices.

title: Cathie Wood's funds bought the dip in Gingko Bioworks after a short-seller called it a 'Frankenstein' of frauds
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest funds purchased over 8 million shares of Ginkgo Bioworks after its stock plunged by as much as 24% following a scathing short-seller report from Scorpion Capital. Scorpion Capital described Ginkgo as a "Frankenstein mash-up of the worst frauds" and "a house of cards," alleging fabricated revenue and a "dubious shell game." Despite the accusations, Ark's Innovation ETF and Genomic Revolution ETF now collectively hold $363 million in Ginkgo, demonstrating Wood's strategy of buying the dip even after serious allegations.

title: Baidu-Backed EV-Maker WM Motor Raises $300 Million Despite String of Setbacks
