Despite the controversies, Musk's presence is expected to bring substantial economic growth, creating thousands of jobs and significant gross state product.

title: Musk asks Twitter followers whether he should sell 10% of Tesla stock
summary: Elon Musk polled his Twitter followers on whether he should sell 10% of his Tesla stock, citing potential "massive" tax bills related to stock options and criticism of unrealized gains as tax avoidance. He stated he would abide by the poll's results, which showed 55% approval for selling the shares. Selling 10% of his shares would amount to approximately $21 billion based on Friday's closing price.

title: Elon Musk Asks Twitter If He Should Sell 10% of His Tesla Stock
summary: Elon Musk polled Twitter users about selling 10% of his Tesla stock, an amount currently valued at approximately $21 billion. He stated he would adhere to the poll's outcome, which, as of 9:30 a.m. in New York, showed 57% of voters supported the sale. Musk's decision comes amid discussions about the wealthy's unrealized gains and his previous statements about high tax rates on exercised stock options.

title: Plans To Dig the Biggest Lithium Mine in the US Face Mounting Opposition
summary: Plans for Lithium Americas' Thacker Pass mine in Nevada, poised to be the largest lithium mine in the US, are encountering strong opposition from tribal groups, ranchers, and environmental activists. Opponents argue that the environmental damage and social impact, including potential water pollution and loss of sacred land, outweigh the benefits of lithium for the clean energy transition. The conflict highlights the growing tension between the demand for critical minerals for green technologies and local environmental and social concerns.

title: Twitter users say 'yes' to Musk's proposal to sell 10% of his Tesla stock
summary: Twitter users have voted in favor of Elon Musk selling 10% of his Tesla stock, with 57.9% approving the proposal in a poll conducted by the CEO. Musk stated he would accept either outcome and had previously indicated that he would need to exercise a large number of stock options, incurring a significant tax bill. The sale of approximately $21 billion worth of stock could help cover these taxes, prompting debate around billionaire taxation.

title: PepsiCo CEO says he expects delivery of first Tesla Semis this quarter
summary: PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta announced that the company expects its first delivery of Tesla Semi trucks in the fourth quarter of 2021. This comes almost four years after PepsiCo initially placed a pre-order for 100 Tesla Semi trucks, a delivery that had been delayed due to production challenges and battery cell limitations. Laguarta stated that transportation accounts for about 10% of PepsiCo's overall gas emissions and that they are actively working on solutions, including the adoption of electric trucks.

title: PepsiCo to take delivery of Tesla electric trucks in fourth quarter - CNBC
summary: PepsiCo is set to receive its first Tesla electric semi-trucks in the fourth quarter of 2021, as confirmed by CEO Ramon Laguarta. The company aims to reduce fuel costs and fleet emissions, with transportation accounting for 10% of its gas emissions. Several other major companies like Walmart, J.B. Hunt, and Sysco have also placed orders for Tesla's semi-trucks.

title: ARK Innovation Has Likely Been a Disappointment for Most Investors
summary: The ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), despite its stellar 2020 performance, has underperformed significantly in 2021, leading to investor disappointment and outflows. Most investors bought into the fund at its peak in late 2020 and early 2021, and its concentrated portfolio, heavily weighted in technology and communication services, was hit hard by market shifts. The article highlights that many funds experiencing rapid growth and high returns in one year often face challenges in subsequent years.

title: Midday Meme Stock Report for 11/8: Coinbase, ContextLogic, Tesla, Tilray and More
summary: On November 8, 2021, U.S. markets opened higher with above-average volume, as crude oil and Bitcoin activity influenced markets. Several meme stocks saw significant movement: Tilray Inc. (TLRY) surged over 14% due to potential U.S. marijuana research legislation, while Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN) rose 7.7% after announcing NFT and Shiba Inu listings. ContextLogic Inc. (WISH) saw a 7.2% gain, potentially driven by retail investors targeting short sellers, and Tesla Inc. (TSLA) recovered half its premarket loss despite CEO Elon Musk's previous stock sale.

title: Tesla Erases $199 Billion in Worst Two-Day Rout in 14 Months
summary: Tesla Inc. experienced its worst two-day selloff in 14 months, shedding approximately $199 billion in market value. This decline followed Elon Musk's Twitter poll about selling 10% of his stake and news that his brother, Kimbal Musk, sold shares prior to the poll. Additionally, a report emerged about Michael Burry suggesting Musk might need to sell stocks to cover personal debts.

title: Cadillac is dropping hundreds of dealers who aren’t ready for electric cars
summary: Cadillac is significantly reducing its number of dealerships, expecting only 560 US locations by the end of the year, a 40% drop over three years. This move is part of General Motors' plan for Cadillac to become mostly electric by 2030, with GM spending $274 million to buy out dealers unprepared for the shift. The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) requires substantial investment from dealers and comes as GM aims to compete more directly with Tesla in the booming EV market.

title: Elon Musk’s Net Worth Has Plunged $50 Billion in 2 Days
summary: Elon Musk's net worth has dropped by $50 billion in two days following a significant plunge in Tesla shares. This decline, the largest two-day fall on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, was influenced by Musk's Twitter poll about selling his stock, his brother's pre-poll stock sale, and a report suggesting Musk might need to sell shares to cover personal debts. Despite the substantial loss, Musk's fortune is still up 70% for the year, and Tesla's market capitalization remains over $1 trillion.

title: 3 Solid Climate Tech Funds for Investors
summary: The article discusses the burgeoning climate tech investment sector, highlighting the volatility and concentration of publicly traded companies in the space. It recommends three funds—GMO Climate Change III, New Alternatives, and SPDR Kensho Clean Power ETF—for investors interested in climate technology, advising caution and diversification due to the sector's risks.

title: Amazon And Other Big Winners In Rivian’s Supercharged IPO
summary: Rivian's anticipated IPO is set to be the largest of 2021, showcasing significant investor confidence in the electric vehicle market despite Rivian being largely pre-revenue. Major stakeholders like Amazon, T. Rowe Price, Global Oryx Company Ltd., Ford Motor Co., and Manheim Investments are poised for substantial financial gains from the public offering. Their investments, primarily made in the past few years, reflect a strong bet on the future of electric transportation.

title: Tesla shares skid again as investors brace for possible Musk stock sale
summary: Tesla shares experienced their largest daily fall in 14 months, wiping out nearly $200 billion in market capitalization, amid concerns over a potential stock sale by Elon Musk. The sell-off followed Musk's Twitter poll asking if he should sell 10% of his stake, with a majority supporting the sale. This potential sale could help Musk address a federal tax bill of approximately $11 billion related to exercising stock options.

title: Investors Can Now Short ARK Invest via SARK ETF
summary: The Tuttle Capital Short Innovation ETF (SARK) has launched, allowing investors to bet against Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK). SARK is an actively managed inverse ETF, rebalanced daily, offering a way for more speculative investors to short ARKK without the direct risks of individual short selling. This new ETF caters to those who believe the bull thesis for transformational industries might be stretched or wish to hedge existing high-growth portfolios.

title: China vehicle sales fall 9.4% in October - industry body
summary: China's auto sales decreased by 9.4% in October compared to the previous year, marking the sixth consecutive month of decline due to a global semiconductor shortage impacting production. Despite the overall downturn, sales of new energy vehicles (NEVs) surged by 135% in October, reaching 383,000 units, supported by government initiatives to promote greener transportation. Key EV manufacturers like Tesla, Nio, Xpeng, and Volkswagen reported their sales figures for the month, indicating a strong performance in the NEV segment amid eased chip supply in Q4.

title: Hertz Relists on NASDAQ Global Select Market as HTZ
summary: Hertz Global Holdings Inc. has relisted its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker HTZ, following its emergence from bankruptcy earlier this year. Shareholder sold 44.5 million shares in an upsized public offering, though Hertz itself did not receive proceeds and plans to repurchase $300 million worth of shares. The company is also focusing on electric vehicles, with plans to acquire 100,000 Teslas and rent 50,000 EVs to Uber.

title: Six Major Automakers Agree to End Gas Car Sales Globally by 2040
summary: Six major automakers, including Ford, GM, and Mercedes-Benz, along with 30 nations, have signed a non-binding pledge at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP26) to end the sale of new gas and diesel-powered cars globally by 2040, and by 2035 in "leading markets." Notably, the US, China, and Japan, as well as major automakers like Toyota and Volkswagen, did not sign the agreement. The pledge aims for 100 percent zero-emission new car and van sales, encompassing both electric and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles.

title: Rivian valued at over $100 bln in debut, after world's biggest IPO of 2021
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc surged over 50% in its Nasdaq debut, reaching a market valuation exceeding $100 billion after the world's largest IPO of 2021, and becoming the second most valuable U.S. automaker after Tesla. Despite limited revenue, the Amazon-backed EV maker is investing heavily in production and plans to expand globally, with its CEO emphasizing growth into new segments and vehicles. General Motors' CEO noted that Rivian's valuation highlighted her company's undervaluation.

title: 26-Year-Old Alex Rodrigues Becomes Youngest Current CEO Of A Publicly Traded Company With $5 Billion Embark SPAC Merger
summary: Alex Rodrigues, at 26, has become the youngest current CEO of a publicly traded company after his autonomous trucking software company, Embark, went public via a $5 billion SPAC merger. Rodrigues, who developed a self-driving golf cart at 19, founded Embark to focus on 18-wheelers, aiming to revolutionize the trucking industry. He is estimated to be worth $500 million and lives a minimalist lifestyle, focused on growing Embark, which aims to fulfill over 14,200 reservations for Embark-enabled trucks by 2024.

title: 26-Year-Old CEO Takes His Autonomous Truck Company Public in $5 Billion Deal
summary: Embark Trucks, led by 26-year-old CEO Alex Rodrigues, has gone public on the Nasdaq under the ticker EMBK in a $5 billion deal. Rodrigues is now one of the youngest heads of an autonomous-driving company to navigate the public market. The initial market reception was cool, with shares falling as much as 7.3% in the first minute of trading.

title: ‘Next Tesla’ Tag Takes Rivian (RIVN) to $90 Billion Value Without Sales
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc. achieved a market value of over $100 billion just two days after its IPO, leading to comparisons with Tesla. However, unlike Tesla, which had $93 million in revenue when it went public in 2010, Rivian reported over $1 billion in losses for the first half of the year and had no sales. The rapid valuation is attributed to backing from Amazon and Ford.

title: Tesla dips after Musk sheds $5 billion in shares
summary: Tesla's stock dipped slightly after CEO Elon Musk sold approximately $5 billion worth of his shares, following a Twitter poll about offloading 10% of his stake. This sale, his first since 2016, included shares sold to cover tax obligations after exercising options and comes amid proposals for taxing billionaires' stock holdings. Despite the sale, analysts believe it won't negatively impact long-term investors, as Musk's compensation is largely stock-based.

title: We Bought a 2021 Tesla Model Y
summary: Cars.com purchased a 2021 Tesla Model Y Long Range All-Wheel Drive to serve as a long-term test vehicle, focusing on the optional three-row, seven-seat configuration. The article details the ordering process, the specific features chosen (including the Deep Blue Metallic Paint and tow hitch), total cost, and the delivery experience, which was largely contactless. The team plans to evaluate its real-world performance, charging capabilities, and the impact of its evolving over-the-air updates over the next couple of years.

title: “미국 경기 향후 5년 호황 국면, SPY·INDA·VNQ ETF로 자산 증식하라”
summary: 대신증권 문남중 수석연구위원은 향후 5년간 미국 경제가 호황을 맞을 것으로 전망하며 ETF 투자를 통한 자산 증식을 제안했다. 그는 한국 증시의 투자 난이도가 높아질 것이라며, SPY, INDA, VNQ와 같은 ETF를 활용해 분산 투자하고, 2026년 9월까지 미국 중심의 위험자산 비중을 높여야 한다고 강조했다. 또한, 메타버스 및 우주항공 산업 관련 ETF를 장기 유망 투자처로 추천했다.

title: Tesla's Musk sold another $1.2 bln of stock on Nov. 12-filing
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk sold 1.2 million shares from his trust on November 12, 2021, for over $1.2 billion. This sale adds to previous multi-billion dollar stock disposals by Musk reported earlier in the week. The transactions were revealed in U.S. securities filings made public on Friday.

title: Elon Musk sells another $1.2 billion in Tesla stocks
summary: Elon Musk sold an additional 1.2 million shares of Tesla stock on Friday, bringing his total sales for the week to 6.4 million shares, valued at $6.9 billion. This marks his first stock sale since 2016 and followed a Twitter poll where he asked followers if he should sell 10% of his shares. The sales, intended to cover tax obligations, led to Tesla's worst weekly stock performance in 20 months, though shares remain up 46% year-to-date.

title: Under Honda CEO Toshihiro Mibe's radical vision, will company be recognizable in 20 years?
summary: Honda CEO Toshihiro Mibe has a radical vision for the company's future, stating that "Honda will not be an automotive company anymore." This suggests a significant transformation that could make the company unrecognizable in two decades. The article, penned by Hans Greimel, explores the implications of Mibe's strategic direction.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Kyle Bass, Ken Griffin, Elliott Management, Soros Fund Management, Sachem Head Capital Management, Renaissance Technologies, Regional Management Corp. (RM), Aon PLC (AON), and More
summary: This article covers recent hedge fund activities, including Renaissance Technologies quadrupling its Tesla stake and boosting its AMC bet, Kyle Bass's skepticism about Bitcoin's future due to regulation, and Soros Fund Management's increased investments in real estate and financial stocks. It also details Elliott Management securing board seats at Duke Energy and Sachem Head Capital Management's strong performance.

title: 2023 Mazda CX-50: Another One Invites the Dust
summary: Mazda introduces the 2023 CX-50, an off-road-themed SUV designed for outdoor enthusiasts. It will offer naturally aspirated or turbocharged 2.5-liter four-cylinder engines, standard AWD, and Mazda Intelligent Drive Select for various driving modes. The CX-50 features a rugged exterior, a modern Mazda interior, and reinforced elements for carrying outdoor gear, with more details including pricing expected closer to its spring 2022 launch.

title: 'The Big Short' investor Michael Burry sold most of his US stocks last quarter — but added 3 new holdings
summary: Michael Burry dramatically reduced his US stock holdings in the third quarter, cutting his portfolio from over 20 to just six positions, aligning with his long-standing predictions of a market crash. His Scion Asset Management firm added new stakes in Lockheed Martin, Now, and Scynexis, while divesting from major tech companies and bearish options on Tesla and the Ark Innovation ETF. This move follows his consistent warnings about an epic bubble in asset prices and an impending historic market downturn.

title: VinFast VF e36 unveiled as electric seven-seat SUV
summary: Vietnamese car-maker VinFast is introducing its new VF e36, a seven-seat electric SUV, at the LA Auto Show, targeting the US and European markets. This flagship model, previously known as the VF33, is similar in length to a BMW X7 and is powered by a dual electric motor setup producing 402bhp with a 106kWh battery, expected to offer a range of nearly 350 miles. Styled by Pininfarina, the VF e36 features a large infotainment screen, minimal physical controls, and an array of sensors for Level 3 autonomous driving.

title: Conductive carbon additives: energise the future
summary: Cabot Corporation's Senior Business Development Manager, Paolina Atanassova, discusses how their extensive range of conductive carbon additives is supporting lithium-ion battery applications. The article highlights Cabot's commitment to sustainability and innovation in battery materials, including their LITX Carbon Black and ENERMAX™ carbon nanotubes, to meet the growing demands of the automotive and energy storage industries. It also touches upon their R&D commitment and collaborative efforts to develop next-generation battery technologies.

title: JPMorgan files $162 million lawsuit against Tesla over warrants, citing Musk tweet
summary: JPMorgan Chase has filed a $162 million lawsuit against Tesla, alleging breach of contract over stock warrants. The lawsuit stems from Elon Musk's 2018 tweet about taking Tesla private at $420, which JPMorgan claims significantly decreased the value of the warrants. JPMorgan asserts Tesla flagrantly ignored its contractual obligation to pay when the warrants expired.

title: New VinFast VF e35 electric SUV revealed as Tesla Model Y rival
summary: Vietnamese brand VinFast is set to debut its new VF e35 electric SUV at the LA Auto Show, targeting rivals like the Volkswagen ID.4 and Tesla Model Y. Designed by Pininfarina, the VF e35 will offer a range of up to 250 miles and level 3 autonomous driving capabilities, with deliveries expected to begin next year. The vehicle aims to be competitively priced in Western markets.

title: Lucid (LCID) Stock Forecast: Next $100 Billion Company After Rivian?
summary: Lucid Motors (LCID) has seen a significant stock increase following its debut Air model deliveries and positive developments like winning "MotorTrend’s 2022 Car of the Year" and having the longest battery range. Analysts are generally positive, with Bank of America doubling its target price to $60. The article explores whether Lucid could follow Rivian in reaching a $100 billion market capitalization, citing factors like vehicle performance, battery technology, and management team as advantages.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Cliff Asness, Bill Ackman, Dan Sundheim, Viking Global Investors, Engine No. 1, Commscope Holding Company Inc (COMM), Tesla Inc (TSLA), and More
summary: This article covers recent activities and news involving prominent hedge fund managers and companies. It discusses AQR Capital Management's resource cuts, Bill Ackman's penthouse project, D1 Capital and Viking Global's significant investments in Peloton, Melvin Capital's portfolio shake-up, and Elon Musk's response to Tesla critic Michael Burry.

title: Crypto Mining for Digital Gold is Going Green
summary: The article discusses the environmental concerns surrounding cryptocurrency mining, particularly Bitcoin, and highlights efforts within the industry to adopt renewable energy sources. It addresses misconceptions about electricity consumption, comparing it to other industries and countries, and details initiatives like the Crypto Climate Accord aimed at decarbonizing the sector. The piece concludes that while environmental sustainability standards are still evolving, crypto mining companies are progressing towards greener operations.

title: JPMorgan sues Tesla for $162 mln after Musk tweets soured warrant deal
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co is suing Tesla Inc for $162.2 million, alleging breach of contract related to warrants Tesla sold to the bank in 2014. The dispute stems from JPMorgan's re-pricing of these warrants following Elon Musk's 2018 tweets about taking Tesla private, which created significant stock volatility. JPMorgan claims Tesla failed to honor its contractual obligations to pay after the warrants expired and Tesla's stock price surged.

title: Taking Charge: Mary Powell on her new gig at Sunrun and the importance of ‘radical collaboration’
summary: Mary Powell discusses her new role as CEO of Sunrun and emphasizes the need for "radical collaboration" to accelerate the energy transition and combat climate change. She highlights lessons from her previous role at Green Mountain Power, focusing on the scalability of distributed energy resources and the cultural shift required from utilities to view these resources as opportunities rather than threats. Powell expresses optimism about the future, noting that existing technologies are sufficient and that the industry is approaching a tipping point for clean energy.

title: Focus: With limited EV options, Uber embraces carbon offsets in Latin America
summary: Uber, aiming for carbon neutrality by 2040, is utilizing carbon offsets in parts of Latin America due to the impracticality of transitioning drivers to electric vehicles in nascent EV markets. This strategy is controversial and raises questions about the genuine impact of the offset projects Uber supports. The company faces challenges in these emerging markets with limited sustainable alternatives, despite plans to encourage EV adoption.

title: Lucid Motors CEO expects to catch up to Tesla’s $1 trillion valuation in the future
summary: Lucid Group CEO Peter Rawlinson believes his electric car company can eventually achieve a valuation similar to Tesla, stating that "the sky's the limit" if Lucid successfully executes its plans and scales production. Lucid's current market cap of $89.87 billion has already surpassed Ford, but it remains significantly below Tesla's over $1 trillion valuation. Rawlinson remains optimistic after the Lucid Air won MotorTrend's 2022 Car of the Year award, despite the company still being in the early stages of vehicle production.

title: Global Market Report - 18 November
summary: This global market report for November 18, 2021, details a projected lower opening for the ASX following Wall Street's decline, driven by disappointing retail earnings and concerns over interest rates and competition. It also covers mixed performances in Asian and European markets, with an emphasis on US retail struggles despite a strong earnings season, and the broader economic implications of inflation and supply chain issues.

title: Hertz to raise $1.5 bln in first debt issue since bankruptcy exit
summary: Hertz Global Holdings Inc. plans to raise $1.5 billion through a senior notes offering, marking its first debt issuance since exiting bankruptcy in June. The proceeds will be used to repurchase preferred stock, with the unsecured notes maturing in 2026 and 2029. This follows their recent large order for Tesla electric rental cars, which initially boosted Tesla's stock before some gains were pared.

title: China's WeRide to launch robotaxis on GAC's Ontime ride-hailing app
summary: Chinese autonomous driving startup WeRide announced plans to make its robotaxis available on Guangzhou Automobile Group's Ontime ride-hailing app by next year. Backed by Nissan Motor, WeRide will offer public test rides at the Guangzhou Auto Show. This move is part of a broader investment trend by automakers and tech firms in autonomous driving technology.

title: Stock of the week - Rivian Automotive (18.11.2021)
summary: Rivian Automotive, the US electric vehicles manufacturer, had its IPO on November 10th, with shares gaining 120% in the first 5 days before dropping 15%. Despite $0 revenue, the company achieved a significant market cap, briefly becoming the third largest automaker. Comparisons are drawn between Rivian's cash burn and early Tesla, with Rivian burning cash at a faster rate but benefiting from a massive order from Amazon.

title: Apple is one step closer to developing fully automated vehicles
summary: Apple is accelerating the development of its electric car project, codenamed "Project Titan," with a renewed focus on achieving full self-driving capabilities that require no human intervention. Kevin Lynch, the new leader of the car team, is pushing for a 2025 launch for a fully autonomous vehicle, equipped with an advanced internally designed chip and a hands-off driving interior. This initiative marks a significant shift in strategy for Apple's long-running and often turbulent car project, aiming to tackle a major technical challenge within the auto industry.

title: NVIDIA CEO Receives Semiconductor Industry’s Top Honor
summary: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, was awarded the Semiconductor Industry Association's (SIA) highest honor, the Robert N. Noyce award, for his pioneering work in accelerated computing. The award ceremony highlighted NVIDIA's significant impact on the industry and AI development. Huang shared his journey from early programming to founding NVIDIA and his vision for advanced computing applications like Earth-2 for climate science.

title: Global X signals intent in Europe with seven thematic ETF launches
summary: Global X has launched seven new thematic ETFs in Europe, expanding its UCITS range to 12 products. These ETFs cover various themes including autonomous vehicles, clean tech, cybersecurity, e-commerce, fintech, IoT, and robotics/AI, with TERs ranging from 0.50% to 0.60%. This move signifies Global X's robust growth and commitment to offering targeted exposure to disruptive global themes for European investors.

title: Best Funds in Fidelity's Sweet Spot
summary: This article identifies five top-performing large-growth funds from Fidelity's extensive lineup, highlighting their management styles and investment strategies. It distinguishes between "style-pure" and "wide-ranging growth" funds, discussing how experienced managers and their approaches contribute to the funds' success despite varying market conditions and asset bases. The piece provides a guide for investors navigating Fidelity's growth-oriented offerings.

title: Ford, GM Step Into Chip Business
summary: Detroit's two largest car companies, Ford and General Motors, are venturing into the semiconductor business in response to the ongoing global chip shortage that has hampered their production. Ford has signed a strategic agreement with GlobalFoundries Inc. to develop chips, potentially leading to joint U.S. production. This move reflects a broader reevaluation of the automotive supply chain by manufacturers.

title: Xpeng goes up against Tesla’s Model Y, Nio with new G9 SUV
summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer Xpeng Inc. has unveiled its new G9 SUV, marking its fourth production model. The G9 is designed to compete directly with Tesla's Model Y and Nio's ES series, targeting both domestic and international markets. The vehicle boasts compatibility with Xpeng's advanced charging network, capable of adding 200 kilometers of range in just five minutes.

title: Global X Blockchain ETF Up Nearly 50% YTD
summary: The Global X Blockchain ETF (BKCH) has seen significant growth in 2021, rising nearly 50% year-to-date due to the rally in cryptocurrencies and increasing interest in blockchain technology. The ETF provides exposure to companies involved in blockchain, such as Marathon Digital Holdings and Coinbase, and is poised to benefit from the global expansion and adoption of blockchain in various sectors. Looking ahead to 2022, trends like increased business investment and a focus on "greenifying" blockchain are expected to further drive the sector's growth.

title: Smart Roads and Intelligent Infrastructure in Connected Urban Transport
summary: This article explores the concept of smart roads and intelligent infrastructure, detailing how digital technologies are transforming traditional transportation. It covers various smart road technologies such as energy harvesting, automatic truck weighing, electrified roads, and V2X communication, explaining their functionalities and benefits. The piece also discusses the critical challenges and sustainability impacts of adopting these advanced systems in urban environments.

title: Samsung Reportedly Picks Texas for $17 Billion U.S. Semiconductor Plant
summary: Samsung Electronics has reportedly chosen Taylor, Texas, for its new $17 billion advanced U.S. chip plant, located about 30 miles from its existing Austin facility. This decision aligns with the Biden administration's focus on supply chain security and increasing domestic semiconductor manufacturing. The new plant is expected to create 1,800 jobs and bolsters Samsung's efforts to compete with TSMC and Intel in meeting surging global chip demand.

title: Tesla China Plant Nearing Capacity Spurs $188 Million Upgrade
summary: Tesla Inc. is planning a $188 million investment to upgrade its Shanghai Gigafactory as the plant approaches its current production capacity limit. The factory, which had an annual production capacity of 450,000 vehicles as of 2020, is expected to reach this limit by the end of the year. This upgrade will allow Tesla to continue increasing its output in China.

title: 2022 Mercedes-EQ EQS: 6 Things We Like and 4 We Don’t
summary: The 2022 Mercedes-EQ EQS is Mercedes-Benz's new luxury electric flagship, launching in EQS450 Plus and EQS580 4Matic variants. This article details six commendable features, including impressive powertrains, refined ride, rear steering, quick charging, advanced Hyperscreen, and augmented reality, while also highlighting four drawbacks such as tough brakes, potential big screen issues, missing luxury touches, and limited interior room compared to the S-Class.

title: A*STAR's IME & Stmicroelectronics Team Up On Silicon Carbide R&D For Ev Market, Industrial Applications
summary: A*STAR's Institute of Microelectronics (IME) and STMicroelectronics have announced a research and development collaboration to advance silicon carbide (SiC) technology for power electronics in electric vehicles and industrial applications. This partnership aims to develop and optimize SiC integrated devices and package modules to improve performance, establish a SiC ecosystem in Singapore, and support STMicroelectronics' global R&D efforts. The collaboration builds on IME's expertise in wide bandgap materials and will contribute to sustainable mobility and energy efficiency.

title: Firms beef up retirement benefits to attract and retain employees
summary: Firms are enhancing retirement benefits to attract and retain employees, as highlighted by KPMG's more generous match being a key differentiator. The article also touches on related topics such as the SEC's delayed work on private credit in 401(k) plans due to government shutdown, investment strategies of university endowments, private equity AUM growth, and CalPERS' voting stance on executive pay packages.

title: Suppliers flail as auto makers, dealers set profit records
summary: In 2021, while automakers and dealerships achieved record profits, their suppliers struggled. This situation highlights a disparity in economic performance within the automotive industry, where different segments experience contrasting fortunes. The article, published in November 2021, indicates that suppliers are not sharing in the success of manufacturers and dealers.

title: Kelly Roofing Publishes White Paper on Tesla Solar Roofs
summary: Kelly Roofing, the 2019 Residential Contractor of the Year, has become a successful Tesla Certified Installer, selling over $12 million in Tesla Solar Roofs in under a year. The company released a white paper detailing its experience and providing guidance for other contractors interested in becoming certified installers for Tesla's solar products. Kelly Roofing attributes its success and recognition as the 2021 Innovator of the Year to its partnership with Tesla, highlighting a "paradigm shift" in roof sales where customers choose replacement for desire rather than necessity.

title: Ford to outsell GM in electric vehicles — but not for long
summary: Ford is projected to temporarily surpass General Motors in U.S. electric vehicle sales for 2021, primarily due to strong Mustang Mach-E sales and a production halt for the Chevrolet Bolt. While Ford aims to double its original EV production plan and become a leading EV maker, GM is investing heavily in EV technology and battery plants, asserting its goal to dominate the EV market in the long term. Both companies are making significant investments to compete with Tesla, which currently holds a substantial lead in the EV market.

title: Ford, GM race to brag 'We're Number 3!' in electric vehicle market
summary: General Motors and Ford are intensifying their long-standing rivalry, this time competing for market share in the electric vehicle industry. While Tesla and Volkswagen Group are projected to remain the top two global EV leaders, GM and Ford are vying for third best. Production forecasts suggest that Stellantis might emerge as a surprise contender for the third spot, potentially surpassing Ford in EV output by 2025.

title: Stellantis CEO says EV cost burden is 'beyond the limits' for automakers
summary: Stellantis CEO Carlos Tavares stated that the financial burden of accelerating electric vehicle (EV) production is "beyond the limits" for automakers, potentially threatening jobs and vehicle quality. He warned that the 50% additional cost of EVs over conventional vehicles cannot be passed on to consumers and that rushed development could lead to quality problems. Stellantis aims to achieve significant productivity gains to manage these costs, while also investing heavily in EV development.

title: How the new SARK ETF lets investors bet against disruptive tech companies
summary: The newly launched SARK ETF allows investors to bet against disruptive, often unprofitable, technology companies, similar to those held by Cathie Wood's ARKK ETF. Matthew Tuttle of Tuttle Capital Management explains that SARK acts as an inverse ETF for innovative tech, providing a hedge for portfolios, especially in a rising-interest-rate and volatile market environment. He also discusses other investment opportunities like real estate and cryptocurrencies, noting that SARK is the first ETF of its kind to offer inverse exposure to another specific ETF.

title: ACES Covers Battery Bases
summary: The article highlights the ALPS Clean Energy ETF (ACES) for its broad exposure to the renewable energy ecosystem, particularly its significant allocation to electric vehicle and energy storage companies. It emphasizes the critical role of battery storage in future growth, citing Goldman Sachs' projections for substantial market expansion. Key holdings like Tesla, Enphase Energy, and Stem underscore ACES' focus on leading players in the battery storage sector.

title: Apple loses a top vehicle engineer to flying-taxi startup Archer Aviation
summary: Michael Schwekutsch, a top vehicle engineer previously with Apple's "Project Titan" electric vehicle initiative, has joined Archer Aviation, a startup focused on building flying taxis. His departure comes as Apple tries to accelerate its self-driving car project, sparking discussions among analysts about Apple Car's potential impact on the broader EV market, particularly on Tesla.

title: The FAANG Market Is Fading
summary: The article discusses the fading hyper-concentration of stock market returns from a handful of large technology stocks, particularly the FAANGs, in 2021 compared to 2020. This shift suggests a healthier market dynamic with less risk for index funds and more opportunities for stock-pickers. While large stocks still contribute significantly, their overall impact on market returns has decreased, resembling a more traditional market distribution.

title: Tesla officially moves headquarters to site of new Austin factory
summary: Tesla has officially moved its corporate headquarters from Palo Alto, California, to Austin, Texas, to the same site where it is building its new $1.1 billion manufacturing facility. Documents filed with the SEC confirmed the relocation to 13101 Harold Green Road in Austin. This move follows CEO Elon Musk's announcement in October and reflects the company's growth limitations in the San Francisco Bay Area and the increasing presence of Musk's other ventures in Central Texas.

title: SCE Quadruples Rebate Offer for Pre-Owned EVs
summary: Southern California Edison (SCE) has quadrupled its rebate for income-qualified customers purchasing or leasing pre-owned electric vehicles, increasing it from $1,000 to $4,000. This initiative aims to make clean transportation more accessible and affordable, particularly for those in income-qualified households or on state/federal assistance programs, thereby stimulating EV adoption to help California meet its climate goals. The rebate program is available to the first, second, and third owners or lessors of pre-owned EVs, and customers can apply online.

title: Solar ETF Is Credible Avenue to Battery Storage Boom
summary: The article highlights the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) as a compelling investment avenue for the burgeoning battery storage market. It explains that several solar companies within TAN's holdings are making significant advancements in battery storage, which Goldman Sachs projects will see substantial growth over the next decade. Major components of TAN, Enphase Energy (ENPH) and SolarEdge Technologies (SDGE), are identified as key beneficiaries of this trend.

title: Why Biden won’t talk about Tesla
summary: President Biden rarely mentions Tesla Inc. and Elon Musk, an omission analysts link to the administration's pro-union stance and Tesla's anti-union policies. Biden frequently praises traditional automakers like Ford and General Motors for their EV initiatives, while conspicuously excluding Tesla from events and discussions despite its leading role in electric vehicle production. This snub has intensified scrutiny from Tesla fans and Musk himself, highlighting a divide between the administration's labor focus and the tech-bro ethos associated with Tesla.

title: Elon Musk’s Tesla Share Sales Pass $10 Billion
summary: Elon Musk has sold over $10 billion worth of Tesla shares, primarily to cover taxes related to exercising stock options. These sales come after he polled Twitter users about offloading 10% of his stake and coincide with Tesla's headquarters moving from California to tax-friendlier Texas, potentially helping him reduce his tax burden by over $2 billion.

title: Cathie Wood's flagship Ark fund plummets 7% as tech sell-off deepens
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) experienced a significant downturn, falling 7.3% to its lowest point in over a year, with a year-to-date decline of 25%. This slump is attributed to a broader tech stock sell-off fueled by inflation fears and concerns over the Omicron variant. Conversely, the Tuttle Capital Short Innovation ETF (SARK), designed to gain inverse exposure to ARKK, saw a 6% increase.

title: Ford aims to be world's #2 electric vehicle maker within two years - COO
summary: Ford Motor Co. expects to become the world's second-largest electric vehicle manufacturer within two years, targeting an annual production capacity of nearly 600,000 EVs. This ambition is fueled by strong demand for its F-150 Lightning pickup and plans for greater vertical integration of EV components and battery production. Ford is also developing various battery technologies with multiple global suppliers to reduce costs.

title: Showcasing Wipro’s Capabilities in the Autonomous Vehicle Industry
summary: Wipro outlines its capabilities and projects in the autonomous vehicle industry, highlighting the sector's rapid evolution, key technical enablers, and market dynamics. The article details Wipro's workflow improvement initiatives and forthcoming services, including a driverless car simulator. It also touches upon market drivers, constraints, opportunities, and challenges within the VUCA nature of the autonomous vehicle industry.

title: Two ETFs to Consider for the Electric Vehicle Push
summary: The trillion-dollar infrastructure package is expected to boost electric vehicle (EV) adoption by funding charging stations, creating opportunities for EV-focused ETFs. This article highlights two ETFs: the Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV), which offers direct exposure to EV development, and the Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT), which provides a "backdoor" play on rising lithium prices due to increased demand. Both funds have shown positive performance in 2021, with LIT also serving as a potential hedge against inflation.

title: Hertz Is Getting Over $100 a Day for Tesla Rentals, Analyst Estimates
summary: Hertz is reportedly charging over $100 per day for Tesla rentals, indicating a significant premium for customers opting for electric vehicles. An analyst estimates these healthy rental rates for Teslas within Hertz's fleet. The company previously announced plans for Teslas to constitute more than 20% of its rental-car fleet by the end of next year.

title: Lucid Motors drops as luxury electric vehicle maker receives SEC subpoena
summary: Lucid Group's shares dropped significantly after the luxury electric vehicle maker announced it received a subpoena from the SEC. The investigation appears to focus on the company's business combination with Atieva, Inc. and certain projections made prior to its multi-billion SPAC deal earlier in the year. Lucid Motors is cooperating fully with the SEC's review.

title: EV maker Lucid gets SEC subpoena on $24-billion blank-check deal
summary: The U.S. securities regulator has issued a subpoena to Lucid Group Inc regarding its $24-billion blank-check merger, causing its shares to drop significantly. This action places Lucid among a growing number of companies, particularly EV makers, facing scrutiny from regulators over their SPAC deals amidst a rush to production and past incidents of alleged fraud.

title: EV maker Lucid gets SEC subpoena on $24-bln blank-check deal
summary: Luxury EV maker Lucid Group Inc received a subpoena from the U.S. SEC regarding its $24 billion blank-check merger with Churchill Capital Corp IV. This investigation, which appears to concern the business combination and certain projections, caused Lucid's shares to fall by nearly 20%. The scrutiny on SPAC deals has intensified, especially for EV manufacturers, following similar issues with companies like Nikola and Lordstown Motors.

title: TVA says Tennesseans are ready to make the switch to electric vehicles
summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) projects a significant increase in electric vehicles (EVs) on Tennessee roads, from 15,000 to 200,000 in the next six years, highlighting the growing demand for charging stations. According to TVA's Travis Reid, Tennesseans are prepared for the transition, treating EVs like cell phones for overnight charging. The TVA also plans to strategically place charging stations every 50 miles along Tennessee interstates to support longer road trips and estimates drivers could save $1,000 annually by switching to EVs.

title: Exclusive: SEC probes Tesla over whistleblower claims on solar panel defects
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has initiated an investigation into Tesla Inc. regarding a whistleblower complaint that the company failed to inform shareholders and the public about fire risks associated with solar panel system defects. The probe follows a complaint from a former Tesla field quality manager, Steven Henkes, who alleged that Tesla and SolarCity concealed "liability and exposure to property damage, risk of injury of users, fire etc to shareholders." Tesla's shares fell significantly following the Reuters report.

title: U.S. says Nvidia-Arm deal harms market for networking, self-driving car chips
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has argued that Nvidia's $80 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. would harm competition in emerging markets for self-driving car chips and data processing units. The FTC believes that chip companies relying on Arm would hesitate to work closely with it due to fears of Nvidia accessing their product plans. Nvidia maintains the deal will benefit the industry and promote competition against Intel's x86 architecture.

title: Intel plans to take self-driving car unit public in the U.S. in mid-2022
summary: Intel announced its plan to take its self-driving car unit, Mobileye, public in the U.S. in mid-2022 through an IPO. Intel acquired Mobileye for $15.3 billion in 2017, and the IPO is expected to value Mobileye at over $50 billion, creating value for Intel shareholders who will remain majority owners. This move aims to give Mobileye more visibility and help fund Intel's expansion plans, including building new chip plants.

title: Elon Musk slams Biden’s agenda, dismisses EV tax credits
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Inc., has criticized President Biden's economic agenda, particularly the proposed $1.7 trillion reconciliation bill. Musk urged the Senate to reject the bill, arguing that the U.S. government spends too much and that electric vehicle tax credits are unnecessary, including the infrastructure for EV charging. He also called for the removal of all subsidies, including those for oil and gas.

title: Electrifying school buses will benefit local economy and children’s health
summary: This article advocates for the electrification of school buses, highlighting the significant health benefits for children and communities by reducing diesel exhaust exposure and air pollution. It also emphasizes the economic advantages, including job creation in manufacturing electric buses and reduced operational costs for school districts. The authors urge Congress, state leaders, and school districts to invest in this transition, citing initiatives like the Clean Commute for Kids Act, which would provide funding for zero-emission buses, especially in communities heavily impacted by climate change.

title: Stellantis Targets ~€20 Billion in Incremental Annual Revenues by 2030 Driven by Software-Enabled Vehicles
summary: Stellantis announced its software strategy aiming to generate approximately €20 billion in incremental annual revenues by 2030, driven by software-enabled product offerings and subscriptions. The company plans to invest over €30 billion through 2025 to transform its software and electrification capabilities, projecting 34 million monetizable connected cars by 2030. This strategy includes deploying three new AI-powered technology platforms (STLA Brain, STLA SmartCockpit, STLA AutoDrive) starting in 2024 and expanding strategic partnerships with companies like Foxconn and Waymo.

title: What's Inside the 4 Largest Clean Energy ETFs
summary: This article examines the four largest clean energy ETFs in the United States, highlighting the diverse approaches their underlying indexes take to define clean energy and select stocks. It details how "clean energy" definitions vary, leading to different portfolio compositions, and reveals that many clean energy funds still have significant fossil-fuel exposure. The piece also notes that these funds often exhibit higher correlations to the technology sector than to traditional energy benchmarks.

title: Tested: 2021 Tesla Model S Plaid Is Absurdly Quick but Also Has a Few Key Flaws
summary: The 2021 Tesla Model S Plaid demonstrates unparalleled acceleration, achieving 0-60 mph in 2.1 seconds and a 9.4-second quarter-mile, matching hypercars. However, despite its impressive speed, it suffers from high-speed instability, inadequate brakes, and a poorly integrated steering yoke, making it less refined and confidence-inspiring at its limits than some competitors. The article highlights that while the Plaid delivers on ludicrous quickness and range, it falls short on overall driving experience and some of Tesla's 200 mph claims.

title: MP Materials to Build U.S. Magnet Factory, Enters Long-Term Supply Agreement with General Motors
summary: MP Materials announced it will construct a rare earth metal, alloy, and magnet manufacturing facility in Fort Worth, Texas. The company also secured a long-term agreement with General Motors to supply U.S.-sourced rare earth materials and magnets for EV motors, supporting over a dozen models using GM's Ultium Platform. This initiative aims to restore a fully integrated U.S. rare earth supply chain, with production expected to begin a gradual ramp-up in 2023 and the facility capable of powering approximately 500,000 EV motors annually.

title: Deere & Co. CEO tapped to serve on Ford's board of directors
summary: Ford Motor Co. announced a leadership reshuffling, including the appointment of John C. May, CEO of Deere & Co., to its board of directors. May's experience in transforming Deere into a "smart industrial company" with a focus on technology is seen as valuable to Ford's own technology-driven initiatives. Additionally, the automaker announced the retirement of Mitch Bainwol, chief government relations officer, effective December 31.

title: Ford Motor Co. beefs up tech strength with director known for global dominance
summary: Ford Motor Co. has elected John May, CEO of Deere & Co., to its board of directors, a move analysts say underscores Ford's commitment to technology and dominance in electric and autonomous vehicles. May's experience with Deere's technologically advanced agricultural equipment and successful resolution of a recent UAW strike are seen as valuable assets for Ford's own transformation and supply chain management. The appointment expands Ford's board to 15 members, though some observers noted the company's lack of progress in increasing female board representation compared to competitors like GM.

title: General Motors returns to rare earth magnets with two U.S. deals
summary: General Motors announced two deals to source rare earth magnets for its electric vehicles from new U.S.-based manufacturing facilities, marking a return to an industry it had largely abandoned. These agreements with MP Materials Inc. and Vacuumschmelze aim to domestically source EV materials for GM's Ultium platform by 2025, aligning with the Biden administration's push for U.S. EV supply chain investments. The move seeks to reduce reliance on China, which currently dominates rare earth production and magnet manufacturing.

title: Tesla drivers can play video games while driving. Federal safety regulators are asking why.
summary: Federal safety regulators are investigating Tesla after a recent over-the-air update allowed drivers to play video games on the vehicle's touchscreen while driving. This issue was brought to light by a retired journalist's complaint to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), raising concerns about distracted driving and Tesla's consistent pushing of safety boundaries, including with its Autopilot and "Full Self-Driving" features. NHTSA has confirmed it is discussing the feature with Tesla, highlighting distraction-affected crashes as a significant concern.

title: Will Tesla CEO Elon Musk join the Great Resignation?
summary: Elon Musk has joked about quitting his jobs to become a full-time influencer after offloading approximately $11.8 billion worth of Tesla stock over five weeks to pay taxes. His social media activity has previously caused market fluctuations and regulatory scrutiny. Tesla shares dropped 2.1% following his latest stock disposal, nearing bear-market territory.

title: How ConocoPhillips is opening an innovation treasure trove
summary: ConocoPhillips is fostering a culture of innovation, led by Director Liz Jolley, to drive success and adapt to a changing industry. The company utilizes its "Fuel" software platform to facilitate global collaboration, allowing employees to share ideas and adopt proven solutions. This approach has led to significant improvements in operations, cost reduction, and problem-solving across various business units worldwide.

title: GM CEO says making ventilators at Indiana factory changed the company culture
summary: GM CEO Mary Barra states that making ventilators at an Indiana factory during the COVID-19 pandemic significantly changed the company's culture, giving them confidence to accelerate other tasks like electric vehicle development. The experience also influenced GM's approach to securing raw materials for EV production as they transition away from internal combustion engines. Barra also hinted at a potential EV battery factory in Michigan and commented on GM's stock valuation compared to Tesla.

title: China’s Next Advance in Electric Vehicles Is a Used-Car Market
summary: China is seeing a significant increase in its used-car market, particularly in the electric vehicle (EV) segment. Efforts to build this market from the ground up are now showing results, with sales of pre-owned vehicles jumping 30% in the first ten months of the year, projected to hit 17 million units in 2021. This growth indicates a maturing EV ecosystem in China.

title: News | CoStar News Wins Eight Awards in Nation's Largest Real Estate Journalism Contest
summary: CoStar News received eight awards, including three gold medals, in the National Association of Real Estate Editors' annual competition, the largest real estate journalism contest in the U.S. Awards were given for breaking news, international reporting, economic analysis, and investigative journalism, recognizing the work of several CoStar staff writers for their insightful and detailed reporting. The contest judging panel included prominent national news organizations, highlighting the high caliber of CoStar News's contributions.

title: TeraWulf Is Attracting A-List Investors For Its Sustainable Bitcoin Solution
summary: TeraWulf, a company focused on environmentally-friendly Bitcoin mining, is attracting A-list investors due to its sustainable approach. Notable investors like Gwyneth Paltrow, Mindy Kaling, and Sara Foster have joined, supporting TeraWulf's goal of achieving 100% zero-carbon emissions in its operations by leveraging nuclear, hydro, and solar power. The company aims to address environmental concerns associated with cryptocurrency mining and is preparing for a public debut to expand its substantial mining capacity.

title: Toyota, lagging rivals, outlines plans to expand sales of electric vehicles. (Published 2021)
summary: Toyota, the world's largest carmaker, has announced plans to significantly expand its electric vehicle sales by 2030, aiming for battery-powered cars to account for one-third of global sales and all sales for its Lexus luxury brand in key markets. While acknowledging its slower adoption compared to rivals like Volkswagen and General Motors, Toyota emphasized its continued commitment to hybrids and fossil-fueled models, citing varying global infrastructure and customer preferences. The company plans to offer 30 battery-powered models and produce 3.5 million electric vehicles by the end of the decade, with the first electric SUV, the bZ4X, launching early next year.

title: Toyota commits $70 bln to bolster electrification, shares rally
summary: Toyota Motor Corp has committed 8 trillion yen ($70 billion) to electrify its automobiles by 2030, with half of this investment dedicated to developing a battery-electric vehicle (BEV) line-up. Despite this significant investment, Toyota anticipates BEV sales will reach 3.5 million vehicles annually by 2030, a figure lower than some rivals but still prompting a rally in Toyota's shares. The company maintains a multi-pronged carbon-reduction strategy, including hybrids and hydrogen-powered vehicles, and plans to introduce 30 BEV models by 2030.

title: EVs to capture 30% of China market in 2022, Lotus CEO Says
summary: The CEO of Lotus predicts that electric vehicles (EVs) will account for 30% of the Chinese market in 2022. This projection highlights the anticipated rapid growth and adoption of EVs in China. The article features the Lotus Evija electric hypercar as an example of EV development.

title: Tesla told France there was no sign of technical fault in Paris crash
summary: Tesla has informed the French government that it found no technical fault related to a fatal accident involving a Model 3 taxi in Paris, according to a government spokesman. The taxi company G7 has suspended its fleet of 37 Model 3 cars following the crash, which resulted in one death and 20 injuries, while the driver is under formal investigation for suspected manslaughter. French authorities are awaiting the outcome of a judicial investigation into the incident, which witnesses described as the car suddenly accelerating and hitting multiple objects and pedestrians.

title: Does Your Company Face Water-Related Investment Risk?
summary: This article highlights that water scarcity and quality pose significant environmental, social, and governance (ESG) challenges to businesses and economies, often underappreciated by investors compared to carbon risks. It explains how investors can assess water-related investment risk by looking at a company's water intensity and the location-specific water conditions where it operates, using tools like Sustainalytics' ESG Risk Rating and the WWF Water Risk Filter. The authors emphasize the need for better corporate disclosure on water usage to help investors make informed decisions, providing examples of companies like Entergy, Intel, and Tesla.

title: Musk says Tesla's Texas factory is $10 bln investment over time
summary: Elon Musk has stated that Tesla's new factory in Austin, Texas, represents an investment of over $10 billion over time. This facility is expected to create at least 20,000 direct jobs and 100,000 indirect jobs. The company recently moved its headquarters to Austin from California and is slated to receive significant local tax rebates for the plant.

title: Governor Kemp Welcomes Rivian for Single-Largest Economic Development Project in State History
summary: Governor Brian P. Kemp announced that Rivian Inc. will invest $5 billion to build an electric adventure vehicle manufacturing plant in Georgia, creating approximately 7,500 jobs. This project, located at the East Atlanta Megasite, represents the single-largest economic development project in the state's history and aims to produce up to 400,000 vehicles annually. The facility, set to begin production in 2024, will also support Rivian's research and development programs and contribute to the expansion of the U.S. electric vehicle industry.

title: GM to start shipping $113,000 electric Hummer pickups to customers
summary: General Motors is commencing customer deliveries of its GMC Hummer EV pickup, a significant step for the automaker and its electric vehicle strategy. The Hummer EV is the first vehicle to use GM's in-house developed Ultium platform, motors, and batteries, which will underpin many future GM electric vehicles. The initial "Edition 1" models are priced around $113,000, and reservations are fully booked for the next year.

title: Tesla faces investor lawsuit over Musk tweets on 10% stock sales
summary: Tesla is facing an investor lawsuit over CEO Elon Musk's social media posts, specifically a Twitter poll regarding stock sales that led to a significant drop in its stock prices. The lawsuit seeks access to internal documents to determine if Tesla and Musk violated a 2018 agreement with the U.S. securities regulator, which required company lawyers to pre-approve tweets with material information. This legal action follows a substantial decrease in Tesla shares after Musk proposed selling 10% of his stake.

title: Made in New Zealand - Model Y
summary: A Tesla Model Y owner questions why their VIN starts with '7,' typically indicating New Zealand as the country of origin, sparking a discussion among forum members about VIN country codes and Tesla's manufacturing locations. It is revealed that recent Model Y VINs starting with '7SA' no longer solely denote New Zealand but are a new manufacturer code assigned by Tesla since November 2021 for certain models, overriding traditional VIN interpretations. The discussion also touches on enthusiasts' desire for vehicles from new factories offering cutting-edge technology like single-piece rear castings and 4680 batteries.

title: A unicorn in South Burlington: Kyle Clark and BETA Technologies
summary: This article profiles Kyle Clark, CEO of BETA Technologies, an electric flight pioneer based in South Burlington, Vermont. Clark, a Harvard graduate and former professional hockey player, has developed electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, initially focusing on cargo and medical deliveries. The company has raised $400 million, is valued at $1.4 billion, and is building a 355,000-square-foot assembly site, with customers including the US Department of Defense, UPS, and United Therapeutics.

title: Indian-Origin CEO Gets $2.3 Billon Pay Package from Bill Gates Backed Energy Storage Co.
summary: Jagdeep Singh, the Indian-origin CEO of QuantumScape Corp., a US-based energy storage startup backed by Bill Gates, is set to receive a compensation package estimated at $2.3 billion, largely in company shares. This substantial pay package is being compared to Tesla CEO Elon Musk's compensation, which also primarily consisted of stock options. QuantumScape is developing advanced solid-state lithium-metal batteries for electric vehicles, with promising performance metrics such as fast charging and high energy density.

title: Tesla secures another order of electric semi trucks
summary: Karat Packaging has announced an order for 10 Tesla Semi trucks to electrify its logistics fleet, indicating continued demand for Tesla's electric Class 8 semis despite production delays. This order highlights Karat Packaging's commitment to environmentally friendly solutions and expanding its 3PL services. The timeline for delivery remains uncertain, especially as other major reservation holders like PepsiCo have conflicting expectations regarding their first deliveries.

title: Payne: Inside Lucid, Tesla's Silicon Valley EV arch-rival
summary: Lucid Motors, a new electric vehicle manufacturer based in California and led by ex-Tesla chief engineer Peter Rawlinson, is emerging as a significant competitor to Tesla. With a market capitalization of nearly $100 billion, Lucid aims to surpass Tesla with its high-performance Air sedan, boasting the industry's longest range and most efficient electric motors. The company is poised for growth with plans for an SUV, expanded production, and international market entry, although some analysts caution about the increasing saturation of the EV market.

title: Volta bets on space technology for battery storage fire prevention
summary: Energy storage developer Volta Energy Products has partnered with KULR Technology Group to integrate KULR's space technology-derived thermal safety solutions into battery storage units. This collaboration aims to prevent thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries, making energy storage safer and potentially less expensive by reducing the need for external fire suppression. The partnership marks the first application of KULR's passive propagation resistant (PPR) solution for energy storage, with Volta planning to deploy thousands of units incorporating this technology in the coming years.

title: A shift is underway in electronics manufacturing
summary: The electronics manufacturing services (EMS) sector is undergoing a significant transformation, evolving from outsourced production workhorses to strategic partners for brands and OEMs. EMS providers now offer diverse capabilities to help clients navigate complex challenges, drive resilience, innovation, speed to market, and sustainability. This partnership has become increasingly crucial, especially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, which necessitated reinvention and new operational approaches.

title: Tencent hands shareholders $16.4 bln windfall in the form of JD.com stake
summary: Tencent is distributing most of its $16.4 billion stake in JD.com as a dividend to shareholders, reducing its holding to 2.3% from 17%. This move comes amidst Beijing's regulatory crackdown on technology firms and is seen as an effort to weaken "walled gardens" and increase competition. While JD.com's shares plunged, Tencent's rose, and the companies will maintain a business relationship.

title: Tesla to stop games on infotainment screens in moving cars, NHTSA says
summary: Tesla will disable its "Passenger Play" feature, which allowed games to be played on infotainment screens while vehicles were in motion, following an investigation by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). This decision comes amidst concerns over potential driver distraction. The change will be implemented through an over-the-air software update.

title: Elon Musk says he is ‘almost done’ selling Tesla stock
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, announced he is "almost done" selling his Tesla stock, having offloaded over $15 billion worth of shares since early November. He stated that he sold enough to reach approximately 10% of his stake, also exercising stock options to pay taxes. Musk attributed some sales to the necessity of exercising expiring stock options and criticized California's "overtaxation" and "overregulation," revealing he would pay over $11 billion in taxes this year.

title: Elon Musk: I'm almost done with Tesla stock sales
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Inc., indicated on Wednesday that he is "almost done" with his Tesla stock sales, which have exceeded $15 billion since early November. He clarified that he had sold enough to reach approximately 10% of his shares, including option exercises, driven in part by expiring stock options and tax obligations. Musk also criticized California's "overtaxation" and "overregulation," stating he would pay over $11 billion in taxes this year.

title: What’s New With BMW for 2022?
summary: BMW introduces significant updates for its 2022 model year, focusing on new electric vehicles and minor refreshes across its SUV, sedan, coupe, and convertible lineups. Key additions include the new i4 electric performance sedan and the iX, BMW's first all-electric SUV, along with various styling tweaks, technology upgrades, and performance enhancements for existing models. The quirky i3 electric subcompact, however, has been discontinued.

title: Automotive News' top stories of 2021
summary: This article from Automotive News highlights its top stories of 2021, focusing on key developments in the automotive industry. It covers topics such as the impact of new EVs like the Ford Mustang Mach-E on Tesla's market share, the implications of new tariffs on vehicle prices, updates in dealership buy-sell activities, and a curious detail about Jeffrey Epstein's interest in Carlos Ghosn's arrest. These featured stories recap significant events and trends that shaped the automotive landscape throughout the year.

title: Honda Defective Transmission Class Action Lawsuit Moves Forward After Appeals Court Reverses Decision
summary: A federal appeals court has reversed a lower court's decision in a class action lawsuit against Honda regarding allegedly defective transmissions in certain Odyssey minivan models. The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the district court erred by excluding expert testimony, remanding the case for further proceedings. The lawsuit claims that transmissions in 2011-2016 Honda Odysseys caused severe shaking and shuddering, potentially leading to over $1.6 billion in classwide damages.

title: Commentary: Why Vietnam’s electric carmaker VinFast is launching in the US and bypassing China
summary: Vietnamese electric carmaker VinFast is strategically launching its EVs in the US market, bypassing China despite its size, to achieve global brand recognition and leverage high American technological standards. The company aims to compete with established EV players like Tesla and Rivian by focusing on experimental innovation and competitive pricing, particularly targeting the trend-setting California market. This move represents a gamble on branding for a start-up, hoping that not being tied to traditional automotive roots will be an asset.

title: Tesla Could Rise 30% Next Year on China Demand
summary: A Wedbush analyst predicts Tesla shares could rise by nearly 30% in 2022, driven by strong demand from China and new factory openings in the U.S. and Germany. The analyst highlights China as a crucial factor, expecting it to account for 40% of Tesla's deliveries next year. Component shortages are also expected to ease, allowing Tesla to meet its increasing demand.

title: Goodyear Launches ElectricDrive GT: Its First EV Replacement Tire
summary: Goodyear has introduced its new ElectricDrive GT tire, the company's first replacement tire in North America specifically designed for electric vehicles. This all-season tire is engineered to be quiet, long-lasting, and offer ultra-high performance, addressing the unique demands of EVs such as load, torque, noise, and rolling resistance. Initially available in one size for popular high-performance EV models, Goodyear plans to broaden its availability and size options in 2022.

title: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest ditched more Tesla to buy shares in virtual healthcare firm Teladoc
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest sold approximately $4 million worth of Tesla shares and acquired about $3 million in Teladoc shares on Tuesday. This move comes as Ark's funds have faced significant losses in December, with the flagship Ark Innovation ETF down over 20% for the year. Despite the downturn, Wood remains optimistic, defending her portfolio and predicting a quadruple return for Ark's funds in the next five years.

title: Can Snowmobiling Really Go Electric?
summary: Canadian startup Taiga Motors is leading the charge in electrifying the snowmobiling industry, a sector long known for significant pollution. With major manufacturers like BRP Inc. and Polaris committing substantial investments to develop electric recreational vehicles, the industry is poised for a significant shift towards more environmentally friendly options. Taiga's innovative approach aims to overcome traditional challenges in performance and design, making electric snowmobiles a viable and competitive choice for outdoor enthusiasts.

title: Tesla recalls more than 475,000 US cars on technical issues
summary: Tesla is recalling nearly 475,000 vehicles in the U.S. due to technical defects that could increase the risk of accidents. The recall includes all Model 3 vehicles made between 2017 and 2020 due to a rearview camera issue, and some Model S cars assembled from 2014 for a faulty front-trunk latch. Despite the large scope, Tesla is offering free repairs, and the company is unaware of any related crashes, injuries, or deaths.

title: Tesla recalls almost half a million electric cars over safety issues
summary: Tesla is recalling over 475,000 Model 3 and Model S electric cars in the U.S. due to rearview camera and front trunk issues that could increase the risk of crashing. The recall affects Model 3 vehicles from 2017-2020 for camera problems and Model S vehicles for front hood issues, with global recalls including nearly 200,000 vehicles in China. Tesla stated it is not aware of any crashes, injuries, or deaths related to these specific defects.
